summary: The article highlights the Invesco Dow Jones Industrial Average Dividend ETF (DJD) as a means for investors to gain exposure to dividend-paying equities, particularly in an environment of low Treasury yields. It notes DJD's outperformance compared to the S&P 500, its lower P/E ratio, and its focus on large-cap value equities with a history of consistent dividends. Other dividend-focused ETFs like FlexShares Quality Dividend Dynamic Index Fund (QDYN) and ProShares S&P 500 Aristocrats ETF (NOBL) are also mentioned as viable alternatives for income investors.

title: Working together in the fight against tuberculosis and malaria
summary: The Helmholtz Centre for Infection Research (HZI) and its branch, the Helmholtz Institute for Pharmaceutical Research Saarland (HIPS), are collaborating with Evotec to develop new drugs for tuberculosis and malaria. This three-year collaboration is funded by the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation with 2.3 million euros, aiming to address the urgent need for new medicines, especially given rising antibiotic resistance. The project will leverage expertise in natural product research and early drug development to find innovative solutions for these major infectious diseases.

title: Deal of the Year: Bristol-Myers Squibb buys Celgene
summary: Bristol-Myers Squibb's $74 billion acquisition of Celgene was named "Deal of the Year" for 2019, poised to significantly reshape the biopharma industry for years to come. While some smaller biotechs anticipate a loss of Celgene's aggressive deal-making presence, others, like venture capitalist Kevin Kinsella, see opportunity in assets that may be shed post-merger. The deal is a major gamble for Bristol-Myers, aiming to create an oncology powerhouse, despite challenges faced by both companies' key drugs.

title: Sanofi, Regeneron uncouple on long-standing drug partnership, splitting up Praluent, Kevzara
summary: Sanofi and Regeneron are restructuring their 12-year drug partnership, converting it into a royalty-based agreement for Praluent and Kevzara, with Regeneron gaining U.S. rights to Praluent and Sanofi securing global rights to Kevzara. This move follows the partnership's recent profitability driven by Dupixent sales, which remains a 50-50 split. Sanofi CEO Paul Hudson announced this as part of a broader strategy to streamline operations, potentially sell its Regeneron stock, and focus on Dupixent's growth and its R&D pipeline.

title: Can Sanofi and Regeneron's Dupixent steal half of a $21B eczema market? Not so fast: analyst
summary: Sanofi's CEO predicted Dupixent would achieve €10 billion in sales, but analysts caution that a crowded pipeline of competing drugs, including those from Dermira, Leo Pharma, and Pfizer, could challenge Dupixent's market dominance in the multi-billion dollar eczema treatment market. Concerns about Dupixent's side effect profile and time to onset, along with potential safety issues for other drug classes, suggest that market overcrowding and marketing challenges will intensify despite the overall growth of the atopic dermatitis market.

title: Glycogen Synthase Kinase-3β Inhibition with 9-ING-41 Attenuates the Progression of Pulmonary Fibrosis
summary: This study investigates the role of Glycogen Synthase Kinase-3β (GSK-3β) in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) and demonstrates that inhibition of GSK-3β with the novel compound 9-ING-41 attenuates the progression of pulmonary fibrosis in preclinical models. The research shows that GSK-3β activation is crucial for fibroblast-to-myofibroblast differentiation, a key process in fibrosis, and that 9-ING-41 can both block and reverse this differentiation. These findings suggest that 9-ING-41 is a promising therapeutic candidate for the treatment of IPF, providing a strong rationale for further clinical investigation.

title: Eli Lilly CEO says Elizabeth Warren’s claims they failed on cheaper insulin is ‘nonsense’
summary: Eli Lilly CEO David Ricks refutes Senator Elizabeth Warren's claims that the company failed to provide lower-priced insulin, calling them "nonsense." Ricks highlights the release of a half-priced version of their bestselling insulin, Insulin Lispro, attributing availability issues to wholesalers and pharmacies preferring high list-price products with higher rebates. The controversy follows a report co-released by Senator Warren suggesting Eli Lilly has not meaningfully increased the availability and affordability of cheaper insulin.

title: Read may say goodbye to Pfizer, but he'll join the board at spinoff Viatris
summary: Ian Read, Pfizer's executive chairman and former CEO, will join the board of Viatris, the new generics giant formed by the merger of Pfizer's Upjohn unit and Mylan. This move comes as Read transitions out of his role at Pfizer by the end of 2019. Viatris is expected to become the world's largest generics maker, generating between $19 million and $20 billion annually.

title: First generics to Bristol-Myers and Pfizer's Eliquis are here. But can they launch before 2026?
summary: The FDA has approved the first two generic versions of Bristol-Myers Squibb and Pfizer's blockbuster blood thinner Eliquis, made by Mylan and Micro Labs. Despite these approvals, the generics are unlikely to launch before 2026 due to ongoing patent disputes and settlements, as Bristol-Myers Squibb and Pfizer are strenuously defending the drug which generates billions in revenue. Eliquis remains a significant growth driver for both companies, outperforming competitors like Johnson & Johnson's Xarelto in the novel oral anticoagulants market.

title: China Approves New Varicella Vaccine For Children
summary: China's National Medical Products Administration (NMPA) has approved Sinovac Biotech's varicella vaccine for children aged 1 to 12, with a protection rate of 87.1 percent. This marks the first vaccine approved by the Chinese government under the new Vaccine Management Law. Sinovac plans to explore international markets for its new product given the global inclusion of varicella vaccines in national immunization programs.

title: Bristol-Myers, Gilead, and Biogen hike US drug prices as the new year begins
summary: Drugmakers including Bristol-Myers Squibb, Gilead Sciences, and Biogen increased U.S. list prices on more than 50 drugs, contributing to a total of over 250 drug price hikes on New Year's Day. Most increases were below 10%, with a median of around 5%. These price adjustments occur amid ongoing political pressure regarding soaring prescription drug costs, particularly as the 2020 presidential election approaches.

title: RNA- Based Therapeutic Market To Record An Exponential CAGR
summary: The global RNA-based therapeutic market was valued at US$ 1,756.5 Mn in 2019 and is projected to grow at an exponential CAGR of 24.6% during the period of 2020-2028. This growth is driven by the efficiency of RNA-based therapy in targeting disease-causing genes and an increasing number of strategic collaborations among key market players. The market is segmented by drug class, therapeutic area, and region, with prominent players including Akcea Therapeutics Inc, Biogen Inc., and Alnylam Pharmaceuticals.

title: VectivBio Launches with $35M Financing to Bring Best-in-Disease Medicines to Patients with Serious Rare Diseases
summary: VectivBio, a clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on serious rare diseases, announced its formation with $35 million in financing from several investors. The company is a spinout of Therachon Holding AG and is led by a team with expertise in rare diseases. Their lead program, apraglutide, is a next-generation GLP-2 analog aiming to treat short bowel syndrome (SBS) with a once-weekly dosing regimen.

title: Where Is The Headquarters Of Pfizer?
summary: This article details the headquarters of Pfizer, located at 235 East 42nd Street in Manhattan, New York City. It provides a brief history of the pharmaceutical giant, highlighting its founding in 1849 and its growth to become a leading drug company known for products like Lipitor, Viagra, and Celebrex. The article further describes the significance of 42nd Street and Manhattan as key locations in New York City.

title: Biogen to Acquire Novel Clinical Stage Asset with Application in Alzheimer’s Disease and Parkinson’s Disease from Pfizer Inc.
summary: Biogen announced an agreement to acquire PF-05251749, a novel clinical stage asset from Pfizer Inc., for an upfront payment of $75 million plus potential milestones of up to $635 million and tiered royalties. This asset, a CNS-penetrant regulator of circadian rhythm, will be developed for the treatment of Sundowning in Alzheimer’s disease and Irregular Sleep Wake Rhythm Disorder in Parkinson’s disease. Biogen plans to initiate a Phase 1b study in Q4 2020.

title: ‘Blood on their hands’: Oklahoma sues opioid distributors
summary: Oklahoma Attorney General Mike Hunter has sued three major opioid distributors: McKesson Corporation, Cardinal Health, and AmerisourceBergen, alleging they ignored red flags and contributed to the opioid crisis in the state. Hunter seeks damages for negligence and misconduct, separate from previous "public nuisance" claims against manufacturers. This lawsuit follows other settlements Oklahoma has reached with opioid manufacturers like Purdue Pharma, Teva Pharmaceuticals, and Endo Pharmaceuticals.

title: Insilico enters into research collaboration with Pfizer Inc. to explore novel data and artificial intelligence system for potential therapeutic targets
summary: Insilico Medicine has announced a research collaboration with Pfizer Inc. to utilize Insilico's machine learning technology and proprietary Pandomics Discovery Platform. The goal of this partnership is to identify real-world evidence for potential therapeutic targets across various diseases. This collaboration highlights Pfizer's interest in exploring new technologies like AI for target and biomarker identification to accelerate drug discovery.

title: Charting a bullish 2020 start: S&P 500 extends break to record territory
summary: This article discusses the bullish start to 2020 for the S&P 500, which has extended its break into record territory. It highlights that major U.S. benchmarks are continuing to rise as early-January volatility subsides. The focus areas include emerging markets taking flight, homebuilders reaching two-year highs, and Netflix sustaining its late-2019 resurgence, mentioning symbols such as EEM, XHB, NFLX, SWKS, and PFE.

title: Global Rosacea Treatment Market 2020:Emerging Trends
summary: The global rosacea treatment market is projected to rise with a steady CAGR of 3.8% from 2019-2026, driven by high prevalence, growing awareness, and increased R&D for novel therapies. Key market players like Nestlé, ALLERGAN, and Merck & Co. are employing various strategies including new product launches and acquisitions to expand their market footprint. Recent developments include FDA approvals for new treatments, indicating a dynamic and competitive market landscape.

title: Big Pharma Strategies and Growth Initiatives: What’s In Store for 2020
summary: This article details the strategic initiatives and growth outlooks for major pharmaceutical companies in 2020, as discussed at the J.P. Morgan Annual Healthcare Conference. It highlights key acquisitions, product launches, financial targets, and therapeutic focus areas for Bristol-Myers Squibb, Pfizer, Novartis, GlaxoSmithKline, and Amgen. The report covers significant deals like BMS's acquisition of Celgene, Pfizer's reorganization, GSK's oncology expansion, and Amgen's strategic alliance in China.

title: Nektar quickly drops opioid drug after FDA panel rejection
summary: Nektar Therapeutics is withdrawing its application for FDA approval of its experimental opioid painkiller, oxycodegol, after an advisory panel unanimously voted against recommending its approval due to concerns about abuse potential and insufficient data. The company had invested at least $250 million in the drug's development and expects cost savings of $75 million to $125 million this year due to the decision. This marks a significant setback for Nektar, whose main focus is now on its cancer work despite previous setbacks in that area as well.

title: We Did It! Pharma Giant Bristol-Myers Squibb Bans Forced Swim Test
summary: Bristol-Myers Squibb has banned the cruel forced swim test after more than a year of campaigning by PETA and its international affiliates. This decision makes Bristol-Myers Squibb one of several major pharmaceutical companies to stop using the test, which involves forcing small animals to swim to avoid drowning and is considered by PETA to be both cruel and scientifically unsound. PETA is now urging Eli Lilly to follow suit and end its use of the forced swim test.

title: Novo's Ozempic scores major win with heart-helping FDA approval. Is Rybelsus next?
summary: Novo Nordisk's Ozempic has received FDA approval to reduce cardiovascular events in patients with Type 2 diabetes and established cardiovascular disease, based on the Sustain 6 study. This approval positions Ozempic similarly to SGLT2 drugs like Jardiance and Farxiga, and bodes well for Novo's oral GLP-1 Rybelsus, which is also being studied for cardiovascular prevention. The expanded indication is expected to boost Ozempic's sales, which already reached $1 billion in the first nine months of 2019.

title: Pfizer Inc. designates UofL first-of-its-kind Center of Excellence for epidemiological research
summary: Pfizer Inc. has designated the University of Louisville's Division of Infectious Diseases as its first Center of Excellence for epidemiological research, focusing on vaccine-preventable diseases in adults. This three-year collaboration, directed by Dr. Julio Ramirez, will involve studies in hospitals, long-term care facilities, and the community to gather data for vaccine recommendations worldwide. Pfizer chose UofL due to its strong capabilities in population-based surveillance and clinical research, and the similar demographics of Jefferson County, Kentucky, to the broader United States.

title: New CEO Brett Monia Takes The Lead As Ionis Prioritizes Non-Partnered Programs
summary: Brett Monia has taken over as CEO of Ionis Pharmaceuticals, succeeding Stanley Crooke. Monia, who was a founding scientist at the company, will focus on advancing Ionis' non-partnered programs. This strategic shift aims to maximize value from the company's internal pipeline.

title: Bristol-Myers Squibb: Strong Quality And Attractive Valuation
summary: Bristol-Myers Squibb is presented as a high-quality pharmaceutical company with a strong track record of growth and profitability. The recent acquisition of Celgene is viewed as a financially and strategically sound move that is expected to be accretive to earnings. The stock is considered reasonably valued, offering an attractive risk-reward trade-off for investors.

title: Pfizer Revenues Slide to End 2019
summary: Pfizer Inc. reported a 1% year-over-year decrease in full-year revenues for 2019, totaling $51.8 billion, with Q4 revenues down 8% to $12.7 billion, largely due to a 32% decline in its Upjohn segment. The company projects 2020 revenues between $48.5 billion and $50.5 billion and adjusted EPS between $2.82 and $2.92, while also highlighting the planned Upjohn-Mylan transaction to create Viatris. Pfizer's stock reacted negatively to the news, trading down more than 3% in early morning trading.

title: FDA approves Aimmune drug as first treatment for peanut allergy
summary: The FDA has approved Aimmune Therapeutics' Palforzia as the first treatment for peanut allergy for children and teens aged 4 to 17. The drug, an oral immunotherapy, aims to desensitize patients to peanuts, though it comes with a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy due to potential allergic reactions. Palforzia's approval gives Aimmune a lead over competitor DBV Technologies, despite concerns over its price and the need for medical supervision during initial dosing.

title: The World Congress 8th Annual Patient Congress
summary: The 8th Annual World Congress Patient Congress, scheduled for April 6-7, 2020, in Philadelphia, focuses on improving patient access and health outcomes. The event features multiple tracks, including Patient Adherence and Engagement, Patient Advocacy, and a Copay Summit, with speakers from prominent healthcare organizations. Drug Channels readers can receive a discount by registering with a special promo code by March 31, 2020.

title: Bristol-Myers launches biotech targeting fibrosis, inflammation
summary: Bristol-Myers Squibb and BioMotiv have launched Anteros Pharmaceuticals, a new company focused on developing therapies for inflammation and fibrosis, utilizing Yale University intellectual property and Bristol-Myers' data. Anteros will initially target liver and lung fibrosis, including idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF). Bristol-Myers Squibb has the right to acquire Anteros if it nominates a pre-clinical candidate, with financial terms already set but undisclosed.

title: Exelixis prostate cancer data could help stave off competitive threats
summary: Exelixis announced positive interim Phase 1 data for its cancer drug Cabometyx, combined with Roche’s Tecentriq, showing tumor shrinkage in nearly one-third of advanced prostate cancer patients. This news is crucial for Exelixis as Cabometyx faces increasing competition in its primary kidney cancer indication. The company plans to seek FDA approval for prostate cancer in early 2021 based on these and future expansion study results.

title: Theranostics Market to Surpass 20 Billion USD by 2027| Leading Players F Hoffman La Roche, Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc., GE Healthcare, Agilent Technologies, Qiagen NV
summary: The Theranostics market is projected to exceed $20 billion USD by 2027, driven by its role in optimizing medical diagnosis and treatment. This growing field combines advanced diagnostics with effective pharmaceuticals, offering significant opportunities in healthcare and regulatory industries. Key players in this market include F Hoffman La Roche, Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc., and GE Healthcare.

title: GSK Offloads Physiogel In North America, Asia To Korea’s LG
summary: GSK has offloaded its Physiogel brand in North America and Asia to LG. The article mentions other related content regarding GSK's divestments and acquisitions, including those with Pfizer and Stada. This signals GSK's ongoing strategic adjustments in its consumer health portfolio.

title: BioCryst Appoints Alan G. Levin to Board of Directors
summary: BioCryst Pharmaceuticals, Inc. announced the appointment of Alan G. Levin, former Pfizer CFO, to its board of directors. Mr. Levin brings extensive experience in pharmaceutical finance, including a 20-year career at Pfizer and significant growth at Endo Pharmaceuticals. His appointment is expected to support BioCryst's transition into a commercial company with a strong pipeline of medicines.

title: Diabetes Treatment Devices Market Expands at 5.4% CAGR till 2026
summary: The global diabetes treatment devices market is projected to reach USD 16,488.6 Million by 2026, growing at a CAGR of 5.4% from USD 10,826.6 Million in 2018. This growth is driven by the rising prevalence of diabetes, increased R&D investments, and technological advancements in insulin delivery devices. Companies like Medtronic, F. Hoffmann-La Roche Ltd., Tandem Diabetes Care, Inc., and Novo Nordisk are leading the market, with Asia Pacific expected to show strong growth due to its increasing diabetic population.

title: Servier bags expanded rights to Cellectis' CD19 CAR-Ts
summary: Servier has expanded its rights to Cellectis’ CD19 CAR-T therapies, including UCART19, ALLO-501, and ALLO-501A, through a revised deal worth €25 million ($27.6 million) upfront and up to €370 million in milestones. This agreement builds on their 2014 partnership and also returns exclusive rights to five other CAR-T targets to Cellectis. Cellectis also announced plans to amend a phase 1 trial for UCART22.

title: Global biopharma supply chain holding together for now: Vertex says supply chain, its business holding steady
summary: As the COVID-19 pandemic spreads, biopharma companies are closely monitoring their supply chains. Vertex Pharmaceuticals, Mylan, AstraZeneca, and WuXi AppTec have reported their supply chains are holding steady despite the global health crisis, with some minor disruptions and adjustments to clinical trials. India has temporarily curbed the export of 26 APIs, while the FDA noted one drug shortage linked to the outbreak.

title: Opinion: As Bernie Sanders is essentially finished, health-care stocks are screaming buys
summary: This opinion piece argues that healthcare stocks have become "screaming buys" due to Bernie Sanders's diminishing chances of winning the presidency, which removes the threat of "Medicare for All." Despite concerns about the U.S. healthcare system's preparedness for COVID-19 and a recent drop in healthcare stock prices, investors are advised to consider these stocks given the changed political landscape. The article suggests that Joe Biden's looming victory eliminates a major political risk for the sector.

title: Pfizer Joins Forces With BioNTech For COVID-19 Vaccine Co-Development
summary: Pfizer Inc. and BioNTech SE have signed a letter of intent to co-develop and distribute a COVID-19 vaccine, building on their previous influenza vaccine collaboration. The partnership aims to accelerate the development of BioNTech’s BNT162 mRNA vaccine candidate, expected to enter clinical testing soon. This global effort responds to Pfizer's call for biopharmaceutical collaboration to combat the escalating pandemic.

title: Pfizer and BioNTech to Co-Develop Potential COVID-19 Vaccine
summary: Pfizer and BioNTech have announced a letter of intent to co-develop and distribute BioNTech’s mRNA-based vaccine candidate, BNT162, to prevent COVID-19 infection. This collaboration aims to accelerate the global development of the vaccine, leveraging both companies' expertise and resources. The initiative builds on their existing 2018 agreement to develop mRNA-based influenza vaccines.

title: How Pfizer Is Using Wearables To Understand The Patient Experience
summary: Pfizer's Early Clinical Development (ECD) team is leveraging wearable technology to gather real-world data on how patients experience chronic diseases like atopic dermatitis. Through their Pfizer Innovation Research (PfIRe) Lab, they are developing methods to quantify symptoms such as scratching during sleep, intending to design clinical trials with more relevant and patient-centric endpoints. This approach aims to bridge the gap between lab measurements and daily life, leading to smarter drug development.

title: Section 101 Update: Pharmaceutical and Life Sciences March 2020
summary: This article discusses two recent U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit opinions concerning Section 101 patent eligibility in pharmaceutical and life sciences cases. In both cases, district court rulings of invalidity for lack of patentable subject matter were reversed. The author details the specifics of _Boehringer Ingelheim Pharmaceuticals Inc. et al. v. Mylan Pharmaceuticals Inc. et al._ and _Illumina Inc. et al. v. Ariosa Diagnostics Inc. et al._, including a strong dissent in the latter case regarding the "method of preparation" category.

title: Biohaven’s Nurtec May Be First Migraine Drug For Acute Treatment And Prevention
summary: Biohaven's Nurtec ODT may become the first oral anti-CGRP drug approved for both acute migraine treatment and prevention. This development follows its approval in the US for acute migraine in February 2020. The article discusses its potential impact in the migraine treatment market.

title: Fate inks $100M J&J pact for ‘off-the-shelf’ cancer cell therapies
summary: Johnson & Johnson and Fate Therapeutics have announced a $100 million deal to co-develop allogeneic, or "off-the-shelf," cancer cell therapies. J&J will also purchase $50 million in Fate shares at a premium. This partnership aims to advance therapies for blood cancers and solid tumors, which could be more accessible and cost-effective than current autologous CAR-T treatments, despite the early stage of allogeneic research and potential COVID-19 related delays.

title: ICON Signs New Service Agreement with Pfizer
summary: ICON plc has signed a new three-year service agreement with Pfizer, with the option for a two-year extension. This agreement expands upon their existing partnership where ICON provides global services for Pfizer's clinical trials. The partnership aims to advance Pfizer's pipeline and drive innovation in drug development.

title: Pfizer’s digital chief: Technology can speed the race to a COVID-19 vaccine
summary: Lidia Fonseca, Pfizer's Chief Digital and Technology Officer, is leveraging technology to support the company's race for a COVID-19 vaccine, enabling remote work for thousands of employees and facilitating data sharing and collaboration with other biopharmaceutical companies. Her team built a "scientific cloud" on Amazon Web Services to centralize Pfizer's previously siloed data, dramatically increasing its value for research. Fonseca emphasizes technology's role in empowering scientists with information to make informed decisions and accelerate the development of life-changing breakthroughs.

title: Continuous Pharmaceutical Manufacturing
summary: The pharmaceutical industry is increasingly adopting continuous manufacturing (CM) due to its undeniable advantages over batch manufacturing, including reduced CAPEX, automation, improved quality control, and shorter lead times. Despite these benefits, challenges like existing infrastructure and regulatory uncertainties have led to slow adoption. However, continuous manufacturing offers a robust solution for fragile pharmaceutical supply chains, especially relevant during global health crises.

title: BioNTech and Pfizer announce regulatory approval from
summary: BioNTech and Pfizer have received regulatory approval from the German authority Paul-Ehrlich-Institut to begin the first clinical trial of their COVID-19 vaccine candidates, BNT162. This trial, a Phase 1/2 study, is the first COVID-19 vaccine clinical trial in Germany and is part of a global development program that will soon include trials in the United States. Four different mRNA vaccine candidates will be evaluated for safety and immunogenicity, targeting healthy subjects and later those at higher risk for severe COVID-19 infection.

title: Efficacy of risankizumab in patients with moderate‐to‐severe plaque psoriasis by baseline demographics, disease characteristics and prior biologic therapy: an integrated analysis of the phase III UltIMMa‐1 and UltIMMa‐2 studies
summary: This integrated analysis from the phase III UltIMMa-1 and UltIMMa-2 studies evaluates the efficacy of risankizumab compared to ustekinumab in patients with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis, considering baseline demographics, disease characteristics, and prior biologic therapy. The study found that risankizumab demonstrated superior and consistent efficacy over ustekinumab across all patient subgroups, including those with higher BMI, body weight, or prior biologic exposure/failure, supporting its use without dose adjustment for a wide range of patients.

title: Novartis announces data showing Jakavi® (ruxolitinib) more effective than best available therapy in acute graft-versus-host disease
summary: Novartis announced that data from its Phase III REACH2 study showed Jakavi® (ruxolitinib) was more effective than best available therapy for patients with steroid-refractory acute graft-versus-host disease (GvHD). The study, published in The New England Journal of Medicine, demonstrated a 62% overall response rate with Jakavi at Day 28 compared to 39% for best available therapy, with a positive safety profile consistent with the drug’s known effects. This advancement offers a new treatment option for a serious complication of stem cell transplants with high mortality rates.

title: $350,000 on Hand Sanitizer: How Werner is Responding to the COVID-19 Pandemic
summary: Werner Enterprises has spent over $350,000 on hand sanitizer and implemented comprehensive measures to protect its drivers and employees during the COVID-19 pandemic. CEO Derek Leathers emphasizes compassion and data-driven decisions, drawing on the company's existing pandemic plan and emergency response experience. Werner has adapted to significant disruptions in supply chains, with executives taking salary reductions while supporting drivers with pay if impacted by the virus.

title: Merck and Pfizer Stocks Head Up a Busy Earnings Week
summary: Pharmaceutical giants Merck (MRK) and Pfizer (PFE) are set to report Q1 earnings, with both stocks gaining relative strength due to declines in other Dow components. The companies are also involved in coronavirus vaccine research, which has garnered market attention. Analysts anticipate Merck to post EPS of $1.34 on $11.46 billion revenue and Pfizer to post EPS of $0.71 on $11.35 billion revenue.

title: 3M’s Mask-on Magic; Pfizer Pfalls; Caterpillar Crawls
summary: This article discusses the market's "hope-inspired" rally despite overwhelming economic indicators pointing to a downturn, highlighting the Federal Reserve's influence. It examines first-quarter earnings for 3M (NYSE: MMM), Pfizer (NYSE: PFE), and Caterpillar (NYSE: CAT), noting contrasting investor reactions to their reports. The article also touches on vaccine development and offers an investing strategy called "Profit Stacking."

title: As Trikafta launched, Vertex's Leiden scored $18.8M in final full year as CEO
summary: Jeffrey Leiden, former CEO of Vertex Pharmaceuticals, received an $18.79 million pay package in his final full year, as the company launched its triple-combo cystic fibrosis drug Trikafta. Vertex achieved significant milestones including a 37% increase in CF sales to $4.16 billion and securing reimbursement deals for its CF medications. Leiden's compensation placed him among the highest-paid pharma executives, while Reshma Kewalramani took over as CEO in April 2020.

title: Pfizer looks to right sterile injectable woes with modernized manufacturing
summary: Pfizer is making significant progress in resolving its long-standing sterile injectable manufacturing issues, largely due to remediation efforts and modernized manufacturing investments. CEO Albert Bourla stated that the company can now stock 90% of its sterile injectables portfolio, with first-quarter growth of 15% year-over-year. This turnaround follows years of FDA scrutiny and substantial investments aimed at improving facilities like the McPherson plant, which was acquired through the Hospira buyout.

title: Vertex, even amid pandemic, raises sales projections thanks to gangbusters start for Trikafta
summary: Vertex Pharmaceuticals raised its 2020 sales projections after its new cystic fibrosis drug, Trikafta, achieved an $895 million launch in its first full quarter, despite the COVID-19 pandemic. The company's overall revenues grew 77% from the previous year, leading to an increased revenue guidance to between $5.3 billion and $5.6 billion. Vertex acknowledged potential future uncertainties due to the pandemic, such as shifts in payer mix and impact on new patient initiations, but plans to maintain a strong negotiation stance for Trikafta's pricing internationally.

title: Valneva and Pfizer collaborate for Lyme disease vaccine
summary: Valneva and Pfizer have announced a collaboration to develop and commercialize Valneva’s Lyme disease vaccine candidate VLA15, which is currently in Phase 2 clinical studies and is the only active Lyme disease vaccine program in clinical development. Valneva is eligible to receive up to $308 million in cash payments, while Pfizer will lead late-stage development and commercialization, paying Valneva tiered royalties starting at 19 percent.

title: 3M completes $650M drug delivery unit sale, but business to remain in Twin Cities
summary: 3M has completed the $650 million sale of its drug delivery unit to Altaris Capital Partners. The business, now named Kindeva Drug Delivery, will retain its 900 employees and operations in the Twin Cities, initially on 3M's Maplewood campus before relocating. 3M will maintain a 17% stake in the new company and net about 40 cents per share from the divestiture.

title: Pfizer begins human testing for experimental coronavirus vaccine in the US
summary: Pfizer has started human trials in the U.S. for an experimental coronavirus vaccine, BNT162, developed in collaboration with German drugmaker BioNTech. This follows earlier trials in Germany, with Pfizer aiming to quickly advance testing and production of a safe and effective vaccine. The company hopes to produce millions of doses by the end of 2020.

title: WSJ News Exclusive | ICE Partners With Amazon, 3M to Identify Counterfeit Coronavirus Gear
summary: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) is partnering with companies including 3M Co., Amazon.com Inc., and Pfizer Inc. to combat the influx of counterfeit coronavirus-related medical gear. ICE's intellectual-property unit announced this collaboration to identify suspicious shipments and remove fraudulent online listings. The companies have agreed to share information and best practices with the agency to curtail the trade of counterfeit masks, tests, and other equipment.

title: The New York Times: NYU Langone Among First Centers to Dose Patients in Pfizer-Led U.S. COVID-19 Vaccine Trials
summary: NYU Langone, specifically NYU Grossman School of Medicine, is among the first centers in the U.S. to begin dosing patients in the Pfizer-led COVID-19 vaccine trials. The vaccine uses an RNA-based technique to instruct cells to produce viral proteins, aiming to train the immune system to fight the virus without causing illness. Infectious diseases expert Dr. Mark J. Mulligan emphasizes the critical need for vaccines to be very safe as they are administered to healthy individuals.

title: Sleep Aids Market to Register CAGR 5% Growth in Value Share During 2019 to 2029
summary: The global sleep aids market, which exceeded US$ 23 billion in 2018, is projected to grow at a promising CAGR of 5% between 2019 and 2029. This growth is driven by increasing prevalence of sleep disorders, changing lifestyles, and advancements in sleep aid products and devices. Key players are focusing on product development and geographical expansion to capitalize on the rising demand for effective sleep management solutions.

title: |Express Scripts Offers Prescription Cost Relief for Newly Uninsured Americans
summary: |Express Scripts announced a new program called Parachute Rx to help newly uninsured Americans afford prescription medications during the COVID-19 pandemic. The program caps costs at $25 for generics and $75 for select brand-name medicines for a 30-day supply, thanks to partnerships with pharmaceutical manufacturers and pharmacies. This initiative aims to assist those whose lives have been impacted by job loss and ensure continued access to vital treatments.

title: Human Growth Hormone Advancement & Growth Analysis with
summary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of the Human Growth Hormone market, including a forecast to 2027. It identifies key players such as Novo Nordisk, Merck & Co., and Pfizer, and discusses market drivers like increased awareness, prevalence of chronic diseases, and rising healthcare expenditure. The report also highlights regional market dynamics, with North America leading and Asia-Pacific projected for the fastest growth.

title: GenFit delivers latest NASH drug failure
summary: GenFit's main drug, elafibranor, failed a late-stage clinical study for NASH, with its efficacy not significantly better than placebo. This result caused the company's share price to drop by half and further highlights the challenges in developing treatments for NASH. Intercept Pharmaceuticals now holds a stronger leading position in the NASH drug development space with its drug obeticholic acid.

title: What's Driving the Alagille Syndrome Market Trends by 2026?
summary: This report analyzes the global Alagille Syndrome market, forecasting substantial growth between 2019 and 2026 due to refined healthcare infrastructure and special regulatory designations. Key market players like Albireo Pharma and Mirum Pharmaceuticals are highlighted, alongside market segmentation by treatment, drugs, diagnosis, end-users, and geography. The article details recent market developments, drivers, restraints, and opportunities within the Alagille Syndrome market.

title: Bristol Myers Squibb finally breaks into first-line lung cancer with Opdivo-Yervoy nod
summary: Bristol Myers Squibb's Opdivo, in combination with Yervoy, has received FDA approval for the first-line treatment of non-small cell lung cancer in patients whose tumors are PD-L1 positive. This approval offers a chemotherapy-free option but faces stiff competition from Merck's Keytruda-chemo combo, which has demonstrated superior mortality risk reduction. Despite this, BMS emphasizes the durability of response with its Opdivo-Yervoy pairing, highlighting long-term survival rates.

title: Coronavirus testing not needed for every American: LabCorp CEO
summary: LabCorp CEO Adam Schechter stated that not every American needs to be tested for coronavirus, only those who are ill or have been exposed. He noted that LabCorp has conducted millions of PCR and serology tests and aims to scale up to 150,000 tests daily by mid-June. Schechter also expressed skepticism about a vaccine being developed by the end of 2020, predicting it would take longer.

title: BlackRock votes to split CEO, chairman roles at Exxon Mobil
summary: Top fund manager BlackRock Inc. announced it voted in favor of splitting the CEO and chairman roles at Exxon Mobil Corp. and opposed the re-election of two directors due to concerns over Exxon's approach to climate risks. BlackRock, a significant shareholder, highlighted the need for independent leadership and greater urgency in addressing climate-related financial disclosures. This move came despite Exxon shareholders rejecting all four shareholder resolutions.

title: Onvansertib Receives FDA Fast Track Designation in KRAS+ mCRC
summary: The FDA granted Fast Track Designation to onvansertib for second-line treatment of KRAS-mutant metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) in combination with FOLFIRI and bevacizumab. This designation will expedite the development and review process for onvansertib, which is currently being evaluated in a phase 1b/2 clinical trial. Onvansertib is a first-in-class PLK1 enzyme inhibitor, showing promise due to its favorable safety profile and tolerability.

title: Are You Ready FDA's Transition From Computer System Validation To Computer Software Assurance
summary: The FDA is preparing to release new guidance for Computer Software Assurance (CSA), moving away from the more documentation-heavy Computer System Validation (CSV). This shift, initially for the medical device industry but applicable broadly, emphasizes critical thinking, risk management, patient safety, data integrity, and quality assurance. Life sciences companies must proactively develop a strategy to transition their current CSV methodologies to CSA to align with these new guidelines.

title: Yost Takes Action Against Generic Drug Manufacturers Who Conspired to Inflate, Manipulate Prices
summary: Ohio Attorney General Dave Yost has joined a coalition of 51 states and territories in filing a lawsuit against generic drug manufacturers for allegedly conspiring to artificially inflate and manipulate prices, reduce competition, and unreasonably restrain trade for generic topical drugs. The lawsuit, filed in the U.S. District Court for the District of Connecticut, targets 26 corporate defendants and 10 individual defendants, seeking damages, civil penalties, and actions to restore competition. The multistate investigation revealed direct evidence of agreements to minimize competition and raise prices on dozens of topical products, impacting federal, state, and commercial payers, as well as millions of U.S. residents.

title: Lassen Therapeutics Raises $31 Million to Pursue IL-11 Antibody for Cancer and Fibrosis
summary: Lassen Therapeutics launched with a $31 million Series A financing round to develop an IL-11 receptor alpha (IL-11R) antibody, LASN01, for fibrosis, rare diseases, and cancer. The company's lead product aims to inhibit IL-11 activity, which is believed to be effective in treating fibrotic diseases and altering the tumor microenvironment. Lassen Therapeutics plans to submit an IND application in 2021 and begin clinical trials the same year, with funding expected to last until the end of Phase I.

title: Pfizer's Lankler Confirmed for Deal Economy Conference
summary: Pfizer's general counsel, Doug Lankler, a 20-year veteran of the company, is scheduled to speak at The Deal Economy Conference in New York on Nov. 20. This comes after Pfizer's recent M&A activities, including the acquisition of Array BioPharma and Therachon, and the deal to combine its Upjohn unit with Mylan. Lankler has overseen significant deals during his tenure as GC, reflecting Pfizer's ongoing M&A strategy.

title: Saunders finds life after Allergan on board at newly IPO'ed BridgeBio
summary: Brent Saunders, former CEO of Allergan, has joined the board of directors at BridgeBio Pharma, a biotech company that recently completed a large IPO. Saunders' experience leading pharmaceutical companies and his reputation as a dealmaker are expected to help BridgeBio as it moves toward commercializing its first drugs and potentially pursuing further M&A. This move follows a trend of former large biopharma CEOs transitioning to roles on the boards of smaller companies.

title: Halozyme Announces Roche Receives FDA Approval For Phesgo™ (Fixed-Dose Combination Of Perjeta® And Herceptin® For Subcutaneous Injection) Utilizing Halozyme's ENHANZE® Technology For The Treatment Of Patients With HER2-Positive Breast C
summary: Halozyme announced that the FDA has approved Roche's Phesgo™, a fixed-dose combination of Perjeta and Herceptin utilizing Halozyme's ENHANZE technology, for subcutaneous injection in patients with HER2-positive breast cancer. This approval marks the first time a product combining two monoclonal antibodies for single subcutaneous injection using ENHANZE technology has been approved, significantly reducing administration time from hours to minutes. Clinical data showed high patient preference for Phesgo™ due to less clinic time and more comfortable treatment, with a safety profile comparable to existing IV administrations.

title: Alnylam's RNAi therapy Givlaari shows lasting effect one year into treatment, new data show
summary: New one-year data from an open-label extension of the phase 3 Envision study show Alnylam's RNAi therapy Givlaari maintains its efficacy in reducing acute hepatic porphyria attacks and presents a safety profile comparable to earlier trials. This longer-term data addresses prior concerns about the drug's safety for prolonged use, reinforcing its potential as a significant treatment for the ultra-rare liver disease. Alnylam is also transitioning patients to a higher dose of Givlaari due to evidence of increased efficacy and is looking to expand its portfolio with several late-stage candidates.

title: How secret deals could keep a COVID-19 drug out of reach for millions
summary: Pharmaceutical giant Gilead Sciences is under scrutiny for confidential licensing deals related to its experimental COVID-19 drug, remdesivir. Activists argue these agreements limit global access, particularly in countries with severe outbreaks, by preventing the distribution of cheaper generic versions and allowing Gilead to control pricing. Despite receiving federal funds for development, Gilead has priced remdesivir at a high cost, drawing criticism against profiting from the pandemic.

title: It Paid Doctors Kickbacks. Now, Novartis Will Pay a $678 Million Settlement. (Published 2020)
summary: Novartis will pay $678 million to settle a fraud lawsuit after admitting to a decade-long kickback scheme involving lavish meals, fishing junkets, golf outings, and speaker fees for doctors. The scheme aimed to influence doctors to prescribe Novartis's cardiovascular and diabetes drugs, leading to fraudulent prescription claims paid by Medicare, Medicaid, and the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs. Prosecutors highlighted that these actions interfered with doctors' duties and increased drug costs, though there were no claims that the prescribed drugs were unnecessary for patients.

title: Ultragenyx wins early approval for rare disease drug
summary: Ultragenyx Pharmaceutical has received early FDA approval for Dojolvi, a drug to treat long-chain fatty acid oxidation disorders, a rare and life-threatening genetic condition. This marks the first approved treatment for the disorder in the U.S., affecting thousands of children and adults. The drug is priced at $4,875 per vial, with an estimated average net price of $138,000 per patient annually, and analysts project sales of $270 million by 2025.

title: ViiV Healthcare announces US FDA approval for Rukobia (fostemsavir), a first-in-class treatment for HIV in adults with few treatment options available
summary: ViiV Healthcare announced that the US FDA has approved Rukobia (fostemsavir) for the treatment of HIV-1 infection in heavily treatment-experienced adults with multidrug-resistant HIV-1. This first-in-class attachment inhibitor offers a new mechanism of action for patients who have limited to no treatment options available. The approval is supported by data from the phase III BRIGHTE study, which demonstrated that Rukobia in combination with optimized background therapy achieved and maintained viral suppression and improved CD4+ T-cell counts in the target population.

title: 2020 Smallpox Treatment Market Research : International Size, Growth, Trends, Outlook and Future Scope Analysis by 2025 - Emergent BioSolutions, Pfizer, SIGA Technologies
summary: The global Smallpox Treatment Market is projected to experience significant growth, driven by increasing stockpiling of therapeutics and rising drug approvals. The market, segmented by product type (drugs, vaccines) and end-use industry (hospital, clinic), is expected to reach high values by 2024. Key players include Bavarian Nordic AS, Emergent BioSolutions Inc., Pfizer Inc., and SIGA Technologies Inc., with strategic initiatives like mergers and new product launches influencing market trends.

title: BD Launches Portable, Rapid Point-of-Care Antigen Test to Detect SARS-CoV-2 in 15 minutes, Dramatically Expanding Access to COVID-19 Testing
summary: BD (Becton, Dickinson and Company) announced that the U.S. FDA granted Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) for its rapid, point-of-care, SARS-CoV-2 diagnostic test, which delivers results in 15 minutes using the BD Veritor™ Plus System. This new assay is critical for expanding access to COVID-19 diagnostics in frontline healthcare settings, leveraging over 25,000 existing Veritor™ instruments. BD expects to ramp up manufacturing to 2 million tests per week by the end of September, significantly increasing testing capacity.

title: GE’s Healthcare Unit Is Developing Covid-19 Treatments. It Could Be Undervalued.
summary: General Electric's healthcare unit is collaborating with Oxford University on developing Covid-19 treatments. This venture highlights a potentially undervalued aspect of GE, which is often primarily associated with commercial aerospace. The article suggests that investors may be overlooking the significant contributions and potential of GE's healthcare division.

title: Johnson & Johnson and Partners Mark Milestone in Imbokodo HIV Vaccine Trial
summary: Johnson & Johnson and its partners have reached a significant milestone in the Imbokodo HIV vaccine trial, with all 2,600 participants fully immunized. This Phase 2b study is evaluating the safety and efficacy of an investigational mosaic-based HIV vaccine regimen across southern Africa. The company's experience in developing this HIV vaccine, particularly its AdVac® viral vector technology, has also been instrumental in its efforts to create a potential SARS-CoV-2 vaccine.

title: Annexon Seeks to Match $100 Million Fund Raise in IPO
summary: Annexon, a South San Francisco-based biotech, is looking to raise an additional $100 million through an IPO after a successful private funding round. The company focuses on developing drugs for autoimmune and neurodegenerative disorders like Guillain-Barré syndrome and Huntington's disease, with lead investors including Bain Capital Life Sciences Investors. Annexon's research is based on combating classical complement-mediated diseases, specifically targeting the C1q protein, and expects initial Phase 2 trial data for several indications next year.

title: Viatris Reveals Branding to Reflect New Company’s Transformative Strategy
summary: Mylan N.V. and Upjohn, a division of Pfizer, have unveiled the new logo and branding for VIATRIS™, the company formed by combining Mylan and Upjohn. The branding reflects Viatris's commitment to access, leadership, and partnership, aiming to redefine healthcare through its Global Healthcare Gateway™. The transaction is expected to close in Q4 2020, subject to closing conditions, and will create a company with 1,400 molecules, global reach, and 45,000 employees.

title: Pfizer, BioNTech's vaccine candidates get FDA's 'fast track' status
summary: Pfizer Inc and BioNTech SE announced that two of their experimental coronavirus vaccine candidates were granted "fast track" status by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, accelerating the regulatory review process. This news caused their stock prices to rise significantly, boosting market sentiment regarding COVID-19 vaccine development. While the fast track designation helps speed up review for drugs addressing unmet medical needs, analysts noted that such a designation doesn't necessarily indicate a candidate's potential and is likely to be granted to most COVID-19 treatments.

title: BNTX Stock Jumped 5% in Pre-market, BioNTech Vaccine Receives Fast Track Status from FDA
summary: BioNTech (BNTX) stock surged in pre-market trading after its experimental coronavirus vaccines, developed with Pfizer, received "Fast Track" designation from the FDA. This regulatory endorsement is seen as a significant milestone in the development of a safe and effective vaccine against SARS-CoV-2. The companies aim to produce millions of doses by the end of 2020 and over a billion by the end of 2021, leading to increased investor attention and a substantial rise in BioNTech's share price.

title: Pfizer, BioNTech Get $1.95 Billion Covid-19 Vaccine Order From U.S. Government
summary: The U.S. government has placed a $1.95 billion order with Pfizer and BioNTech for 100 million doses of their experimental COVID-19 vaccine, with an option to acquire another 500 million doses. The vaccine, which has shown promising early results, will be provided to Americans free of charge if it receives regulatory clearance. This agreement signifies the government's preparations to distribute a vaccine, once proven safe and effective.

title: Pfizer and US government reach $1.95 billion deal to produce millions of Covid-19 vaccine doses
summary: The US government announced a $1.95 billion deal with Pfizer to secure 100 million doses of a Covid-19 vaccine, with an option to acquire an additional 500 million doses. The vaccine, developed by Pfizer and BioNTech, would be delivered nationwide in Q4 2020 if it receives emergency use authorization and proves effective in trials, and would be available to Americans at no cost. This agreement is part of the Operation Warp Speed program aimed at making an effective Covid-19 vaccine readily available.

title: U.S. signs contract with Pfizer for COVID-19 vaccine doses
summary: The Trump administration has signed a contract with Pfizer to pay nearly $2 billion for 100 million doses of a COVID-19 vaccine, with an option to purchase an additional 500 million doses. This agreement is part of Operation Warp Speed, aiming to deliver 300 million vaccine doses by January 2021, contingent on FDA approval for safety and effectiveness. Americans are expected to receive the vaccine for free once authorized.

title: Pfizer Vaccine Deal, Microsoft's Strong Performance
summary: Pfizer announced a $1.95 billion deal with the U.S. government to deliver a coronavirus vaccine in 2021, causing its shares and BioNTech's shares to surge. Microsoft also reported strong fourth-quarter results, surpassing estimates with a 13% revenue increase, though net income decreased due to physical store closures. Tesla also beat Wall Street expectations for its second-quarter profits, with significant increases in cash and vehicle deliveries, and its stock continues to perform well.

title: US govt spends US$1.95 bil to secure Covid-19 vaccine
summary: The US government has agreed to pay Pfizer Inc and German biotech firm BioNTech SE $1.95 billion for 100 million doses of their Covid-19 vaccine candidate. This agreement includes an option for the US to acquire an additional 500 million doses and is part of the Trump administration's "Operation Warp Speed" to accelerate vaccine development. The vaccine candidate is currently undergoing testing, with regulatory approval expected as early as October if trials are successful.

title: Arcturus and Duke-NUS announce approval of clinical trials for COVID-19 vaccine candidate
summary: Arcturus Therapeutics Holdings Inc. and Duke-NUS Medical School have received approval for clinical trials of their COVID-19 vaccine candidate, LUNAR-COV19, from the Singapore Health Sciences Authority. This vaccine utilizes Arcturus' STARR™ technology and Duke-NUS's rapid screening platform, aiming for a single, low-dose administration. Human dosing is expected to begin soon in a study evaluating safety, tolerability, and immune response in up to 108 adults.

title: Glaucoma drug delivery devices enter new frontier
summary: This article discusses new developments in glaucoma drug delivery devices presented at the annual Glaucoma 360 meeting. Various companies are developing innovative solutions, including bioresorbable implants, micro-fluidic delivery systems, biodegradable implants, subconjunctival devices, and hand-held precise micro-dose applicators, all aimed at improving patient adherence and treatment efficacy for glaucoma. These advancements focus on long-term, sustained, and more convenient drug delivery compared to traditional eye drops.

title: U.S. to pay Pfizer, BioNTech $1.95 billion for COVID-19 vaccine
summary: The U.S. government has agreed to pay Pfizer Inc and BioNTech SE nearly $2 billion for 100 million doses of their COVID-19 vaccine, enough to inoculate 50 million people, pending safety and efficacy approval. The agreement includes an option for an additional 500 million doses, with the vaccine to be made available to Americans at no cost. Pfizer aims to begin late-stage trials soon and expects to manufacture up to 100 million doses globally by the end of 2020.

title: Mattel Appoints Diana Ferguson to Its Board of Directors
summary: Mattel Inc. has appointed Diana S. Ferguson, CFO of Cleveland Avenue LLC, to its board of directors, effective July 21, 2020. Ferguson, who brings extensive experience in corporate financial management and strategic planning, will serve on the board’s audit committee and become its chair on September 1. This appointment supports Mattel's strategy to transform into an IP-driven, high-performing toy company and drive shareholder value.

title: An Easier Way to Understand the Pharma Industry
summary: This article provides an overview of the global pharmaceutical industry, detailing its subfields, regulatory bodies, and growth drivers. It covers publicly traded stocks and ETFs, the industry's supply chain, and critical regulations, highlighting why the pharma sector is unique due to its high regulation and capital intensity. The piece also explores factors contributing to the industry's growth, such as an aging population, changing lifestyles, increased income, chronic diseases, and globalization.

title: Moderna gets further $472 million U.S. award for coronavirus vaccine development
summary: Moderna has received an additional $472 million from the U.S. government's BARDA to support the late-stage clinical development of its coronavirus vaccine candidate, bringing the total funding to approximately $955 million. The additional funding will support the expanded Phase 3 study planned to begin on July 27 with 30,000 participants. Moderna aims to deliver 500 million to 1 billion doses per year starting in 2021.

title: Global Phase 2/3 Clinical Trial for COVID-19 Vaccine Starts at NYU Langone Health
summary: NYU Langone Health announced the commencement of a global Phase 2/3 clinical trial for a lead mRNA COVID-19 vaccine candidate, with NYU Grossman School of Medicine participating as one of 120 centers. This phase follows successful initial safety trials and aims to enroll up to 30,000 healthy participants globally to assess the vaccine's ability to prevent SARS-CoV-2 infection. The trial is a collaboration between Pfizer Inc. and BioNTech SE, testing the BNT162b2 vaccine candidate, which has already shown promising immune responses in earlier phases.

title: Final test of Moderna’s COVID-19 vaccine trial begins
summary: The final stage of Moderna's COVID-19 vaccine study has commenced, with 30,000 US participants testing the experimental immunization. This trial, co-developed by the National Institutes of Health and Moderna, Inc., is the first of several large-scale studies planned for leading vaccine candidates through the fall. Researchers will monitor participants for infections to assess the vaccine's efficacy and safety.

title: Robust Growth Visible for Inhalation Anesthesia Market
summary: The Global Inhalation Anesthesia Market is projected to experience robust growth between 2020 and 2025, driven by an increase in emergency cases, accidents, and the aging population suffering from various diseases. Key players in this market include Baxter, AbbVie, Piramal Enterprises, Halocarbon Products, Hikma Pharmaceuticals, Lunan Pharmaceutical Group, Jiangsu Hengrui Medicine, and Fresenius Kabi. The market is segmented by type (Sevoflurane, Desflurane, Isoflurane), application (Induction, Maintenance), and region, with North America expected to show the highest CAGR.

title: Moderna and Pfizer Begin Late-Stage Vaccine Trials (Published 2020)
summary: Moderna and Pfizer have both initiated late-stage clinical trials for their respective coronavirus vaccines, each aiming to enroll 30,000 participants to assess safety and effectiveness. Moderna's trial began with volunteers receiving shots, while Pfizer, in partnership with BioNTech, also started its study after securing a $1.95 billion deal with the U.S. government for vaccine doses. Both studies will monitor for side effects and evaluate the vaccines' ability to prevent Covid-19 infection and severe illness.

title: Moderna Gets OK to Start Larger Trial for a Coronavirus Vaccine (Published 2020)
summary: Moderna has received approval from the FDA to proceed with a larger Phase 2 clinical trial for its experimental coronavirus vaccine, involving approximately 600 people. This trial aims to assess the vaccine's safety and replicate positive results from its initial phase. This move marks a significant step forward in the global race to develop a vaccine against the highly infectious coronavirus.

title: Trump Administration Selects Five Coronavirus Vaccine Candidates as Finalists (Published 2020)
summary: The Trump administration has selected five companies as finalists to develop a coronavirus vaccine, aiming for widespread inoculation by the end of the year. The chosen companies are Moderna, Oxford University/AstraZeneca, Johnson & Johnson, Merck, and Pfizer. While seen by the White House as a critical step in progress, many scientists view the goal of early availability as optimistic due to the complex nature of vaccine development.

title: Sonoco ThermoSafe Creating Industrywide PharmaPortal™
summary: Sonoco ThermoSafe is developing PharmaPortal™, a vendor-neutral blockchain platform built on IBM Blockchain Transparent Supply, to enhance transparency and traceability in the temperature-controlled pharmaceutical supply chain. This initiative aims to address inefficiencies contributing to an estimated $35 billion in losses within the $230 billion cold chain pharmaceutical distribution market. The platform will initially focus on traceability of temperature-controlled drugs like vaccines, ensuring an audit trail of environmental conditions, and will invite industry leaders to collaborate on its development.

title: AGILE: Phase III, Double-Blind, Randomised, Placebo-Controlled Study of Ivosidenib in Combination with Azacitidine in Adults with Newly Diagnosed Acute Myeloid Leukaemia and an IDH1 Mutation
summary: This article details the AGILE Phase III clinical trial, a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled study evaluating ivosidenib in combination with azacitidine for newly diagnosed acute myeloid leukaemia (AML) patients with an IDH1 mutation who are ineligible for intensive chemotherapy. The study builds on promising Phase Ib results, including a 78.3% overall response rate and 60.9% complete remission rate with a manageable safety profile. Key changes to the Phase III protocol include event-free survival as the primary endpoint and specified criteria for induction chemotherapy ineligibility.

title: U.S. Reaches $2.1 Billion Deal With Sanofi, GlaxoSmithKline For COVID-19 Vaccine Push
summary: The U.S. government announced a $2.1 billion deal with Sanofi and GlaxoSmithKline for COVID-19 vaccine development, including the purchase of 100 million doses. This agreement is part of Operation Warp Speed and marks the sixth vaccine candidate to join the portfolio and the largest vaccine deal to date. The companies have committed to making the vaccine affordable and accessible, with 100 million doses to be available to Americans at no cost if approved.

title: US to Pay $2.1 Billion to Sanofi, GSK in COVID-19 Vaccine Deal
summary: The US government has agreed to pay Sanofi SA and GlaxoSmithKline Plc $2.1 billion for COVID-19 vaccines sufficient to inoculate 50 million people, marking the largest deal yet under "Operation Warp Speed." This agreement also covers testing and manufacturing costs for the experimental vaccine, with options for the US to purchase an additional 500 million doses. Sanofi and GSK are also in talks to supply up to 300 million doses to the European Union.

title: Award-Winning Television Host Meredith Vieira Joins Pfizer's Find Your MBC Voice to Help Empower People Living with Metastatic Breast Cancer to Speak Up
summary: Meredith Vieira has partnered with Pfizer for the "Find Your MBC Voice" initiative, aiming to empower individuals with metastatic breast cancer (mBC) to actively engage in discussions about their treatment options with their doctors. The program provides a Treatment Discussion Guide and launches WMBC Radio, a streaming station offering resources and stories. This initiative seeks to improve communication and shared decision-making for those living with mBC, a condition for which there is no cure.

title: Pfizer reups PPD deal in a contract research pact spree
summary: Pfizer has expanded its contract research organization (CRO) partnerships by signing a new three-year agreement with PPD for drug development services, with an option to extend for two more years. This move follows similar extended pacts with Syneos Health and Icon, reinforcing Pfizer's strategy of utilizing preferred CROs. The financial terms of the deal were not disclosed.

title: PPD Signs New Service Agreement With Pfizer
summary: Wilmington-headquartered PPD Inc. (Nasdaq: PPD) has signed a new three-year agreement with Pfizer Inc. to provide drug development services, with optional two-year extensions. This agreement builds on their existing relationship, where PPD supports Pfizer's drug development initiatives across multiple therapeutic areas. Financial details were not disclosed, but PPD expressed commitment to innovative solutions and quality execution for Pfizer.

title: Regeneron and BioNTech Partner on Immunotherapy Combo for Melanoma
summary: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals and BioNTech have formed a strategic collaboration to develop an immunotherapy combination for melanoma. The partnership will combine BioNTech’s BNT111 FixVac product with Regeneron and Sanofi’s checkpoint inhibitor Libtayo (cemiplimab) and plans to initiate a randomized Phase II trial in patients with anti-PD1-refractory/relapsed, unresectable Stage III or IV cutaneous melanoma. The companies will equally share development costs and retain full commercial rights to their respective products.

title: FDA rejects a peanut allergy treatment, sinking a small biotech’s shares
summary: The FDA rejected DBV Technologies' peanut allergy treatment, Viaskin Peanut, citing design issues and requesting more clinical data and manufacturing information. This setback significantly impacted DBV's shares and financial outlook, while a rival treatment from Aimmune Therapeutics, Palforzia, saw a temporary stock increase despite initial sales challenges due to the coronavirus pandemic. Analysts believe the rejection could force DBV to raise more capital due to the costly new requirements.

title: Moderna sets high price in early coronavirus vaccine supply deals
summary: Moderna has set a high price of $32 to $37 per dose for its experimental coronavirus vaccine in early preorder deals, which is significantly more expensive than competitors. While these initial agreements are for small quantities, future larger supply deals might involve a lower price. This pricing strategy from Moderna is likely to generate controversy, especially when compared to the lower prices implied by deals made by Pfizer and Johnson & Johnson.

title: Pfizer, Amgen will rake in billions during 'golden age' for biosimilars: analyst
summary: An analyst report suggests that Pfizer and Amgen are entering a "golden age" for biosimilars, with Pfizer's biosimilar sales growing significantly and Amgen's biosimilar business also robust. Despite potential future pricing pressures, the U.S. market offers strong commercial prospects for biosimilars compared to Europe due to higher achievable prices. Both companies are expected to generate billions annually from their biosimilar portfolios in the coming years.

title: Johnson & Johnson pledges 100M coronavirus vaccine doses to U.S. for $10 each
summary: Johnson & Johnson has secured a deal with the U.S. government to supply 100 million doses of its COVID-19 vaccine candidate, Ad26.COV2.S, for just over $1 billion, pricing each dose at approximately $10. This agreement, which includes manufacturing in the U.S., allows for an additional purchase of 200 million doses. While still in early human trials, J&J anticipates initial results in September and could begin phase 3 efficacy testing next month.

title: With Court Win, BMS and Pfizer Stave Off Eliquis Generic Challengers – For Now
summary: Bristol Myers Squibb (BMS) and Pfizer secured a federal court victory, upholding patents for their anticoagulant drug Eliquis. This ruling prevents generic competitors Sigmapharm, Sunshine Lake, and Unichem from entering the market until at least 2026, and potentially until 2031 for some manufacturers, protecting a significant revenue stream for both companies. The decision follows previous settlements with Micro Labs Limited and Mylan Pharmaceuticals Inc., further solidifying BMS and Pfizer's market position for Eliquis.

title: Trump signs ‘Buy American’ executive order for essential drugs
summary: President Trump signed an executive order requiring federal agencies to purchase essential drugs and medical supplies from U.S. manufacturers. This initiative aims to reduce reliance on foreign supply chains and prevent shortages, a concern highlighted by the coronavirus pandemic. The order also directs the FDA to determine which drugs qualify, with exemptions for cost and availability, and seeks to streamline regulatory processes for domestic manufacturing.

title: Icelandic Biopharmaceutical Company Alvotech Signs Huge Contract with Teva
summary: Alvotech, an Icelandic biopharmaceutical company, has signed a significant collaboration agreement with Teva Pharmaceuticals. This partnership, one of the largest business contracts ever for an Icelandic company, focuses on commercializing five biosimilar product candidates in the US market. The agreement is expected to generate hundreds of billions of ISK for Alvotech over the next decade and will lead to an increase in staff at its Reykjavík headquarters.

title: Bausch + Lomb to be spun off. Rochester impact out of focus for now
summary: Bausch Health announced plans to spin off its Bausch + Lomb eye care division into a separate publicly traded entity. The immediate impact on Rochester, where Bausch + Lomb has over 1,100 employees and manufactures key eye products, is currently unclear though the Rochester facility is expected to be part of the new eye care business. This move follows Valeant's acquisition of Bausch + Lomb in 2013 and recent expansions at the Rochester site for contact lens production.

title: Bristol Myers, Pfizer fend off a key challenge to their top-selling heart drug
summary: A Delaware district court judge has upheld two key patents for Bristol Myers Squibb and Pfizer's blockbuster blood-thinner Eliquis, protecting it from generic competition from Sigmapharm, Sunshine Lake, and Unichem until 2031. This ruling is a significant victory for both companies, especially for Bristol Myers, as Eliquis is a critical revenue driver and helps offset debt from its acquisition of Celgene. While other generic versions might launch as early as 2026 due to prior settlements, the upholding of these patents secures Eliquis' market position for a longer period.

title: Pfizer agrees to manufacture Gilead's coronavirus drug remdesivir
summary: Pfizer has committed to manufacturing and supplying Gilead Sciences' antiviral drug remdesivir through a multiyear agreement. This collaboration aims to significantly increase the availability of the intravenous drug, which has been shown to reduce recovery times for some hospitalized coronavirus patients. Pfizer will produce the drug at its facility in McPherson, Kansas, contributing to global efforts to combat the COVID-19 crisis.

title: Pfizer to make Gilead's COVID-19 treatment remdesivir
summary: Pfizer Inc. announced a multiyear agreement to manufacture Gilead Sciences Inc.'s COVID-19 treatment, remdesivir. This deal comes as Gilead faces pressure to increase the supply of the antiviral drug, which has been difficult to access despite its proven efficacy for hospitalized COVID-19 patients. Pfizer will produce remdesivir at its McPherson, Kansas plant, aiming to boost global availability of the treatment.

title: WilmerHale Achieves Significant Victory for Bristol-Myers Squibb and Pfizer in Patent Suit
summary: WilmerHale secured a decisive trial victory for Bristol-Myers Squibb Company and Pfizer Inc. in a Hatch-Waxman litigation concerning patents for their blockbuster drug Eliquis®. The District of Delaware court found that proposed generic products from three defendants infringed on patents expiring in 2026 and 2031, following a case that initially involved 25 generic companies.

title: Japan plans to buy AstraZeneca’s COVID-19 vaccine
summary: Japan plans to acquire AstraZeneca's experimental COVID-19 vaccine and support local manufacturing of Novavax's candidate to bolster its vaccine stockpile amidst rising infections. The country will order 120 million doses from AstraZeneca and has a separate deal to buy 120 million doses of Pfizer and BioNTech's vaccine candidate. Japan is also developing its own vaccines while procuring supplies from international pharmaceutical companies.

title: Kansas plant will produce Covid-19 drug that is in short supply
summary: Gilead Sciences Inc. has partnered with Pfizer Inc. to increase the production of its Covid-19 treatment, remdesivir. A Pfizer plant in Kansas will be involved in manufacturing the drug, which is currently in short supply. This initiative aims to address the urgent demand for remdesivir among hospitals and state attorneys general for treating Covid-19 patients.

title: Dr.Reddy’s launches generic version of Ciprodex
summary: Dr. Reddy's Laboratories has launched a generic version of Ciprodex (Ciprofloxacin 0.3% and Dexamethasone 0.1%) Otic Suspension, USP, in the U.S. market. This product, indicated for treating ear infections, is the first-to-market generic and follows USFDA approval. Ciprodex had U.S. sales of approximately $453 million MAT for the twelve months ending June 2020.

title: US Makes Deal with Biotech Company for 100 Million Doses of Potential COVID-19 Vaccine
summary: The U.S. government has announced a deal with biotech company Moderna to acquire 100 million doses of a potential COVID-19 vaccine. This comes as three vaccine candidates in the U.S. are in final human trials, while Russia has controversially registered its own vaccine, Sputnik V, before completing Phase 3 trials. Other countries like China and Mexico are also advancing their vaccine development and trial efforts.

title: US government strikes $1.525 billion deal with Moderna for 100 million doses of its Covid-19 vaccine
summary: The US government has finalized a $1.525 billion deal with Moderna Inc. to secure 100 million doses of its Covid-19 vaccine, mRNA-1273, once approved. The contract allows for an additional 400 million doses and aims to provide vaccines to Americans at no cost as part of Operation Warp Speed. This agreement follows similar deals with Pfizer and Janssen, emphasizing the Trump administration's efforts to create a diverse vaccine portfolio.

title: U.S. inks $1.5 billion deal with Moderna for 100 million doses of COVID-19 vaccine
summary: The United States has finalized a $1.5 billion agreement with Moderna Inc. to secure 100 million doses of its potential COVID-19 vaccine, mRNA-1273. This deal is part of the U.S. government's Operation Warp Speed, aiming to deliver a vaccine by year-end, and follows other advanced purchase agreements with various pharmaceutical companies to ensure a substantial vaccine supply for the nation. Moderna's vaccine candidate is currently in its final testing stage, with results expected in September.

title: Bristol Myers Squibb takes on racial inequality with $300M pledge to up diversity, improve healthcare access
summary: Bristol Myers Squibb has pledged $300 million over the next five years to combat racial inequality by increasing diversity within its workforce, enhancing clinical trial diversity, and improving healthcare access for underserved populations globally. This initiative, spurred by recent discussions around racism, includes specific goals such as doubling executive roles for Black and Latinx staff in the U.S. by 2022 and training 250 diverse clinical investigators. The company also aims to address issues like inadequate minority patient inclusion in clinical trials and will spend $1 billion with diverse-owned suppliers by 2025.

title: 4 innovative ways Johnson & Johnson has helped protect the public's health during outbreaks since the late 1800s
summary: Johnson & Johnson has a long history of contributing to public health during outbreaks, dating back to the late 1800s. The company's efforts include educating the public about hygiene, being one of the first to vaccinate employees during a smallpox outbreak, mass-producing epidemic masks during the Spanish flu, and actively working on treatments and vaccines for current global health threats like COVID-19, tuberculosis, and Ebola. These initiatives demonstrate Johnson & Johnson's sustained commitment to safeguarding global public health.

title: Phase I/II study of COVID-19 RNA vaccine BNT162b1 in adults
summary: This study reports available safety, tolerability, and immunogenicity data from an ongoing placebo-controlled, observer-blinded dose-escalation study of the COVID-19 RNA vaccine BNT162b1 in 45 healthy adults. The vaccine demonstrated dose-dependent local reactions and systemic events that were generally mild to moderate and transient, with a 30-μg dose showing robust immunogenicity comparable or superior to convalescent sera. These promising results support further evaluation and accelerated clinical development of this mRNA vaccine candidate.

title: Kaiser Permanente joins late-stage COVID-19 vaccine study
summary: Kaiser Permanente has begun participating in a phase 3 clinical trial for an investigational SARS-CoV-2 vaccine developed by Pfizer, Inc. and BioNTech, aiming to enroll approximately 1,400 participants across four sites in California and Oregon. The organization, with its extensive experience in vaccine research, is contributing to determining the vaccine's effectiveness and safety. This randomized, double-blind trial is crucial for gathering data on safety, immune response, and efficacy for regulatory review.

title: Pfizer's COVID vaccine shows 'robust' results in early trial
summary: Pfizer's experimental COVID-19 vaccine, BNT162b1, demonstrated a robust immune response in an early-stage trial involving 45 healthy adults. The RNA-based vaccine elicited significantly higher levels of neutralizing antibodies compared to those recovering from SARS-CoV-2, with responses increasing with dose and a second shot. While generally well-tolerated, phase 3 trials are necessary to confirm its safety, strength, and duration of protection.

title: US eyes controversial human challenge trials for COVID-19 vaccine
summary: US government scientists are beginning to manufacture a synthetic strain of the novel coronavirus for potential use in human challenge trials, where volunteers would be intentionally infected after vaccination. These controversial trials, advocated by groups like 1 Day Sooner, would aim to accelerate vaccine testing but raise significant ethical concerns due to the lack of "rescue therapies" for COVID-19. While the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) considers such studies for future vaccine generations, many scientists emphasize prioritizing current field trials and question the ethical and practical implications of challenging healthy, young individuals when there's no treatment and the pandemic is widespread.

title: Genentech’s New NMOSD Drug Offers At-Home Treatment, Lower Cost
summary: Genentech has introduced a new NMOSD drug, Enspryng, which provides at-home treatment options for patients. The drug is priced lower than its competitors from Alexion and Viela Bio. Enspryng had already received approvals in Canada, Japan, and Switzerland before its announcement for US availability.

title: Yale and Yale New Haven Hospital begin Phase 3 trial of COVID-19 vaccine
summary: Yale School of Medicine and Yale New Haven Hospital have commenced Phase 3 of the Pfizer COVID-19 vaccine trial.
