summary: Indiana Attorney General Todd Rokita has disclosed ongoing advisory roles with several private businesses, including a $25,000 annual payment from a pharmaceutical company and $15,000 in stock. These roles continued into his term as Attorney General, raising concerns from the state Democratic Party about potential conflicts of interest. Rokita's office states he is in compliance with legal and ethics guidelines.

title: The corona hunters from Germany
summary: This article discusses the rapid development of COVID-19 vaccines by German biotech companies, primarily BioNTech and CureVac. It highlights BioNTech's swift success with its mRNA vaccine, co-developed with Pfizer, and CureVac's ongoing efforts. The piece also touches on the significant investments, German billionaire backing, and international collaborations that have propelled these companies to the forefront of the pandemic response.

title: Pfizer Alleges Micro Labs Infringing on Xeljanz Patents
summary: Pfizer and its subsidiaries have filed a complaint against Micro Labs Ltd. in the District of Delaware, alleging infringement of patents related to its drug Xeljanz. Micro Labs submitted an abbreviated new drug application (ANDA) for a generic version of 10 mg tofacitinib citrate tablets, claiming non-infringement due to patent invalidity. Pfizer contends that the manufacturing, marketing, and selling of Micro Labs' ANDA product before the expiration of Pfizer's patents constitutes infringement and seeks injunctive relief and monetary damages.

title: COVID: Sanofi starts human trials of 2nd vaccine candidate
summary: French pharmaceutical firm Sanofi has initiated human trials for its second COVID-19 vaccine candidate, developed with US company Translate Bio, utilizing mRNA technology. This comes despite its first vaccine, created with GlaxoSmithKline, still being in the testing phase. The trials involve 415 healthy adults, with results expected in the third quarter of 2021, though approval is not anticipated this year.

title: Pfizer (PFE) CEO Albert Bourla’s Pay Climbed 17% to $21 Million in 2020
summary: Pfizer Inc. CEO Albert Bourla's total compensation for 2020 rose by 17% to $21 million. This increase coincided with the pharmaceutical giant being the first to receive U.S. authorization for a coronavirus vaccine. The pay package included his salary, bonus, stock, and other incentive pay.

title: BioNTech Recruits Rivals to Boost Covid-19 Vaccine Production - WSJ
summary: BioNTech is forming a new manufacturing alliance with 13 companies, including Novartis AG, Merck KGaA, and Sanofi SA, to boost Covid-19 vaccine production. This initiative aims to address a global shortage of vaccine doses and counter a rebound in infections. Their ambitious goal is to produce two billion doses this year.

title: ‘Most comprehensive’ study yet finds Pfizer vaccine is highly effective at preventing infection
summary: A new study conducted in Israel has found the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine to be 97% effective in preventing symptomatic disease, critical disease, and death, and 94% effective against asymptomatic infections. This real-world evidence, gathered between January and March 2021 when the B.1.1.7 variant was dominant, confirms the high efficacy observed in clinical trials. The findings suggest the vaccine can significantly reduce severe cases and transmission, offering hope for combating the pandemic globally.

title: Ocugen Needs Pieces To Fall Into Place Before It’s a Solid Vaccine Play
summary: Ocugen (OCGN) stock, despite a significant rally, remains a speculative investment in the Covid-19 vaccine space. While its partner Bharat Biotech reported 81% efficacy for Covaxin in interim trials, the vaccine faces high hurdles for U.S. approval, including potential FDA requirements for U.S.-based studies and intense competition from established players like Moderna, Pfizer, Johnson & Johnson, and Novavax. The company's valuation of over $1.5 billion is considered largely unjustified given these challenges.

title: Brazil signs Pfizer deal for 100 million vaccine doses: source
summary: Brazil has officially secured a deal with Pfizer Inc. to acquire 100 million doses of its COVID-19 vaccine. This agreement follows recent discussions between Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro and Pfizer executives, resolving previous negotiation delays. The deal aims to bolster Brazil's vaccination efforts against the coronavirus.

title: Moderna begins testing its COVID-19 vaccine in children as young as 6 months
summary: Moderna has initiated a clinical trial for its COVID-19 vaccine in children as young as 6 months old, aiming to determine its safety and efficacy in young populations. The trial will enroll approximately 6,750 volunteers in the U.S. and Canada, testing various doses and comparing the vaccine to a placebo. This study is crucial as COVID-19 cases are less frequent in children, potentially affecting the statistical significance of efficacy calculations based solely on infection rates, thus immune response will also be a key metric.

title: Pfizer to halt biosimilar output in China, sell assets to WuXi Biologics
summary: Pfizer Inc. announced it will cease producing biosimilar products in China and sell its Hangzhou unit to WuXi Biologics Inc. The U.S. drugmaker stated that the site was originally intended to manufacture three biosimilars for the Chinese market, but other evaluated products did not meet the necessary production scale. WuXi Biologics confirmed the acquisition will help meet the surging demand for drug substance and product manufacturing, with the deal expected to close in the first half of the year.

title: Pfizer Scales Down Biosimilars Activity in China
summary: Pfizer is ceasing its biosimilars production in China, selling its $350 million Hangzhou plant to WuXi Biologics. This decision comes after a comprehensive review of the biosimilars market and Pfizer's global manufacturing network, despite China's recent reforms to encourage biologics development. Pfizer will continue to produce drugs for the China market through other means, while WuXi Biologics will acquire the plant and its workforce to meet surging manufacturing demands.

title: Jazz Pharmaceuticals and Hypersomnia Foundation Launch Campaign to Increase Understanding and Awareness of Idiopathic Hypersomnia
summary: Jazz Pharmaceuticals and the Hypersomnia Foundation have launched the "I Have IH" campaign to increase understanding and awareness of idiopathic hypersomnia. A survey conducted as part of the campaign revealed a significant lack of awareness and education among healthcare providers regarding IH, leading to misdiagnoses and delayed diagnoses for patients. The initiative aims to empower patients and improve discussions with healthcare providers about this debilitating sleep disorder.

title: Self-amplifying may be the next frontier in RNA therapies
summary: Self-amplifying RNA (saRNA) is emerging as a promising next-generation RNA therapy, building on the success of mRNA vaccines. saRNA offers a differentiated immune profile, enabling lower and longer-lasting doses, and is being explored for both infectious diseases and cancer due to its ability to induce strong cytotoxic T cell responses. Companies like Arcturus Therapeutics Holdings Inc. and Glaxosmithkline plc are focusing on this technology.

title: 2021 Best in Class 401(k) Plans
summary: PLANSPONSOR has announced its seventh annual "Best in Class 401(k) Plan" designations for 2021. This recognition is based on a proprietary system evaluating over 30 criteria related to plan design, oversight, and participant outcomes. The article lists the 20 companies that received this designation for 2021, and also notes that plans must requalify every five years.

title: Pfizer to go solo on new vaccines using mRNA technology - WSJ
summary: Pfizer plans to independently develop new vaccines for other viruses using the messenger RNA (mRNA) technology that was successful in its COVID-19 shot. This move follows the drugmaker's collaboration with BioNTech on the COVID-19 vaccine and signifies its confidence in pursuing mRNA technology on its own. The success of mRNA technology in the COVID-19 vaccine has spurred wider interest in its application beyond vaccines, including in cancer treatment.

title: WSJ News Exclusive | Pfizer Goes It Alone to Expand Vaccine Business Beyond Covid-19 Pandemic
summary: Pfizer plans to expand its vaccine business beyond Covid-19 by utilizing the gene-based mRNA technology developed for its successful Covid-19 vaccine. CEO Albert Bourla stated that the company gained significant experience working with BioNTech and is now prepared to independently pursue mRNA technology to target other diseases. This move positions Pfizer to become a leader in this new vaccine technology.

title: It’s a tRNA World: How aTyr Transformed tRNA Synthetases into Clinical Stage Medicines
summary: aTyr Pharma has transformed tRNA synthetases, once considered basic enzymes for protein synthesis, into a potential source for clinical-stage medicines. The company, founded on the discovery that fragments of tRNA synthetases can act as extracellular modulators, is advancing ATYR1923 for inflammatory lung diseases and exploring other applications, including oncology and COVID-19 related inflammation. CEO Sanjay Shukla discusses the company's evolution, strategic partnerships, and future plans to develop multiple therapies from this novel area of biology.

title: Pfizer Inc. stock rises Thursday, still underperforms market
summary: Pfizer Inc. stock saw a modest gain of 0.17% on Thursday, closing at $35.67, even as the broader market, including the S&P 500 and Dow Jones, also rose. Despite this increase, Pfizer's stock remained $7.41 below its 52-week high. The company's trading volume was also below its 50-day average.

title: The Tubulin Inhibitor VERU-111 in Combination With Vemurafenib Provides an Effective Treatment of Vemurafenib-Resistant A375 Melanoma
summary: This research investigates the effectiveness of VERU-111, an orally bioavailable tubulin inhibitor, in combination with vemurafenib (Vem) for treating vemurafenib-resistant A375 melanoma. The study demonstrates that this combination significantly inhibits cancer cell proliferation and tumor growth in vitro and in vivo. Key findings indicate that VERU-111 helps overcome Vem-resistance by arresting the cell cycle and modulating the Skp2-AKT signaling pathway, offering a promising new treatment strategy for melanoma patients with BRAF (V600E) mutations.

title: iShares Launches International Small Cap Value ETF, 'ISVL'
summary: BlackRock's iShares has launched a new ETF, the iShares International Developed Small Cap Value Factor ETF (ISVL), to cater to growing investor interest in international small-cap value exposure. This launch follows the recent success of their U.S. counterpart, SVAL, and aims to capitalize on the rally in value stocks since late 2020. ISVL offers a transparent and cost-efficient way for investors to access historically rewarded value and size factors in international markets.

title: EMA accepts regulatory submission for Takeda’s dengue vaccine candidate
summary: The European Medicines Agency (EMA) has accepted Takeda’s regulatory submission for its dengue vaccine candidate, TAK-003, for individuals aged four to 60. This filing includes long-term Phase III safety and efficacy data, with Takeda also planning submissions in several dengue-endemic countries and through the EU-M4all procedure. The company aims to provide a widely available vaccine to address the significant global health burden of dengue.

title: Merck sets up Organon spinout with a women’s health medical device acquisition
summary: Merck is acquiring Alydia Health, a women's health medical device startup, for an upfront payment of $215 million, with an additional $25 million contingent milestone payment. This acquisition is intended to bolster the portfolio of Organon, Merck's women's health and off-patent drugs spinout company, ahead of its expected completion in the second quarter of this year. Alydia Health's Jada system, a device to prevent postpartum hemorrhage, will be a key product for the new entity.

title: Pfizer, Moderna Vaccines Highly Effective After First Shot in Real-World Use
summary: A real-world US study by the CDC found that Pfizer and Moderna COVID-19 vaccines greatly reduced the risk of infection after the first dose, with an 80% reduction two weeks post-first shot and a 90% reduction two weeks after the second shot. The study, involving nearly 4,000 US healthcare personnel and first responders, validated earlier findings and confirmed the vaccines' efficacy against asymptomatic infections. While some countries extended dose schedules due to supply limits, US officials continued to recommend two doses based on clinical trial schedules.

title: Pfizer Breaks Ground on One of the World’s Most Technically Advanced Sterile Injectable Pharmaceutical Production Facilities
summary: Pfizer has broken ground on its new Modular Aseptic Processing (MAP) facility in Kalamazoo, Michigan, which will be one of the world's most technically advanced sterile injectable pharmaceutical production facilities. This $465 million investment is expected to create approximately 450 new high-wage jobs in Kalamazoo County. The facility will play a crucial role in manufacturing over 150 products, including the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine, emphasizing Michigan's leadership in life sciences and medical device manufacturing.

title: White House knew more than a week ago of J&J contractor vaccine-supply problems
summary: Senior Biden administration officials were aware of production problems at Johnson & Johnson's contractor, Emergent BioSolutions, more than a week before the public learned that 15 million vaccine doses were ruined. These issues will likely cause delays in future J&J vaccine shipments, making distribution to states patchy in the coming weeks. The Biden administration has requested J&J to directly oversee Emergent's manufacturing process to resolve the issues.

title: Pfizer Vaccine Gives 100% Protection at Ages 12-15 in Study
summary: Pfizer announced that its Covid-19 vaccine was 100% effective in a late-stage trial for children aged 12 to 15. This result could allow adolescents to receive the vaccine before the new school year. Pfizer and BioNTech SE plan to submit these findings to U.S. and European regulators to expand their vaccine authorization to this younger age group.

title: Johnson & Johnson COVID- 19 Vaccine Manufacturing Error Affects 15 Million Doses
summary: A manufacturing error at a Baltimore facility affected 15 million doses worth of an ingredient for Johnson & Johnson’s COVID-19 vaccine. Johnson & Johnson stated that the affected batch did not meet quality standards and was not advanced to later manufacturing stages, and confirmed it still met its March delivery targets and expects to meet future commitments. The company is now expanding its oversight at the Emergent BioSolutions facility to ensure quality control.

title: China Health Care: A Rediscovered Sector Keeps Its Momentum
summary: China's healthcare sector, particularly biotechnology, experienced significant growth and innovation in 2020, driven by the COVID-19 pandemic and government reforms encouraging technological advancement. The KraneShares MSCI All China Health Care Index ETF (KURE) performed strongly, reflecting increasing healthcare demands from an aging population and a shift towards an innovation-driven model. This article explores the sub-industries of China's healthcare sector and highlights the substantial potential for long-term growth, especially in biopharmaceuticals, supported by R&D spending and international partnerships.

title: Reopening Economies and the Resurgence in Value
summary: This article discusses the resurgence of value investing strategies as economies reopen, highlighting how value indexes have historically outperformed during recovery and expansion phases. It examines several factors contributing to this trend, including rising interest rates and inflation expectations, and attractive valuations of value stocks in a historical context. The authors also consider sector and country selections, and the significant inflows into value ETFs, questioning whether this marks a long-term shift in market leadership.

title: Roughly 15 million doses of the Johnson & Johnson vaccine were ruined because of a factory mixup, report says
summary: A factory mixup at a Baltimore plant run by Emergent Biosolutions led to the spoilage of approximately 15 million doses of Johnson & Johnson's COVID-19 vaccine due to human error. The incident will delay future shipments, though doses already delivered are unaffected, and Johnson & Johnson states it still expects to meet its delivery commitments. The FDA is investigating, and the Biden administration has reportedly asked J&J to directly supervise production at the facility.

title: Pfizer Shot Remains More Than 91% Effective After Six Months
summary: The Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine maintained high effectiveness against symptomatic illness for at least six months, with a 91.3% overall efficacy rate and 92.6% in the U.S. These long-term results from a trial of over 46,000 people could support expanding the vaccine's regulatory approvals. The vaccination also effectively prevented severe cases of the disease.

title: Pfizer data suggests COVID-19 shot protects against SA variant
summary: New clinical trial data from Pfizer and BioNTech indicates their COVID-19 vaccine is 100% effective in preventing illness among participants in South Africa, where the B1351 variant is dominant. The companies also stated their vaccine is approximately 91% effective overall at preventing COVID-19, based on updated trial data extending up to six months. This data supports the possibility of the vaccine protecting against currently circulating variants and aids in the pursuit of full US regulatory approval.

title: Pfizer Expanding Operations in Fast-Growing Tampa and Restarting Manufacturing in Michigan
summary: Pfizer announced plans to create a professional services office in Tampa, Florida, consolidating finance, HR, digital services, and sourcing into a central hub, generating hundreds of new jobs. Concurrently, Pfizer is restarting a major construction project in Portage, Michigan, near Kalamazoo, originally approved in 2018, which is expected to create 450 new jobs and involves an $800 million investment for a new modular aseptic processing facility. These expansions highlight Pfizer's growth and investment in key operational and manufacturing capabilities.

title: U.S. puts J&J in charge of plant that botched Covid vaccine, removes AstraZeneca
summary: The U.S. has appointed Johnson & Johnson to take full control of the Emergent BioSolutions facility in Baltimore after 15 million doses of its COVID-19 vaccine were ruined due to a mix-up with AstraZeneca's vaccine ingredients. This decision removes AstraZeneca from using the plant and aims to prevent future manufacturing errors. J&J has reaffirmed its commitment to deliver 100 million doses to the government by the end of May.

title: IceCure shares up as tumor-freezing tech gets FDA breakthrough device nod
summary: IceCure Medical, an Israeli company, saw its shares rise significantly after its ProSense tumor-freezing technology received "breakthrough device" designation from the US FDA. This recognition, given for devices treating life-threatening conditions, is expected to expedite the marketing approval process for ProSense, particularly for breast cancer treatment. The technology offers a minimally invasive alternative to surgery for various tumors.

title: Walgreens Not Following U.S. Guidance on Pfizer Vaccine Spacing (Published 2021)
summary: Walgreens initial scheduling of Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine second doses at four-week intervals, rather than the CDC-recommended three weeks, caused confusion among customers and drew attention from federal health officials. This decision was made to simplify scheduling, as Moderna's vaccine uses a four-week gap, but Walgreens has since committed to aligning with the CDC guidance for Pfizer's vaccine. The CDC states that while three weeks is recommended, up to six weeks between doses is acceptable if necessary, and there is no evidence that an extra week decreases vaccine effectiveness.

title: Israel Biotech Fund closes $112m second fund
summary: Israel Biotech Fund (IBF) has successfully closed its second fund at $112 million, exceeding its initial target. The fund, co-founded by Dr. David Sidransky, Dr. Yuval Cabilly, and Ido Zairi, invests in drug development and medical diagnostics and has attracted major investors like Harel Insurance and Bristol Myers Squibb. IBF has seen significant achievements in its portfolio companies, including Biond Biologics selling cancer treatment rights to Sanofi for over $1 billion and Ayala Pharmaceuticals completing a Nasdaq IPO.

title: Therapeutic application of alpha-1-antitrypsin in COVID-19
summary: This study investigates the therapeutic potential of Alpha-1-antitrypsin (AAT) for COVID-19, highlighting its anti-proteolytic and anti-inflammatory properties. Findings suggest that AAT inhibits SARS-CoV-2 activity in human cell models and was well-tolerated in a small cohort of COVID-19 patients, showing associated clinical stabilization and reduced inflammation. The authors propose AAT as a promising candidate for further evaluation in randomized controlled trials for both early disease stages and severe cases.

title: For Biden, a New Virus Dilemma: How to Handle a Looming Glut of Vaccine (Published 2021)
summary: The Biden administration faces a dilemma regarding a projected surplus of COVID-19 vaccine doses by mid-May, as U.S. manufacturing outstrips domestic demand. While a significant portion of the world lacks vaccine access and some countries are restricting exports, the U.S. government must decide whether to keep, modify, or redirect its substantial future orders. Officials are considering factors like potential booster shots, vaccination for children, and new variants, alongside the ethical implications of global vaccine inequity.

title: Targeting Overseas Tax Shelters (Published 2021)
summary: This article discusses how Bristol Myers Squibb used offshore tax shelters in Ireland and other locations to avoid paying an estimated $1.4 billion in U.S. federal income taxes. The Biden administration plans to crack down on these practices by proposing a global minimum corporate tax rate of 21% to fund infrastructure projects. The article explores the history of such tax avoidance schemes, the motivations behind them, and the challenges the Biden administration faces in implementing its new tax policies.

title: NIH begins study of allergic reactions to Moderna, Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccines
summary: The NIH has launched a Phase 2 clinical trial to investigate if individuals with severe allergies or mast cell disorders face an elevated risk of allergic reactions to Moderna or Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccines. The study, involving 3,400 adults, aims to understand the biological mechanisms behind these reactions and identify predictive genetic patterns. This research seeks to provide crucial data to help medical professionals advise allergic patients on the risks and benefits of COVID-19 vaccination.

title: Celcuity Announces Worldwide Licensing Agreement with Pfizer to Develop and Commercialize Gedatolisib, a First-in-Class PI3K/mTOR Inhibitor for Breast Cancer
summary: Celcuity announces a global licensing agreement with Pfizer for gedatolisib, a PI3K/mTOR inhibitor, to develop and commercialize it for breast cancer treatment. Celcuity paid an upfront fee of $10 million in cash and stock, with Pfizer eligible for up to $330 million in milestone payments and royalties. The agreement leverages Celcuity's CELsignia platform to advance this potential first-in-class targeted therapy, which has shown promise in preliminary Phase 1b clinical trials for ER+/HER2-negative advanced or metastatic breast cancer.

title: The Messenger
summary: Kristen Park Hopson '01, a leader in molecular medicine, discusses how mRNA technology is revolutionizing drug discovery and development, exemplified by Moderna's COVID-19 vaccine. The article highlights the speed of mRNA vaccine creation, its potential applications beyond infectious diseases, and the role of machine learning in accelerating the development of new medicines through intentional drug generation rather than traditional trial-and-error. Hopson emphasizes the importance of applying lessons learned during the pandemic to streamline future drug development for various diseases, including personalized cancer treatments.

title: Q&A: BioNTech vaccine is only ‘mRNA 1.0’. This is just the beginning, say co-founders
summary: Dr. Özlem Türeci and Dr. Uğur Şahin, co-founders of BioNTech, discuss the transformative potential of mRNA vaccines beyond Covid-19, calling the current vaccine "mRNA 1.0." They explain how the technology's speed and effectiveness open doors for new vaccines against infectious diseases like the flu and cancer, leveraging their prior work in cancer immunotherapy. The co-founders also touch upon the surprisingly high efficacy of their Covid-19 vaccine and the ongoing need for real-world data to understand its broader impact.

title: Celcuity and Pfizer Enter Agreement for Breast Cancer Drug Following Positive Data
summary: Celcuity and Pfizer have signed a global licensing agreement for gedatolisib, Pfizer's PI3K/mTOR inhibitor for breast cancer, following positive Phase Ib trial data. Celcuity will pay Pfizer $5 million cash and $5 million in common stock upfront, with Pfizer eligible for up to $330 million in milestone payments and royalties. Celcuity plans to launch a Phase II/III trial pending FDA feedback to further evaluate gedatolisib.

title: Pfizer asks US to allow more kids to get vaccine
summary: Pfizer and BioNTech SE have requested the U.S. Food and Drug Administration to expand the emergency use authorization for their COVID-19 vaccine to include adolescents aged 12 through 15. Preliminary results from late-stage testing in this age group show the vaccine is safe and 100% effective in preventing infections, with side effects consistent with those observed in older age groups. The companies are working with regulators globally to secure authorization for this younger demographic.

title: Celcuity Stock Surges After Pfizer Licensing Agreement
summary: Shares of biotechnology company Celcuity Inc (NASDAQ: CELC) surged on Friday after the company revealed it has entered into a global licensing agreement with Pfizer Inc (NYSE: PFE), granting Celcuity exclusive rights to Pfizer’s gedatolisib, a Phase 1b pan-PI3K/mTOR inhibitor, which is in clinical development for the treatment of patients with metastatic breast cancer. Celcuity paid an upfront license fee of $5 million of cash and $5 million of its common stock, with Pfizer eligible to receive up to $330 million in development and sales-based milestone payments and tiered royalties.

title: Sanofi Snatches Up Tidal Therapeutics in $470 Million Deal
summary: Sanofi has acquired Tidal Therapeutics in a deal worth up to $470 million, including an upfront payment of $160 million. Tidal Therapeutics specializes in developing nanoparticles to deliver messenger RNA (mRNA) to reprogram immune cells for oncology and immune diseases. This acquisition aims to develop in-body CAR-T-like therapies, expanding treatment options for a broader patient population. Sanofi also recently completed the acquisition of Kymab Group Ltd. for $1.1 billion upfront, focusing on immune-mediated and immuno-oncology treatments.

title: How the Johnson & Johnson COVID-19 vaccine works
summary: The Johnson & Johnson (Janssen) COVID-19 vaccine utilizes an adenovirus, a viral vector, to deliver the virus' DNA to cells, prompting the immune system to produce antibodies against the spike protein. This approach differs from mRNA vaccines like Pfizer and Moderna, but both ultimately equip the body to recognize and fight the coronavirus. Researchers have been working with adenovirus technology since the 1970s, with similar platforms used for Ebola and HIV vaccines, contributing to the quick approval processes due to existing safety data.

title: Covid-19: Johnson & Johnson Vaccine Pause Is Another Hurdle For Europe (Published 2021)
summary: The Johnson & Johnson vaccine rollout faced significant hurdles in Europe and the U.S. after federal health agencies paused its use due to rare blood clotting cases, mirroring earlier concerns with the AstraZeneca vaccine. This pause, while seen as a setback for vaccination efforts, particularly in Europe which had struggled with supply, was deemed temporary by U.S. officials who emphasized that alternative vaccines were ample. Public health experts debated the impact on vaccine hesitancy versus the necessity of transparency regarding potential side effects.

title: Johnson & Johnson vaccine suspension – a doctor explains what this means for you
summary: The article explains the temporary suspension of the Johnson & Johnson COVID-19 vaccine due to a potential rare side effect: blood clots in the brain combined with low platelet counts. Dr. William Petri clarifies this is a treatable condition, distinct from reactions to mRNA vaccines, affecting about one in a million recipients. The CDC and FDA paused vaccinations for further review, emphasizing their commitment to vaccine safety.

title: Why the Johnson & Johnson vaccine is more effective than you think
summary: This article explains why the Johnson & Johnson COVID-19 vaccine is more effective than its initial efficacy numbers might suggest. While its overall efficacy against any symptomatic infection was reported at 66%, the vaccine showed 85% effectiveness in preventing severe disease and complete protection against COVID-19 related hospitalization and death as of Day 28, similar to other mRNA vaccines. Experts emphasize focusing on protection against severe outcomes rather than mild symptoms, and highlight the convenience of J&J's single-dose regimen.

title: Mayo Clinic responds to the Johnson & Johnson COVID-19 vaccine pause
summary: Mayo Clinic has paused the distribution of the Johnson & Johnson COVID-19 vaccine at its Midwest locations following a joint recommendation from the CDC and FDA due to rare blood clotting events. This pause is out of an abundance of caution while a review is underway, with an Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP) meeting scheduled to evaluate reported data. Patients who received the Johnson & Johnson vaccine within the last three weeks and experience severe new symptoms like headaches, leg pain, abdominal pain, or shortness of breath should seek emergency care; however, this advisory does not affect Pfizer and Moderna vaccines.

title: What is Novavax, Australia’s third COVID vaccine option? And when will we get it?
summary: Australia has secured 51 million doses of the Novavax COVID-19 vaccine, making it the country's third vaccine option alongside Pfizer and AstraZeneca. While Pfizer is now the preferred vaccine for adults under 50 and AstraZeneca for those over 50, Novavax offers a different "protein subunit" technology. Initial trials showed Novavax to be highly effective (96%) against the original COVID-19 strain and 86% effective against the UK variant, with 100% protection against severe disease despite lower efficacy (55%) against the South African variant.

title: Sangamo Therapeutics Stock Looks Attractive At $11
summary: Sangamo Therapeutics (NASDAQ: SGMO) stock appears attractive at its current price of $11, following a 30% year-to-date correction. The company, focused on genomic medicine, maintains a strong pipeline despite past stock price declines attributed to P/S multiple contraction and increased share issuance. Key collaborations with pharmaceutical giants like Pfizer and Sanofi, coupled with promising clinical trials, suggest potential for significant upside in the future.

title: Gross-to-Net Bubble Update: Net Prices Drop (Again) at Six Top Drugmakers
summary: This article analyzes pricing data from six major pharmaceutical companies (Eli Lilly, GlaxoSmithKline, Janssen, Merck, Novartis, and Sanofi) for 2020, revealing that while list prices saw modest growth, net drug prices declined for most, consistent with a four-year trend. The author highlights the growing "gross-to-net bubble," where significant rebates and discounts mean manufacturers earn less than half of the list price, driven by factors like PBM concentration, 340B program growth, and formulary exclusions. The article criticizes the focus on list prices as misleading and calls for policies addressing the gross-to-net gaps to shield patients and enhance competition.

title: Chinese official acknowledges low effectiveness of the country’s Covid vaccines. (Published 2021)
summary: A senior Chinese official, Gao Fu, director of China's disease control center, stated that the country's COVID-19 vaccines might require adjustments such as greater doses or combined shots due to their low effectiveness. These comments, later clarified as being misunderstood, imply potential changes for distribution programs in China and over 60 other countries using these vaccines. The efficacy rate for some Chinese vaccines, like CoronaVac, has been reported to be just over 50 percent, in contrast to Moderna and Pfizer-BioNTech which show around 90 percent effectiveness.

title: CVS Health Live: The race to vaccinate
summary: This article discusses a "CVS Health Live" episode focusing on the national COVID-19 vaccine distribution effort. The moderated discussion features CVS Health President and CEO Karen S. Lynch and Pfizer CEO Albert Bourla, who address the progress, challenges, and opportunities in vaccinating America, including the drive for vaccine equity.

title: Takeda’s Phase III mobocertinib study in 1L NSCLC on enrolment pause
summary: Takeda Pharmaceuticals has put its Phase III trial for mobocertinib in first-line EGFR exon 20 mutation non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) on a recruitment hold for a futility analysis. This decision is likely due to updated efficacy data from Phase I/II trials, which showed a decreased overall response rate. Depending on the futility analysis results, Takeda may consider new strategies like combination therapy or patient enrichment for mobocertinib, which has an anticipated peak revenue potential of $300m–$600m in first and second-line settings.

title: \_Celcuity Licensing Deal with Pfizer Drives Stock Up 85% in One Week
summary: Celcuity's stock surged 85% in one week following its announcement of an exclusive worldwide licensing deal with Pfizer Inc. to develop and commercialize gedatolisib for advanced breast cancer. The Plymouth-based biotechnology company paid an upfront fee of $10 million ($5M cash, $5M stock) and Pfizer is eligible for up to $330 million in milestone payments and royalties. Despite a 2020 net loss and no product revenue yet, this deal highlights Celcuity's CELsignia platform and has boosted its year-to-date stock performance to 190%.

title: New JAK Inhibitor, Rinvoq, Shows Promise for Treating Psoriatic Arthritis
summary: A phase 3 clinical trial indicates that upadacitinib (Rinvoq), a new JAK inhibitor, is a promising treatment option for psoriatic arthritis (PsA) patients, showing significant improvement across various symptoms including joint pain, skin clearance, and fatigue. While Rinvoq is already FDA-approved for rheumatoid arthritis, its application for PsA is under review, with the FDA taking extra time to evaluate the drug class due to general concerns about JAK inhibitors, which carry black box warnings for risks like cancer and blood clots. Despite these concerns, medical advisors suggest that JAK inhibitors could still be a viable option for certain PsA patients.

title: Israel to buy millions of Pfizer COVID-19 vaccine doses
summary: Israel has signed a significant deal to acquire millions of Pfizer COVID-19 vaccine doses through 2022, announced Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. These new vaccines are designed to combat various coronavirus variants, and Netanyahu expressed his intention to secure a similar agreement with Moderna Inc. The move aims to ensure a plentiful supply of vaccines for both adults and children, building on Israel's already high vaccination rates.

title: Thailand negotiating to buy 5-10 mln doses of Pfizer vaccine - PM
summary: Thailand's Prime Minister announced on Tuesday that the country is in negotiations to acquire five to ten million doses of the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine. These doses are anticipated to be delivered between July and the end of 2021. The agreement would be a significant step in Thailand's vaccination efforts.

title: Johnson & Johnson reports $100 million in quarterly sales from Covid vaccine
summary: Johnson & Johnson reported $100 million in first-quarter sales from its Covid-19 vaccine, even as its use was paused in the U.S. due to a rare blood-clotting issue. The company's pharmaceutical business saw a 9.6% increase in revenue, contributing to overall earnings and revenue that exceeded Wall Street expectations. J&J also raised its full-year profit and revenue guidance, while actively working to restore confidence in its vaccine following safety concerns.

title: J&J to resume rollout of COVID-19 vaccine in Europe with safety warning
summary: Johnson & Johnson announced it will resume the rollout of its COVID-19 vaccine in Europe after the European Medicines Agency (EMA) concluded that the benefits outweigh the rare risk of blood clots. The vaccine's product label will be updated to include a warning about these rare blood clots, and J&J aims to restore confidence in its product. This decision follows a temporary halt in the U.S. and Europe due to blood clot reports, and manufacturing issues at a Baltimore plant for J&J are still being addressed.

title: Brazil in talks to buy 100 mln more Pfizer/BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine doses
summary: Brazil is negotiating to purchase an additional 100 million doses of Pfizer/BioNTech's COVID-19 vaccine, as announced by Communications Minister Fabio Faria. This move aims to accelerate the country's vaccination program, which has faced criticism for its slow start amidst Brazil being a global epicenter of the pandemic. The new doses, if acquired, would ensure supplies for 2022, building on an existing deal for 100 million doses.

title: Pfizer identifies fake COVID-19 shots abroad as criminals exploit vaccine demand
summary: Pfizer has confirmed the discovery of counterfeit COVID-19 vaccine versions in Mexico and Poland, highlighting criminal exploitation of the global vaccination campaign. In Mexico, about 80 people received fraudulent doses disguised in fraudulent packaging, while in Poland, seized vials likely contained an anti-wrinkle treatment. This comes as law enforcement and drugmakers work to combat a surge in criminal activity related to vaccine demand.

title: IDEA Pharma's 10th annual Pharmaceutical Innovation Index: Eli Lilly is the most innovative company for the first time
summary: Eli Lilly has topped IDEA Pharma's 10th annual Pharmaceutical Innovation Index for the first time, recognized for its ability to deliver innovation to patients through clinical data wins, novel FDA approvals, and strong performance of recently-launched drugs. The index evaluates companies based on their "return on invention" over a five-year period (2015-2020). Separately, Bristol-Myers Squibb leads the Pharmaceutical Invention Index, which ranks companies based on the novelty and meaningful development of their pipelines, partly due to its Celgene acquisition.

title: WHO sets dates for reviews of Sinopharm and Sinovac COVID-19 vaccines
summary: The World Health Organization (WHO) has scheduled reviews for COVID-19 vaccines from Chinese manufacturers Sinopharm and Sinovac for potential emergency use listing. Sinopharm's vaccine will be reviewed on April 26, followed by Sinovac's on May 3, with decisions expected a few days after each review. This move could endorse the vaccines' safety and efficacy, guiding regulatory agencies in various countries.

title: CVS Health names Kathryn Metcalfe Chief Communications Officer
summary: CVS Health announced Kathryn Metcalfe has joined the company as Senior Vice President and Chief Communications Officer, responsible for all internal, external, crisis, and reputation communications. Metcalfe brings extensive experience from previous roles at Aetna, Bristol-Myers Squibb, Deloitte, Pfizer, and Novartis, and rejoins CVS Health after leading communications for the integration between CVS Health and Aetna. She expressed excitement about transforming the healthcare system and highlighted CVS Health's significant role in the pandemic response.

title: FDA grants accelerated approval for GSK’s JEMPERLI (dostarlimab-gxly) for women with recurrent or advanced dMMR endometrial cancer
summary: The FDA has granted accelerated approval to GSK's JEMPERLI (dostarlimab-gxly) for adult patients with recurrent or advanced mismatch repair-deficient (dMMR) endometrial cancer that has progressed after platinum-containing treatment. This approval is based on results from the GARNET study, showing an overall response rate of 42.3%, with 93% of responders maintaining the response for at least six months. JEMPERLI offers a new treatment option for this underserved patient population, particularly given the high rate of dMMR in endometrial cancer and its association with increased recurrence.

title: FDA Approves Loncastuximab Tesirine for Relapsed/Refractory Large B-Cell Lymphoma
summary: The FDA has granted accelerated approval to loncastuximab tesirine (Zynlonta) for adults with relapsed/refractory large B-cell lymphoma after two or more lines of systemic therapy. This approval is based on the LOTIS-2 study, where the drug achieved a 48.3% objective response rate, including a 24.1% complete response rate, demonstrating significant clinical outcomes across various disease subtypes. Loncastuximab tesirine is also being investigated in combination with other treatments for similar lymphoma types.

title: Ovid Stops Development and Testing of OV101 for Fragile X
summary: Ovid Therapeutics has announced it is discontinuing the development and testing of OV101 (gaboxadol) for fragile X syndrome due to insufficient overall efficacy, despite being safe and well-tolerated in clinical trials. The company will now focus on its early-stage pipeline, including OV882 for Angelman syndrome. This decision follows combined efficacy results that failed to meet expectations for OV101 in both fragile X and Angelman syndromes.

title: S.Korea signs with Pfizer for additional 40 mln COVID-19 vaccine doses
summary: South Korea has signed a deal with Pfizer for an additional 40 million doses of its COVID-19 vaccine, bringing the total Pfizer doses to 66 million and the overall secured vaccines to 192 million. This procurement aims to vaccinate roughly 100 million people, double the nation's population, with a goal to vaccinate 12 million by June and achieve herd immunity by November. The agreement comes as South Korea faces spiking infections and a relatively low vaccination rate of just over 4%.

title: What you need to know about the Johnson & Johnson vaccine
summary: U.S. health officials have lifted the pause on the Johnson & Johnson COVID-19 vaccine after determining its benefits outweigh the risks, despite a rare blood clot side effect in a small number of recipients. This single-dose vaccine uses an inactivated adenovirus to deliver DNA instructions for the spike protein, making it easier to store and distribute compared to the two-dose mRNA vaccines from Pfizer and Moderna. While slightly less effective at preventing symptomatic illness than the mRNA vaccines, it is 100% effective against death and highly effective against severe illness, and its single-dose nature makes it valuable for hard-to-reach populations.

title: The Lessons of the Johnson & Johnson Vaccine Saga
summary: The article discusses the FDA and CDC's decision to lift the pause on the Johnson & Johnson COVID-19 vaccine, emphasizing the importance of transparency in public health communication. It highlights the rare blood clot risk, particularly for women under fifty, and stresses the need to provide clear information while reaffirming the vaccine's overall benefits. The author argues that acknowledging and addressing such risks, rather than ignoring them, builds public trust in vaccines.

title: Millions Are Skipping Their Second Doses of Covid Vaccines (Published 2021)
summary: Millions of Americans are missing their second doses of Pfizer or Moderna Covid-19 vaccines, with nearly 8% of those who received a first shot not completing their vaccination. This trend, double the initial rate, poses a challenge for health authorities aiming to ensure full vaccination despite vaccine hesitancy. Reasons for missed doses include concerns about side effects and perceptions of adequate protection from a single shot, as well as logistical issues like provider supply shortages or incorrect vaccine brands.

title: Procter & Gamble Is One of the 2021 TIME100 Most Influential Companies | TIME
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) was recognized as one of the 2021 TIME100 Most Influential Companies due to its significant performance during the pandemic. The company saw a banner year with $71 billion in sales, a 6% increase, driven by high demand for its household products like Charmin and Tide. Additionally, P&G repurposed its manufacturing capabilities to produce hundreds of thousands of face shields for healthcare workers.

title: Vertex moves pain drug into mid-stage testing
summary: Vertex Pharmaceuticals is advancing its experimental pain drug, VX-548, into mid-stage clinical trials after initial studies demonstrated its safety and intended effect. VX-548 aims to block the NaV1.8 sodium channel to provide non-addictive pain relief, addressing the significant demand for alternatives to opioids. This move is part of Vertex's broader strategy to diversify its drug pipeline beyond cystic fibrosis, despite some investor and analyst skepticism regarding its diversification efforts.

title: What women should know about the Johnson & Johnson coronavirus vaccine
summary: The CDC and FDA lifted the pause on the Johnson & Johnson Covid-19 vaccine after a review of rare blood clotting cases, primarily affecting women younger than 50. Dr. Leana Wen discusses the specific risks of TTS (thrombosis with thrombocytopenia syndrome) associated with the J&J vaccine, differentiating it from common blood clots, and advises women under 50 to consider mRNA vaccines (Pfizer-BioNTech and Moderna) as first-line alternatives due to their lack of this rare risk. The article emphasizes informed decision-making based on individual circumstances, benefits, risks, and available alternatives.

title: Moderna expanding near Norwood manufacturing campus
summary: Moderna Inc. is expanding its manufacturing operations in Norwood, Massachusetts, by leasing a 236,566-square-foot office space that Alexandria Real Estate Equities acquired for $105 million. This expansion is part of Moderna's strategy to rapidly scale up production of its COVID-19 vaccine, with the new facility located near its existing manufacturing campus.

title: Pfizer puts 340-acre Collegeville campus up for sale
summary: Pfizer has put its 340-acre Collegeville campus, which includes 1.89 million square feet of office and lab space, up for sale. Pfizer occupies half of the space, while Dow Chemical Co. leases the remainder. The sale was reported by Natalie Kostelni of the Philadelphia Business Journal.

title: FDA Authorizes Pfizer-BioNTech Covid-19 Vaccine for 12- to 15-Year-Olds
summary: The FDA has authorized the Pfizer-BioNTech Covid-19 vaccine for use in children aged 12 to 15, marking the first time a Covid-19 vaccine has been approved for this age group in the U.S. This decision follows a study showing the vaccine's safety and efficacy in adolescents and aims to expand the vaccination campaign ahead of summer camps and the next school year, potentially allowing for the easing of pandemic restrictions. The move is expected to help immunize more people against dangerous variants.

title: Who Owns CRISPR in 2021? It’s Even More Complicated Than You Think
summary: The ownership of CRISPR technology, particularly CRISPR-Cas9, is a complex and evolving landscape marked by ongoing legal battles and a proliferation of patents for various Cas molecules. While the initial patent dispute between UC Berkeley and the MIT-Harvard Broad Institute grabbed headlines, numerous other companies and institutions now hold intellectual property rights for different CRISPR variations and applications. The article explores the implications of this fragmented ownership, discussing potential scenarios for the future of CRISPR accessibility and innovation in medicine and agriculture.

title: Seresto Flea Collar Class Action Lawsuit Claims EPA Turning Blind Eye To Pet Deaths
summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Elanco Animal Health Incorporated and Bayer Healthcare LLC over Seresto flea and tick collars. The plaintiff alleges that the collars, which release pesticides, caused her dog's death and have been linked to thousands of adverse reactions and pet deaths, claiming the EPA has ignored the problem. The lawsuit seeks damages for other pet owners and highlights a congressional probe into Elanco's sales practices.

title: Antibody cocktail shown to neutralise SARS-CoV-2 variants of concern
summary: A new antibody cocktail called IMM-BCP-01, developed by Immunome, Inc., has demonstrated the ability to neutralise several SARS-CoV-2 variants, including those from the UK, Brazil, South Africa, and California, in pre-clinical studies. This cocktail contains three monoclonal antibodies that bind to non-overlapping regions of the SARS-CoV-2 Spike protein with high affinity and exhibit combinatorial effects against multiple variants. The company plans to advance IMM-BCP-01 towards an Investigational New Drug (IND) filing, emphasizing the importance of antibodies targeting conserved epitopes to address mutational drift.

title: Wilson Sonsini Advises Amplyx on IP Matters Related to Acquisition by Pfizer
summary: Wilson Sonsini Goodrich & Rosati advised Amplyx Pharmaceuticals, Inc. on intellectual property matters related to its acquisition by Pfizer Inc. Pfizer had previously made an equity investment in Amplyx in December 2019. Amplyx is a company dedicated to developing therapies for debilitating and life-threatening diseases in immunocompromised individuals, with its lead compound, Fosmanogepix, for invasive fungal infections.

title: Eczema treatment and vaccines lift Sanofi first quarter results
summary: Sanofi reported stronger-than-expected first-quarter results, driven by robust sales of its eczema treatment and high demand for flu and polio vaccines. Despite a dip in cough and cold treatment revenue due to lockdowns, the French drugmaker maintained its 2021 targets and anticipates Phase II results for its Covid-19 vaccine candidate in May. The company's net income increased by 14.7% to 2.017 billion euros, with overall revenue rising 2.4% to 8.6 billion euros.

title: Pfizer Ventures' Barbara Dalton Appointed as AMRA Medical's Newest Board Member
summary: AMRA Medical announced the appointment of Barbara J. Dalton, Ph.D., Senior Managing Partner at Pfizer Ventures and Vice President, Worldwide Business Development at Pfizer Inc., to its Board of Directors. Dr. Dalton brings extensive experience in pharmaceutical venture capital, having led Pfizer Ventures to invest over $700 million in more than 90 portfolio companies. Her expertise is expected to guide AMRA's growth and accelerate its innovations in digital health and precision medicine.

title: Bristol Myers first-quarter earnings miss expectations as cancer drugs underperform
summary: Bristol Myers Squibb reported lower-than-expected first-quarter profits due to cancer drugs Revlimid and Opdivo underperforming Wall Street estimates, despite better-than-expected sales of the blood thinner Eliquis. The company still anticipates full-year earnings within its projected range, expecting growth in Eliquis and a recovery for Opdivo in the latter half of the year.

title: Coronavirus: This May Be Dark Horse Of Vaccine Race. It's More Variant-Proof
summary: Valneva SE, a French biotech company, is developing a COVID-19 vaccine based on an inactivated whole virus, a traditional approach that may offer better protection against variants compared to other vaccines. The company has a significant deal with the U.K. for its vaccine, which is currently in phase three trials. Valneva executives believe this vaccine could serve as an effective booster shot and are also working to bring other vaccines for Lyme disease and Chikungunya to market by 2025.

title: Alnylam Pharmaceuticals Inc (ALNY) Q1 2021 Earnings Call Transcript
summary: Alnylam Pharmaceuticals Inc. reported strong Q1 2021 earnings, highlighting significant growth in product revenues, particularly for ONPATTRO, and positive initial uptake for OXLUMO. The company provided updates on its pipeline, including the accelerated enrollment for the HELIOS-B study of vutrisiran and progress in its late-stage clinical programs. Executives discussed the impact of COVID-19 on certain products, reaffirmed financial guidance, and emphasized their commitment to value-based agreements and innovation.

title: Pfizer begins to export US-made COVID shots: Report
summary: Pfizer has begun exporting US-made COVID-19 vaccine doses, with the first shipment sent to Mexico. This marks the first time the drugmaker has delivered abroad from US facilities since a Trump-era restriction on dose exports expired in March. The move comes as the US faces growing pressure to share surplus vaccines with other countries in need, using extra capacity in its US facilities while fulfilling its domestic commitment.

title: BioNTech Hits Record as Vaccine Success Spurs on Biotechs
summary: BioNTech (BNTX) stock surged 10% to over $200 a share, setting a new record and continuing its rally from the previous week. This rise reflects renewed optimism in the biotech sector as economies reopen and vaccine efforts, including those from Pfizer and BioNTech, successfully administer millions of doses in the U.S.

title: Next Generation of Covid-19 Vaccines Could Be Pill or Spray - WSJ
summary: The next generation of Covid-19 vaccines is being developed in forms such as pills or nasal sprays, aiming for easier storage and transport compared to current injectable vaccines. These new vaccines, developed by government labs and companies like Sanofi SA, Altimmune Inc., and Gritstone Oncology Inc., also seek to provide longer-lasting immunity and better protection against new viral variants, potentially preventing future pandemics. The article mentions that as more adults receive current vaccines, a variety of side effects are emerging.

title: Roivant’s move to go public reveals just how much its drug strategy has changed
summary: Roivant Sciences is going public through a merger with SPAC Montes Archimedes Acquisition Corp., revealing a significant shift in its strategy from acquiring overlooked drugs to investing heavily in computational drug discovery and development technologies. The deal values the new company at an expected market capitalization of $7.3 billion and provides $611 million in new capital to support its transformed focus. Roivant's evolution includes forming tech subsidiaries like Lokavant and Datavant, and making strategic acquisitions like Silicon Therapeutics, emphasizing AI and machine learning in its drug pipeline.

title: Brazil looks to new Pfizer contract to speed up vaccinations
summary: Brazil is negotiating a second contract with Pfizer for an additional 100 million doses of its COVID-19 vaccine, with 35 million doses expected by October. This new agreement would double Brazil's Pfizer vaccine supply to 200 million doses for the year, aiming to alleviate vaccine shortages amidst the country's severe COVID-19 outbreak. The Health Minister criticized failures in intensive care units and the government's previous slow response to securing vaccines.

title: Hospira Issues A Voluntary Nationwide Recall for One Lot of 0.5% Bupivacaine Hydrochloride Injection, USP and One Lot of 1% Lidocaine HCl Injection, USP Due to Mislabeling
summary: Hospira, a Pfizer company, has voluntarily recalled one lot of 0.5% Bupivacaine Hydrochloride Injection, USP and one lot of 1% Lidocaine HCl Injection, USP nationwide due to mislabeling. A portion of each lot was incorrectly labeled as the other product, posing risks from underdosing or overdosing for patients. While no adverse events have been reported to date, the recall is being conducted with the knowledge of the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.

title: Pfizer Reaps Hundreds of Millions in Profits From Covid Vaccine (Published 2021)
summary: Pfizer announced that its Covid-19 vaccine generated $3.5 billion in revenue in the first quarter of 2021 and projected roughly $900 million in pretax profits for the period. While the company stated its intention to profit from the vaccine unlike some rivals, the distribution has disproportionately favored wealthy countries, with poor countries receiving only a fraction of the doses. This contrasts with Pfizer's CEO's pledge for equitable access.

title: Fighting MS through innovation
summary: This article discusses the critical need for innovation in treating multiple sclerosis (MS), particularly concerning timely diagnosis, early treatment, and the development of new therapies. It highlights the significant economic and social burden of MS on patients, families, and society, using a French study that calculated a cost of EUR 2.8 billion annually. The piece emphasizes that investing in innovative treatments and technologies, such as the MS Copilot® app, can improve patient outcomes and significantly reduce the burden of the disease.

title: Hospira Issues A Voluntary Nationwide Recall for One Lot of Sterile Water for Injection, USP, Due to the Potential Presence of Visible Particulate
summary: Hospira, a Pfizer company, is voluntarily recalling lot DN9185 of Sterile Water for Injection, USP, 100 mL Single Dose Glass Fliptop Vial, due to a confirmed report of a visible particulate. The recall is being conducted to the hospital/institution level, as the presence of particulate matter could lead to serious adverse events such as anaphylaxis, vein inflammation, or pulmonary emboli. Hospira has notified affected wholesalers, distributors, and hospitals and has provided contact information for further assistance and reporting adverse events.

title: S.Korea says AstraZeneca, Pfizer COVID-19 vaccines 87% effective after first shot
summary: South Korea's real-world data indicates that one dose of AstraZeneca or Pfizer's COVID-19 vaccines is 86.6% effective in preventing infections among people aged 60 and older. The Pfizer vaccine showed 89.7% effectiveness, while AstraZeneca's was 86.0% effective. These findings aim to boost vaccination participation, with South Korea setting a target of vaccinating 70% of its population by September to achieve herd immunity by November.

title: Peru signs deal to purchase 12 million additional doses of Pfizer vaccine
summary: Peru has signed a new agreement with Pfizer Inc and BioNTech SE to acquire an additional 12 million doses of their COVID-19 vaccine, with delivery expected by the end of the year. This deal comes as Peru grapples with a severe second wave of the virus and aims to accelerate its vaccination efforts, which have been slow, with less than 4% of the population inoculated. Previously, Peru had already contracted with Pfizer for 20 million doses.

title: Moderna Dominates COVID-19 Vaccine Manufacturers, at Least for Now
summary: The COVID-19 vaccine market is dominated by mRNA firms like Moderna and BioNTech in the short term, despite emerging competitors and uncertainties about long-term dominance. The article explores the market's future, considering factors like vaccine efficacy duration, variant evolution, pricing, and the potential for annual vaccinations, especially for high-risk groups. It also touches upon Moderna's strong intellectual property and its future in the non-COVID-19 vaccine market.

title: Eikon Therapeutics Closes $148 Million Series A Financing to Develop High-Throughput, Super-Resolution Microscopy for Drug Discovery
summary: Eikon Therapeutics announced it has closed a $148 million Series A financing round to advance its drug discovery platform, which is based on live-cell super-resolution microscopy. The company also appointed Roger M. Perlmutter, MD, PhD, former President of Merck Research Laboratories, as its new CEO. Eikon aims to industrialize this Nobel Prize-winning technology to track protein dynamics and discover new therapies.

title: A New Wave of Vaccines Is Coming, and They’re Not All Also-Rans
summary: Despite the initial success of established vaccine makers like Pfizer and Moderna, a new wave of companies is developing Covid-19 vaccines, driven by the need for cheaper, easier-to-ship alternatives and shots targeting new variants. The World Health Organization believes there's still room for improvement in vaccine technology. This ongoing development suggests the global pandemic's challenges are extensive enough to support additional players in the vaccine market.

title: Pfizer and BioNTech requested the F.D.A.’s authorization to use their vaccine in 12- to 15-year-olds. (Published 2021)
summary: Pfizer and BioNTech have requested that the FDA broaden the emergency use authorization for their COVID-19 vaccine to include adolescents aged 12 to 15. This expansion could allow young teens to be vaccinated before the upcoming school year. Clinical trials showed the vaccine to be highly effective in this age group, with no symptomatic infections or serious side effects reported.

title: Moderna sees no impact on COVID-19 vaccine from potential patent waiver
summary: Moderna believes a waiver of COVID-19 vaccine patents would not significantly impact its sales, as rivals would face substantial manufacturing hurdles. The company's CEO, Stephane Bancel, highlighted the difficulty in rapidly scaling up complex vaccine production, expecting countries to continue purchasing Moderna's vaccine for years. Despite the patent waiver news, Moderna raised its 2021 sales forecast for its COVID-19 shot to $19.2 billion and anticipates producing up to 1 billion doses this year, potentially increasing to 3 billion by 2022.

title: Pfizer and Organon Provide a Glimpse of Biosimilars Strategy
summary: Pfizer reported a 45% increase in first-quarter 2021 revenues, with biosimilar sales up 79%, driven by several recent launches. The company reiterated its commitment to combating rebates and working with legislators to ensure patient savings. Organon, Merck's planned biosimilars and women's health products spinoff, revealed its strategy to launch several biosimilars, including Hadlima in the U.S. in 2023, and aims to introduce 1 to 2 new biosimilars annually through partnerships.

title: How the Johnson & Johnson Vaccine Works (Published 2022)
summary: The article details how the Johnson & Johnson COVID-19 vaccine, also known as JNJ-78436735 or Ad26.COV2.S, functions. It explains that the vaccine uses a modified adenovirus to deliver DNA instructions for building the coronavirus's spike protein, which then prompts the immune system to produce antibodies and T cells. The article also covers the vaccine's development timeline, efficacy rates, and logistical advantages related to storage.

title: Covid hospitalisation spike in the US a trigger for future mRNA deployment
summary: Experts agree that the deployment of Covid-19 mRNA vaccine boosters by Moderna and Pfizer/BioNTech will be triggered by multiple factors, not just waning immunity. A clear sign for booster deployment would be an increase in hospitalizations among fully vaccinated individuals, though some specialists suggest earlier use for milder disease cases to prevent societal disruption and new variants. However, prematurely deploying boosters poses risks, including diverting limited global supply from unvaccinated populations and hindering the collection of real-world durability data for the initial vaccine doses.

title: First Tranche of U.S. Pfizer-BioNTech Vaccines Delivered to the Philippines
summary: The first shipment of 193,050 doses of the U.S. Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine arrived in the Philippines on May 10, 2021. This delivery, part of the COVAX initiative, follows an earlier AstraZeneca vaccine shipment, bringing the total COVAX deliveries to the Philippines to 2,673,000 doses. The United States is the largest contributor to COVAX, having funded $2 billion and committed an additional $2 billion to ensure global access to COVID-19 vaccines.

title: Latest AAFP Immunization Materials Keep FPs Up to Date
summary: The American Academy of Family Physicians (AAFP) is distributing updated immunization resources to its members, including the 2021 adult, childhood/adolescent, and catch-up schedules from the CDC's Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP). These materials are vital for family physicians to stay current on vaccine recommendations, communicate with patients about immunizations, and address vaccine hesitancy. The article highlights key changes to the immunization schedules and provides an overview of the COVID-19 vaccines available, emphasizing the crucial role of family physicians in promoting vaccination.

title: Insulin Product Samples Recalled Due to Improper Storage Temperature Conditions
summary: Novo Nordisk is voluntarily recalling 1,468 product samples of several insulin products, including Levemir, Tresiba, Fiasp, Novolog, and Xultophy, because they were stored below required temperatures. This recall only impacts product samples and not those available in pharmacies. Improper storage could lead to a lack of efficacy and device damage, potentially causing hypoglycemia or hyperglycemia in patients.

title: Unused shots pile up as mistrust blights Hong Kong vaccine drive
summary: Hong Kong is experiencing a significant challenge with its COVID-19 vaccination program, as low uptake leads to an abundance of unused doses despite free and widely available shots. This reluctance is primarily due to deep-seated mistrust between the government and its citizens, stemming from past political unrest and a perception that the virus does not pose a major threat. The situation threatens Hong Kong's return to normalcy and its status as a business hub, with experts highlighting that political distrust outweighs public health concerns.

title: Johnson & Johnson vaccine linked to 28 cases of blood clots, CDC reports
summary: The CDC reported 28 cases of blood clots linked to the Johnson & Johnson Covid-19 vaccine among over 8.7 million people vaccinated. Most cases were thrombosis with thrombocytopenia syndrome (TTS) and occurred in women aged 18 to 49, with three fatalities. The CDC and FDA previously paused and then lifted the vaccine's use, advising against heparin for TTS treatment.

title: Federal Inspectors Fear More Vaccines Were Exposed to Contamination (Published 2021)
summary: Federal regulators have identified serious flaws at Emergent BioSolutions' Baltimore plant, casting doubt on the safety of Johnson & Johnson's coronavirus vaccine production. An FDA report suggests that up to 15 million discarded doses were not fully investigated for contamination and that other batches may also be compromised due to poor manufacturing practices, facility design, and worker training. This report further complicates matters for Johnson & Johnson, which has already faced production delays and a temporary halt in distribution due to blood-clotting concerns.

title: Pfizer Begins Testing Its Vaccine in Young Children (Published 2021)
summary: Pfizer has initiated trials for its COVID-19 vaccine in children under 12, with the first participants being 9-year-old twin girls at Duke University. Results are anticipated in the latter half of the year, with hopes to vaccinate younger children by early next year. Other pharmaceutical companies like Moderna, AstraZeneca, and Johnson & Johnson are also conducting or planning similar trials for pediatric populations to aid in achieving herd immunity and facilitating school reopenings.

title: FDA allows Pfizer’s COVID-19 vaccine to be used in adolescents
summary: The FDA has expanded the emergency use authorization (EUA) for the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine to include adolescents aged 12 through 15. This decision followed a rigorous review of safety and effectiveness data, showing the vaccine was 100% effective in preventing COVID-19 in this age group during trials, with side effects consistent with those reported in older individuals. The expansion aims to protect a younger population and move closer to ending the pandemic.

title: CVS, Walgreens administering Pfizer vaccine to kids 12-15 nationwide
summary: CVS and Walgreens have begun administering the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine to adolescents aged 12-15 nationwide, following the FDA's emergency use authorization. The pharmacies require parental consent and adult accompaniment for vaccinations. This move aims to protect a younger population from COVID-19 and help return to a sense of normalcy, with the FDA emphasizing a rigorous review process for the vaccine's safety and efficacy in this age group.

title: Pfizer got no response to offers to supply vaccine to Brazil last year, exec says
summary: A Pfizer executive told Brazilian lawmakers that the company repeatedly offered to sell its COVID-19 vaccine to Brazil’s Health Ministry between August and November 2020 but received no response. A Senate commission is investigating whether President Jair Bolsonaro's government mishandled the pandemic by not securing vaccines in time, which led to a high death toll. Brazil eventually signed a contract with Pfizer for 100 million doses in March 2021, and Pfizer is set to sign another contract for an additional 100 million doses for delivery in the fourth quarter.

title: Pfizer Inc. CFO to Address St. John’s University Graduates
summary: Frank D’Amelio '83MBA, CFO and Executive Vice President of Global Supply at Pfizer Inc., is scheduled to deliver the Commencement Address to the St. John’s University Class of 2021. D'Amelio, an alumnus, is recognized for his financial expertise and leadership in navigating global challenges, including Pfizer's role in the COVID-19 pandemic response. His career highlights include significant roles at AT&T, Lucent Technologies, and Alcatel-Lucent Enterprise before joining Pfizer.

title: Empaveli Approved for Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria
summary: The FDA has approved Empaveli (pegcetacoplan) for the treatment of adults with paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH). This approval is based on the PEGASUS study, which showed Empaveli's superiority to eculizumab in increasing hemoglobin levels. Empaveli is the first FDA-approved targeted C3 therapy, representing a new class of complement medicine.

title: BD to Build $200M PFS Mfg. Facility in Spain
summary: BD (Becton, Dickinson and Company) is investing $200 million to build a new high-tech manufacturing facility in Zaragoza, Spain, dedicated to producing pre-fillable syringes for vaccines and other biologics. This new plant is part of a larger $1.2 billion investment by BD to expand its manufacturing capacity and technology for pre-fillable syringes and advanced drug delivery systems. The facility, expected to create up to 600 jobs by 2030, will incorporate eco-efficiency standards and Industry 4.0 solutions, serving primarily the European market.

title: Chairs Maloney, Nadler, and Cicilline Ask FTC to Open Formal Inquiry into AbbVie
summary: Chairs Maloney, Nadler, and Cicilline have requested the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to formally investigate AbbVie Inc.'s alleged actions to delay U.S. biosimilar entry for its drug Humira. Documents obtained by the Committee on Oversight and Reform suggest that AbbVie delayed competition longer than internal evaluations warranted. The request comes as AbbVie charges significantly more for Humira in the U.S. than in Europe, where biosimilar competition has drastically reduced prices.

title: Pfizer Vaccine Can Stay Longer At Warmer Temperatures Before Being Discarded
summary: The FDA has authorized an extension for storing the undiluted Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine at standard refrigerator temperatures (2°C to 8°C or 35°F to 46°F) for up to one month. This significantly increases the previous limit of five days, making the vaccine easier to store, distribute, and administer, thereby increasing its accessibility for wider vaccination efforts. This change is expected to help accelerate the end of the pandemic.

title: Japan health panel approves Moderna, AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccines
summary: A health ministry panel in Japan recommended the approval of COVID-19 vaccines from Moderna Inc and AstraZeneca PLC, which is expected to be officially approved by the government as early as Friday. This move aims to accelerate Japan's vaccination campaign, which has been slow due to initial supply issues and logistical bottlenecks. Moderna doses are already imported for use in mass vaccination centers, while AstraZeneca's vaccine supply, mostly produced domestically, might have age restrictions due to blood clot concerns.

title: Japan panel gives Moderna and AstraZeneca vaccines the green light
summary: A health ministry panel in Japan has approved the emergency use of COVID-19 vaccines developed by AstraZeneca and Moderna. This move will significantly boost Japan's vaccination efforts, as the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine was previously the only one available in the country. The approval comes amidst a fourth wave of infections and Japan's race to catch up with other developed nations in inoculating its population.

title: Eli Lilly hires Greg Daniel as head of global public policy
summary: Eli Lilly has appointed Greg Daniel as its head of global public policy. In this role, Daniel will lead the company's federal and state policy efforts, focusing on addressing barriers to innovation, access, affordability, and global competition within the pharmaceutical industry. He joins Eli Lilly from Edwards Lifesciences and previously held positions at Duke-Margolis Center for Health Policy, Brookings Institution, and Healthcore, Inc.

title: The Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices’ Interim Recommendation for Use of Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine in Adolescents Aged 12–15 Years — United States, May 2021
summary: The Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP) issued an interim recommendation for the use of the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine in adolescents aged 12–15 years in May 2021, following the FDA's expanded Emergency Use Authorization. This decision was based on a systematic review of data showing high efficacy in preventing symptomatic COVID-19 and acceptable safety profiles with mostly mild-to-moderate reactogenicity. The recommendation emphasizes the importance of vaccinating adolescents to protect against the disease and reduce community transmission, noting that COVID-19 is a significant public health problem for this age group.

title: LianBio is Driving Innovation in China with Next-Gen CEO Yizhe Wang
summary: LianBio, founded by Perceptive Advisors in October 2019, is focused on bringing innovative medicines to China and other major Asian markets. The company recently appointed Yizhe Wang, Ph.D., formerly of Eli Lilly and GlaxoSmithKline, as its new CEO. Wang's experience in developing over 25 innovative medicines and his strategic leadership are expected to drive LianBio's mission and advance its portfolio of partnered assets.

title: Moderna vaccine safe and highly effective in kids ages 12 to 17, company says
summary: Moderna announced that its Covid-19 vaccine is safe and highly effective in children ages 12 to 17, with 100 percent efficacy against symptomatic Covid-19 in a Phase 2/3 clinical trial. This would provide a second vaccine option for this age group in the U.S., alongside the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine. The company plans to submit its findings to the Food and Drug Administration in early June.

title: Quest Diagnostics and Paige Form Collaboration to Advance AI-generated Pathology Insights to Improve Cancer Diagnosis and Care
summary: Quest Diagnostics and Paige have partnered to use artificial intelligence (AI) to improve and accelerate the diagnosis of cancer and other diseases. They will analyze pathology diagnostic data and digitized slides to identify cancer markers and develop new software products. These products, upon regulatory approval, will be marketed to healthcare providers and licensed to biopharmaceutical and research organizations.

title: Mexico ramping up COVID-19 trial work tapping Sanofi, China's shots in late-stage tests
summary: Mexico is accelerating its COVID-19 vaccine trial efforts, with Sanofi and China's Walvax Biotechnology set to begin Phase 3 trials in the country. Additionally, Mexico's own "Patria" vaccine is aiming for mid-stage trials and potential emergency use authorization this year. These steps are crucial for Mexico, which has a large population and has faced significant challenges in securing sufficient vaccine supplies.

title: Moderna Vaccine Highly Effective in Adolescents, Company Says (Published 2021)
summary: Moderna announced that its coronavirus vaccine is highly effective in 12- to 17-year-olds, with no symptomatic Covid-19 cases among fully vaccinated teens in a clinical trial. The company plans to seek FDA authorization in June, potentially making it the second vaccine available for U.S. adolescents. This development adds to evidence of vaccine safety and effectiveness in younger populations, potentially aiding societal reopening.

title: Coya Therapeutics™ Announces the Appointment of Anabella Villalobos, Ph.D. to its Board of Directors
summary: Coya Therapeutics, a clinical-stage biotechnology company, has appointed Dr. Anabella Villalobos, Head of Biotherapeutics and Medicinal Sciences at Biogen, to its Board of Directors. Dr. Villalobos brings extensive experience in neurologic drug discovery and medicinal chemistry from her roles at Biogen and Pfizer. Her expertise is expected to be invaluable as Coya Therapeutics advances its lead candidate, ALS001, and expands its research and development pipeline for neurodegenerative and autoimmune diseases.

title: Inovio’s Electrical Device Zaps a COVID-19 Vaccine Into the Body
summary: Inovio Pharmaceuticals is developing a DNA-based COVID-19 vaccine delivered using an electrical electroporation device, which may overcome the cold-chain storage and significant side effect issues of current mRNA vaccines. Although the device adds logistical complexity and has drawn skepticism, its ability to deliver a stable, room-temperature vaccine without strong side effects holds significant promise for global distribution, especially in remote regions or for military applications.
