The company is currently completing Phase 2 trials and addressing FDA questions regarding its Cellectra 3PSP device.

title: Myovant Sciences and Pfizer Receive FDA Approval for MYFEMBREE®, the First Once-Daily Treatment for Heavy Menstrual Bleeding Associated With Uterine Fibroids
summary: Myovant Sciences and Pfizer Inc. announced FDA approval for MYFEMBREE (relugolix 40 mg, estradiol 1 mg, and norethindrone acetate 0.5 mg), a first-of-its-kind once-daily treatment for heavy menstrual bleeding associated with uterine fibroids in premenopausal women, effective for up to 24 months. This approval is based on successful Phase 3 LIBERTY studies, showing significant reductions in menstrual blood loss. The companies will jointly commercialize MYFEMBREE in the U.S., with availability expected in June 2021, and Myovant will host a conference call on May 28, 2021, to discuss the approval.

title: FDA Approves Biohaven's NURTEC® ODT (rimegepant) for Prevention: Now the First and Only Migraine Medication for both Acute and Preventive Treatment
summary: The FDA has approved Biohaven's NURTEC ODT (rimegepant 75 mg) for the preventive treatment of migraine, making it the first oral CGRP antagonist approved for both acute and preventive migraine treatment. This expanded indication allows NURTEC ODT to be used for adult patients with episodic migraine, addressing approximately 95% of U.S. migraine sufferers. The approval is based on a Phase 3 trial showing significant reduction in migraine days, offering a new comprehensive treatment option.

title: Bristol Myers' multiple sclerosis drug Zeposia snags first-in-class nod to treat ulcerative colitis
summary: Bristol Myers Squibb's multiple sclerosis drug Zeposia has received FDA approval to treat moderate-to-severe active ulcerative colitis, marking its expansion into inflammatory bowel disease. This makes Zeposia the first S1P receptor modulator to be approved for UC, offering a pill option against prevalent injectable biologics. Despite a pricing gap between MS and UC drugs, BMS plans to maintain the same list price while potentially negotiating larger discounts for payers in the UC market.

title: The U.K. approves the use of the Johnson & Johnson vaccine. (Published 2021)
summary: Britain's drug regulator has approved the single-dose Johnson & Johnson coronavirus vaccine, making it the fourth vaccine authorized in the country. This approval comes amidst increasing concerns over the spread of a coronavirus variant first detected in India. The U.K. has vaccinated over 58% of its population with at least one dose.

title: Johnson & Johnson’s Vaccine Offers Strong Protection but Fuels Concern About Variants (Published 2021)
summary: Johnson & Johnson announced that its single-dose COVID-19 vaccine provides strong protection, making it the fifth company backed by the U.S. government to develop an effective vaccine. While offering a significant advantage due to its single-dose nature, its efficacy rate dropped notably in South Africa, where a highly contagious variant is prevalent, raising concerns about the vaccine's effectiveness against new mutations. Scientists still consider it a strong vaccine, comparable to annual flu shots in effectiveness, despite being less effective than Pfizer and Moderna's offerings.

title: UK approves Johnson & Johnson's single-dose Covid vaccine for use
summary: The U.K. has approved Johnson & Johnson's single-dose Covid-19 vaccine for use, making it the fourth vaccine authorized in the country. The government has secured 20 million doses, with initial availability expected later this year. This approval is set to boost the U.K.'s vaccination program, particularly given the vaccine's single-dose nature and easier storage requirements.

title: Early Covid-19 Treatment With SARS-CoV-2 Neutralizing Antibody Sotrovimab
summary: This study presents findings from a preplanned interim analysis of the COMET-ICE trial, investigating the efficacy and safety of sotrovimab for early treatment of Covid-19 in high-risk, non-hospitalized patients. The results indicate an 85% reduction in the risk of hospitalization or death for patients receiving sotrovimab compared to placebo, demonstrating profound efficacy. The treatment was also well-tolerated, with no significant safety concerns identified.

title: Japan to consider sharing COVID-19 vaccines amid calls to help Taiwan
summary: Japan is considering sharing its surplus COVID-19 vaccines with other countries, particularly Taiwan, which is experiencing a surge in domestic infections and has a low vaccination rate. This comes after a ruling party panel urged Japan to provide some of its AstraZeneca vaccine stock to Taiwan, noting Taiwan's past assistance to Japan. Japan has secured double the vaccine doses needed for its adult population, and a significant portion of its AstraZeneca stock is nearing expiration.

title: U.S. giant takes aim at Vancouver’s Precision NanoSystems with latest acquisition deal
summary: U.S. innovation giant Danaher Corp. has acquired Vancouver-based Precision NanoSystems Inc. (PNI), a company specializing in technology for developing and manufacturing genetic medicines. This acquisition is expected to significantly accelerate PNI's goals, including the development of a COVID-19 vaccine and the construction of a $50-million biomanufacturing facility in Metro Vancouver, with PNI's co-founder and CEO continuing to lead the company as a subsidiary. The deal highlights a period of significant growth and investment in British Columbia's life sciences sector.

title: With new CEO, Veracyte outlines €260M deal for French test maker HalioDx and global cancer testing expansion
summary: Veracyte announced a €260 million deal to acquire French test maker HalioDx, aiming to expand its global footprint in cancer diagnostics and enter immuno-oncology testing and in vitro diagnostic kit manufacturing. This acquisition, Veracyte's second this year, also broadens its testing menu to include HalioDx's colon cancer immune response test and Immunoscore platform. The deal coincides with the first day of Veracyte's new CEO, Marc Stapley, and follows its $600 million acquisition of Decipher Biosciences for urological cancers.

title: Israel sees probable link between Pfizer vaccine and myocarditis cases
summary: Israel's Health Ministry reported a probable link between Pfizer's COVID-19 vaccine and cases of myocarditis, primarily in young men, observed between December 2020 and May 2021. Of 275 reported cases among over 5 million vaccinated people, 95% were mild and resolved quickly. Despite Pfizer stating no causal link was established, an Israeli committee approved vaccinating 12-to-15-year-olds, emphasizing that the vaccine's efficacy outweighs potential risks.

title: Around the house: new legal leaders for Hershey and Knock
summary: This article details recent senior in-house legal appointments at several prominent companies. James Turoff has been promoted to SVP, General Counsel, and Secretary at Hershey, while Jennifer Miller joins Knock as its first Chief Legal Officer. Additionally, James Waters is the new General Counsel and Corporate Secretary for KeyCorp, Diane Peters takes on the GC role at Kickstarter, Inderpal Singh joins Immunic as General Counsel, Julie Gremillion becomes General Counsel at GoExpedi, and Isabel Giancristofano is named Director of Legal and Compliance for Condor, among other changes.

title: Pfizer Flight Dept Helped Get Vaccine to Market Sooner, Exec Says
summary: The head of Pfizer's corporate flight department highlighted the crucial role their operation played in accelerating the Covid-19 vaccine's market entry. The department's efficiency contributed significantly to the timely distribution of the vaccine. This showcases the often-unseen but vital support functions within large corporations during critical global events.

title: Association of the transthyretin variant V122I with polyneuropathy among individuals of African ancestry
summary: This study investigated the association between the transthyretin variant V122I and polyneuropathy in individuals of African ancestry using three large biobanks. It found a significant association between V122I and polyneuropathy diagnosis, suggesting that V122I carriers, historically linked to cardiomyopathy, are also at increased risk for polyneuropathy. The research highlights the underdiagnosis of hereditary transthyretin-mediated (hATTR) amyloidosis in V122I carriers and emphasizes the need for earlier identification and comprehensive understanding of multisystem manifestations for timely treatment.

title: Hubs established in Qatar and Rwanda for final vaccination opportunity for Olympic and Paralympic Games participants
summary: The IOC, with support from Pfizer and the National Olympic Committees of Qatar and Rwanda, has created two vaccination hubs in Doha and Kigali. These hubs offer the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine to Olympic and Paralympic Games participants who cannot be vaccinated in their home countries before traveling to Tokyo 2020. This initiative aims to ensure the safety of the Games for both participants and the Japanese people, with an expected vaccination rate well over 80% for Olympic Village residents.

title: U.K. Authorizes Pfizer Covid Vaccine for Use in Adolescents
summary: The U.K. drugs regulator has authorized the Pfizer-BioNTech Covid-19 vaccine for use in adolescents aged 12 to 15, following similar approvals in the U.S. and European Union. This decision comes as various countries aim to inoculate younger populations to combat the pandemic, with the agency confirming a positive safety profile for the vaccine in this age group.

title: Taiwan's COVID-19 vaccine stocks more than doubled by Japan donation
summary: Japan has donated 1.24 million doses of AstraZeneca's COVID-19 vaccine to Taiwan, effectively doubling the island nation's vaccine supply. This donation comes as Taiwan battles a surge in domestic infections and has only vaccinated about 3% of its population. The gesture reinforces the friendship between Japan and Taiwan, while Taiwan continues to face challenges in vaccine acquisition, partly due to alleged obstruction from China.

title: FDA Accepts Application for Lupin Limited’s Pegfilgrastim Biosimilar
summary: The FDA has accepted Lupin Limited's biologics license application (BLA) for a proposed biosimilar to pegfilgrastim (Neulasta), a drug used to decrease infection incidence in cancer patients receiving myelosuppressive anticancer agents. This acceptance is supported by comprehensive similarity data from analytical, pharmacokinetic, pharmacodynamic, and immunogenicity studies. Lupin Limited views this as a significant step to expand its oncology portfolio and provide more affordable biologic options to patients.

title: A New Type Of COVID-19 Vaccine Could Debut Soon
summary: Two new types of COVID-19 vaccines from Novavax and Medicago, based on protein subunit technology, are expected to debut soon. These vaccines differ from current mRNA and viral vector vaccines by directly introducing the spike protein or using plants to produce virus-like particles, offering an alternative for vaccination. Sanofi is also developing a protein subunit vaccine after correcting an initial dosing error in early trials.

title: Teva Vascepa ANDA Is ‘Discontinued’ Despite Settlement Agreement
summary: Teva's ANDA for Vascepa has been discontinued, despite a previous settlement agreement, according to Amarin's CEO. This development follows a court ruling that had seemingly opened the door for Teva's generic version. The article details Teva's situation regarding the generic cardiovascular drug.

title: Indy Company Manufacture Pfizer COVID Vaccine
summary: Indianapolis-based Exelead Inc. has delivered its first batch of the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine manufactured at its Indy facility. Through an agreement with Pfizer Inc., Exelead plans to add up to 50 jobs and has dedicated a portion of its expanded manufacturing capacity to support vaccine production. This partnership aims to leverage Exelead's expertise in complex drug manufacturing to increase the availability of vaccine doses.

title: Merck signs $1.2 billion deal with US government for experimental COVID treatment
summary: The U.S. government has agreed to purchase $1.2 billion worth of Merck's experimental COVID-19 treatment, Molnupiravir, if it receives regulatory approval. This deal would cover 1.7 million courses of treatment for the mild-to-moderate drug, which is currently in Phase 3 clinical trials. Merck anticipates seeking emergency use authorization in the latter half of 2021 and expects to have enough supply to treat 10 million people by year-end.

title: Why big pharma had a responsibility to profit from the pandemic
summary: The article argues that pharmaceutical companies like Pfizer and Moderna had a responsibility to profit from the COVID-19 pandemic, not just to shareholders but to society. It explains that corporate law, particularly in common law countries and the US, supports the idea that corporations have responsibilities beyond pure profit maximization, encompassing employees, communities, and the wider society. By developing vaccines and profiting from them, these companies acted in accordance with their legal and social responsibilities, acknowledging the societal benefit alongside business risks and financial gains.

title: Pfizer to begin COVID vaccine testing in larger group of children under age 12
summary: Pfizer announced it will expand testing of its COVID-19 vaccine to a larger group of children under 12, after selecting lower doses for this age group. The study will involve up to 4,500 children across several countries, with data for 5-11 year olds expected in September for potential emergency use authorization. Data for younger age groups (6 months to 5 years) is anticipated later in the year.

title: Paraguay publishes names of the vaccinated to stop COVID cheaters
summary: Paraguay, grappling with a high COVID-19 death rate and widespread corruption, is publicly listing the names, vaccination sites, vaccine types, and doses of all vaccinated individuals to combat vaccine queue-jumping. This measure, though unusual in its lack of privacy, aims to increase transparency and public trust in the vaccination process, especially as the country has limited vaccine supplies. The initiative has already led to the discovery and resignation of a senator who was vaccinated out of turn.

title: Canada releases redacted versions of COVID-19 vaccine contracts
summary: The Canadian federal government has released heavily redacted versions of its COVID-19 vaccine contracts, preventing the public from seeing key details like prices per dose and delivery schedules. This move comes after months of demands from opposition parties for transparency. Experts criticize the extensive redactions, stating it makes it impossible to assess the competitiveness of Canada's negotiated prices or the strength of delivery guarantees, especially given earlier delays in the vaccination campaign.

title: Paul Reid Named Managing Director at Pfizer Healthcare Ireland
summary: Paul Reid has been appointed as the new Managing Director of Pfizer Healthcare Ireland, bringing 18 years of pharmaceutical experience, 12 of which were with Pfizer Inc. In his new role, Reid will oversee the commercialization of medicines across various therapeutic areas. He emphasized the importance of ensuring patient access to innovative medicines and highlighted Pfizer's current global launch of five new medicines, including three in cancer.

title: G7′s billion vaccine plan counts some past pledges, limiting impact
summary: The G7's pledge to donate one billion COVID-19 vaccine doses to poorer countries is expected to have a limited impact due to the inclusion of existing commitments and the vast shortfall in the required doses. While the plan offers a much-needed boost to COVAX, the global vaccine buying system, it faces challenges in distribution and doesn't fully address the 5-6 billion doses needed. Experts highlight that many pledged doses are not new resources, and issues like limited distribution infrastructure in developing countries persist.

title: GSK and iTeos Therapeutics announce development and commercialisation collaboration for EOS-448, an anti-TIGIT monoclonal antibody, enabling novel next-generation immuno-oncology combinations
summary: GSK and iTeos Therapeutics have announced a collaboration to co-develop and co-commercialize EOS-448, an anti-TIGIT monoclonal antibody for cancer treatment. This partnership strategically positions GSK with a comprehensive portfolio targeting the CD226 axis for next-generation immuno-oncology therapies. iTeos will receive an upfront payment of $625 million, with potential for an additional $1.45 billion in milestone payments, and the companies will share profits in the US while GSK will have exclusive commercialization rights outside the US.

title: Novavax Offers U.S. a Fourth Strong Covid-19 Vaccine (Published 2021)
summary: Novavax announced strong results from its Covid-19 vaccine trial in the U.S. and Mexico, showing 90.4% overall efficacy and 100% against moderate or severe disease, similar to Pfizer-BioNTech and Moderna. Despite impressive data, the vaccine's U.S. future is uncertain due to existing supplies and potential delays in FDA authorization, while the company seeks approval in other countries first. Its protein-based technology may be valuable for future booster shots against waning immunity and emerging variants.

title: FDA Approves Novo Nordisk’s Obesity Drug Wegovy
summary: The FDA has approved Novo Nordisk's Wegovy for chronic weight management in overweight adults with at least one weight-related condition. Additionally, the FDA approved ProMetic Biotherapeutics' Ryplazim for plasminogen deficiency type 1 and Chimerix Inc's Tembexa to treat smallpox. These approvals address unmet medical needs in obesity, a rare genetic disorder, and public health preparedness.

title: Former FDA chief Hahn joins venture firm that launched Moderna
summary: Stephen Hahn, former FDA commissioner under President Donald Trump, has joined venture capital firm Flagship Pioneering as its chief medical officer. Flagship, known for co-founding Moderna, announced a new $3.4 billion fund to support 20-25 new companies, with Hahn leading a division focused on preventive medicine and health security. This move has sparked debate due to Flagship's significant stake in Moderna, a company whose COVID-19 vaccine Hahn's FDA authorized.

title: Lilly Announces Head-to-Head Study Comparing Once-Monthly Emgality® with Every-Other-Day Nurtec® ODT for the Preventive Treatment of Migraine
summary: Eli Lilly and Company is initiating a head-to-head Phase 4 study to compare its once-monthly injectable Emgality (galcanezumab-gnlm) with every-other-day Nurtec ODT (rimegepant) for the preventive treatment of episodic migraine. This study marks the first head-to-head clinical trial comparing two CGRP-targeted medications and aims to provide valuable insights for clinicians and patients in making informed treatment decisions. The primary endpoint will be a 50% reduction in monthly migraine headache days, with enrollment expected to begin later in 2021.

title: CureVac fails in pivotal COVID-19 vaccine trial with 47% efficacy
summary: CureVac's COVID-19 vaccine achieved only 47% efficacy in a late-stage trial, missing its main goal and casting doubt on its agreements to supply hundreds of millions of doses to the European Union and Germany. The disappointing results, influenced by a broad diversity of virus variants, caused CureVac's U.S. traded shares to fall 50.6%. The company hopes for a better outcome with further analysis and plans a second-generation vaccine for late 2022.

title: First patient receives controversial Biogen Alzheimer’s drug
summary: The first patient outside of clinical trials received Biogen's controversial Alzheimer's drug, Aduhelm, in the U.S. The drug, approved despite expert panel objections, is expensive at $56,000 a year, raising concerns about insurance coverage and patient access, especially since its efficacy beyond reducing brain plaques is still debated.

title: Driving change to defeat diabetes and other serious chronic diseases
summary: Novo Nordisk, a leading healthcare company, is dedicated to addressing unmet medical needs in diabetes, obesity, and other serious chronic diseases, building on its rich history since the discovery of insulin. The article highlights Novo Nordisk's advancements in insulin therapies, GLP-1 analogues for diabetes and obesity, and treatments for rare disorders like haemophilia and growth hormone deficiency. The company emphasizes its commitment to sustainable business practices, global partnerships, and continued innovation in prevention and regenerative interventions.

title: Global clinical trials market to value $77 billion by 2026
summary: The global clinical trials market is projected to reach over $77.2 billion by 2026, growing at a CAGR of 7.1 percent from 2021. This growth is driven by factors such as the rise of infectious diseases like COVID-19, increasing prevalence of chronic and neurological conditions, and the growing adoption of virtual clinical trials. Government support and increased R&D expenditure particularly in oncology and the Asia Pacific region, are also significant contributors to market expansion.

title: US to Invest $3 Billion on Antiviral Drugs for COVID-19
summary: The United States is investing $3.2 billion in a new "antiviral program for pandemics" to develop drugs for COVID-19 and other potential pandemic viruses. Dr. Anthony Fauci announced this initiative, which aims to accelerate human trials for promising COVID-19 treatments and support research for new antiviral drugs. The program seeks to create simple, orally administered treatments, contrasting with existing antibody treatments that require medical facility administration.

title: Pfizer Announces Ramcess Jean-Louis as Global Chief Diversity, Equity And Inclusion Officer
summary: Pfizer has announced the appointment of Ramcess Jean-Louis, Esq. as its Global Chief Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) Officer. Jean-Louis brings over 20 years of experience in human capital solutions, previously serving in a similar role at Verizon Media and as Director of Workforce Diversity and Inclusion at Comcast. In his new position, he will be responsible for developing and executing Pfizer's global DEI strategies to enhance its culture of inclusivity.

title: Sinovac vaccine remains effective vs severe COVID-19, says DOH
summary: The Department of Health (DOH) reaffirmed that the Sinovac COVID-19 vaccine remains effective against severe infection, despite reports of over 350 vaccinated medical workers in Indonesia contracting the virus. Health Undersecretary Maria Rosario Vergeire emphasized that real-world studies show all vaccines used in the Philippines are equally effective in preventing severe infection and hospitalization. She also urged caution in interpreting incomplete data regarding the Indonesian cases and encouraged the public to get vaccinated.

title: Philippines seals biggest COVID-19 vaccine order yet, for 40 mln Pfizer doses
summary: The Philippine government has signed its largest COVID-19 vaccine deal to date, securing 40 million doses of the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine, with deliveries starting in late September. This order significantly boosts the country's national immunization program, aiming for herd immunity by year-end and targeting 70 million vaccinated people. The Philippines has now acquired a total of 113 million doses from various manufacturers.

title: Adams Graduates from Elmira College
summary: Jessica Adams of Ashland was among the graduates celebrated at the 163rd Elmira College Commencement on Sunday, June 6, graduating with a Bachelor of Science. The ceremony included 169 undergraduate and 23 graduate students, and featured the conferral of an honorary Doctor of Letters to Ron Verkleeren, senior vice president and general manager of Life Sciences at Corning, Inc. Verkleeren was recognized for his leadership in providing critical products during the COVID-19 pandemic, including vaccine vials.

title: Incannex Healthcare to develop IHL-216A formulation for traumatic brain injury clinical trials
summary: Incannex Healthcare (ASX: IHL) has engaged drug manufacturer Vectura Limited to develop the specific formulation for clinical trials of IHL-216A, its lead drug for treating traumatic brain injury (TBI). IHL-216A combines cannabidiol (CBD) and a volatile anaesthetic agent, intended to reduce neuronal damage, neuroinflammation, and behavioral deficits following TBI. Vectura will handle formulation studies, manufacturing optimization, stability assessments, and regulatory support for IHL-216A and its inhalation delivery mechanism.

title: Philippines signs deal for 40 million Pfizer/BioNTech vaccine doses – report
summary: The Philippine government has signed a supply agreement for 40 million doses of the Pfizer/BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine, according to CNN Philippines. Deliveries are expected to commence "after eight weeks starting August." This agreement was confirmed by Carlito Galvez, head of the government's COVID-19 vaccine procurement.

title: Pfizer, Roche, Teva grab pharma Cannes Lions for 2021, but a wearable company scores the top creativity prize
summary: The Cannes Lions festival for 2021 awarded its top pharma Grand Prix to Woojer, a non-pharma wearable audio company, for its "Sick Beats" vest designed to help cystic fibrosis patients. Traditional pharmaceutical companies like Teva, Roche, and Pfizer still secured numerous gold, silver, and bronze awards for various campaigns, demonstrating strong representation despite not winning the top prize. The pharma category saw a significant 40% increase in entries compared to the last festival in 2019, highlighting growing engagement in pharmaceutical advertising creativity.

title: AbCellera selects Vancouver site for new 130k-sq-ft manufacturing plant
summary: AbCellera Biologics Inc. has chosen a site in Vancouver's east side for a new 130,000-square-foot manufacturing plant dedicated to therapeutic antibodies, potentially costing up to $250 million. This facility, partly funded by a $175.6 million grant from the federal government's Strategic Innovation Fund, aims to integrate with AbCellera's new 380,000-square-foot headquarters and bolster Canada's biomanufacturing capabilities. The project is expected to break ground later this year and open in 2024, creating hundreds of jobs and enabling faster development and manufacturing of antibodies from patient samples.

title: TRexBio has Jurassic day picking up ex-Lilly VP as CEO, snagging Big Pharma funding
summary: TRexBio closed the final tranche of its $59 million Series A funding, with investments from Eli Lilly, Johnson & Johnson, Pfizer, SV Health, and Alexandria Venture Investments. The company also appointed Johnston Erwin, a former Eli Lilly VP, as its new CEO, and Ovid Trifan, M.D., Ph.D., as CMO. These developments will help advance TRexBio's six preclinical therapeutic programs in cancer and inflammatory diseases, with candidate selections expected in the coming months.

title: Brazil probes vaccine contract with India’s Bharat Biotech
summary: Brazilian federal prosecutors have launched an investigation into a $320 million contract with India's Bharat Biotech for 20 million doses of its COVID-19 vaccine. The probe was initiated due to red flags including the high price of the vaccine, the speed of negotiations, and pending regulatory approvals. The contract is also under scrutiny by a Brazilian Senate inquiry, which noted "abnormal pressures" from senior health ministry officials to finalize the deal.

title: Pfizer (PFE) Pauses Chantix Smoking Drug Distribution After Finding Carcinogen
summary: Pfizer has halted global distribution of its smoking-cessation drug Chantix and is recalling certain lots. This decision was made after detecting elevated levels of nitrosamines, a probable carcinogen, in the medication. The company stated the action is a precautionary measure while further testing is conducted.

title: With Alzheimer’s drugs in focus, Bristol Myers rejoins the hunt
summary: Bristol Myers Squibb is re-entering Alzheimer's research by paying $80 million for exclusive rights to Prothena's experimental drug PRX005, which targets the tau protein. This move comes at a pivotal time in Alzheimer's drug development, following controversies around Aduhelm's approval and Eli Lilly's plans for accelerated approval of donanemab. Prothena stands to gain significantly from the collaboration, with potential payments totaling up to $2.2 billion plus royalties.

title: In Vivo Safety of Tumor Treating Fields (TTFields) Applied to the Torso
summary: This study investigates the in vivo safety of Tumor Treating Fields (TTFields) when applied to the torso of healthy rats at frequencies of 150 and 200 kHz, crucial for treating various torso cancers. The research found no treatment-related mortality or significant adverse effects on animal health, blood parameters, or internal organs over two weeks, despite therapeutic-level electric field intensities. These findings suggest that TTFields can be safely applied to the torso, attributed to the frequency specificity of TTFields for cancerous cells versus normal cells with high proliferation rates.

title: FDA adds warning about rare heart inflammation to Pfizer, Moderna COVID shots
summary: The U.S. drug regulator has added a warning to Pfizer and Moderna COVID-19 vaccine literature regarding a rare risk of heart inflammation, specifically myocarditis and pericarditis. These adverse events are more common in young males after the second dose, with symptoms appearing within days of vaccination. Over 1,200 cases have been reported out of 300 million mRNA vaccine doses administered, leading the CDC to identify 309 hospitalizations in people under 30.

title: FDA Grants Fast Track Designation to SNDX-5613 for R/R MLLr and NMP1-Mutant Acute Leukemias
summary: The FDA has granted fast track designation to SNDX-5613 for the treatment of adult and pediatric patients with relapsed or refractory acute leukemias who harbor a mixed lineage leukemia rearranged or nucleophosmin mutation. SNDX-5613, an oral menin inhibitor developed by Syndax Pharmaceuticals, Inc., is currently being investigated in the phase 1/2 AUGEMENT clinical trial, which has shown robust clinical responses in the dose-escalation portion. This designation underscores the drug's potential to significantly improve outcomes for patients with these genetically-defined acute leukemias, an underserved area with poor prognosis.

title: Online medicine purchases gain ground in China
summary: Online pharmacies are rapidly developing in China, driven by convenience, timely deliveries, and easy access, especially during and after the COVID-19 pandemic. Monthly active users on platforms like 111 Inc and Dingdang Medicine Express surged, with the market growing to 159.3 billion yuan in 2020. Companies like AliHealth and JDH Online Healthcare also reported significant sales increases, innovating to ensure medicine supply and delivery even in challenging circumstances.

title: Gilead, Foresite back biotech developer of COVID-19 pill in latest SPAC deal
summary: Pardes Biosciences, a biotech company developing an antiviral pill for COVID-19, is going public through a merger with a blank-check company launched by Foresite Capital. This deal will provide Pardes with $276 million to advance its drug candidate into clinical testing. Gilead and other investors are backing Pardes, highlighting the continued push for oral COVID-19 treatments which could complement existing infused therapies, especially given emerging variants and global vaccine distribution challenges.

title: The Anavex results
summary: A biotech company, Anavex Life Sciences, announced encouraging clinical trial results for their experimental therapy, ANAVEX2-73 (blarcamesine), in people with Parkinson’s disease dementia. The study showed significantly positive outcomes in both cognitive and motor symptoms over a 14-week period. The article delves into the mechanism of action of ANAVEX2-73 as a Sigma-1 receptor agonist and compares it with other therapies targeting Parkinson's.

title: Williams-Sonoma CEO Laura Alber Named Top CEO
summary: Williams-Sonoma, Inc. CEO Laura Alber has been recognized on the Barron’s Top CEO List 2021 for her leadership during the COVID-19 pandemic, positioning the company for future growth with robust e-commerce and a relevant product lineup. Barron's also highlighted Williams-Sonoma's commitments to gender equity and environmental goals, including achieving carbon neutrality for its operations by 2025. The list features other prominent executives from various industries.

title: Abbott Laboratories stock falls Wednesday, underperforms market
summary: Abbott Laboratories (ABT) stock declined by 1.09% on Wednesday, closing at $115.93, despite an overall positive day for the stock market. This fall ended a four-day winning streak for the company. The stock underperformed compared to competitors like Johnson & Johnson, Roche Holding AG, and Pfizer Inc.

title: Pfizer halts distribution of anti-smoking drug after finding carcinogen
summary: Pfizer Inc. has paused the distribution of its anti-smoking treatment, Chantix, after detecting elevated levels of cancer-causing agents called nitrosamines in the pills. The company is recalling several lots of the drug, which was approved by the FDA in 2006. Pfizer stated that the pause is a precautionary measure and that the benefits of Chantix still outweigh the potential risks from nitrosamine exposure.

title: Spero Therapeutics Announces $40 Million Equity Investment from Pfizer Inc. and Licensing Agreement for SPR206
summary: Spero Therapeutics announced a $40 million equity investment from Pfizer Inc. as part of the Pfizer Breakthrough Growth Initiative, and a licensing agreement for SPR206. The agreement grants Pfizer rights to develop, manufacture, and commercialize SPR206 in ex-U.S. and ex-Asia territories, with Spero eligible for up to $80 million in milestones and royalties. This funding aims to support Spero's clinical programs and preparation for the tebipenem HBr launch, extending its cash runway into the second half of 2022.

title: Spero Therapeutics Announces $40M Equity Investment from Pfizer
summary: Spero Therapeutics announced a $40 million equity investment from Pfizer as part of the Pfizer Breakthrough Growth Initiative. Additionally, Spero granted Pfizer rights to develop, manufacture, and commercialize SPR206, an IV-administered next-generation polymyxin product candidate, in ex-U.S. and ex-Asia territories. This investment is expected to extend Spero's cash runway into the second half of 2022 and support the development and potential launch of its pipeline products.

title: Innate Pharma’s ANKET NK Engager Platform Eradicates Tumors Safely and Efficiently
summary: Innate Pharma has developed ANKET™ (Antibody-based NK cell Engager Therapeutics), a novel immunotherapy platform that utilizes the innate immune system to eradicate solid and metastatic tumors. Preclinical studies using ANKET have shown exceptional efficacy and safety in animal models, leading to complete tumor eradication and no observed toxicity. Innate Pharma's partner, Sanofi, is advancing the lead asset toward human clinical trials in 2022, aiming to improve upon traditional T-cell therapies by harnessing the immediate killing capabilities of NK cells.

title: Pakistan receives 2.5 million Moderna doses from U.S.
summary: Pakistan has received 2.5 million doses of Moderna's COVID-19 vaccine from the United States through the COVAX facility, boosting its ongoing vaccination campaign. The country has primarily relied on Chinese vaccines but also plans to acquire Pfizer doses and uses AstraZeneca. With over 13 million partially vaccinated and 3 million fully vaccinated, Pakistan has recorded 959,685 cases and 22,345 deaths from COVID-19.

title: GSK returns to brain drugs with major biotech deal
summary: GlaxoSmithKline announced a deal to pay at least $700 million to Alector for rights to two experimental drugs targeting neurodegenerative diseases, marking GSK's return to brain drug development after over a decade. The collaboration, which could involve an additional $1.5 billion in milestone payments, focuses on drugs that boost a protein crucial for brain health and are being tested against various dementias, including Parkinson's and Alzheimer's. This move follows recent advancements and new investments in Alzheimer's drug development by other major pharmaceutical companies.

title: Dr Reddy's expects biz growth to be volatile in current fiscal
summary: Dr. Reddy's Laboratories anticipates "volatile" business growth in the current fiscal year due to ongoing disruptions from the COVID-19 pandemic. Despite these challenges, the company expects to deliver satisfactory performance by leveraging growth levers such as market share expansion, new product launches, business scaling, and opportunities from COVID-19 related products. The drugmaker also reported its consolidated net profit for FY2020-21 was Rs 1,952 crore, with net sales reaching Rs 18,420 crore, and highlighted its focus on digital transformation and complex product development.

title: Japan to ship millions more COVID-19 vaccines to Taiwan, Asian neighbours this week
summary: Japan announced it would send millions more doses of AstraZeneca's COVID-19 vaccine to Taiwan and other Asian neighbors this week. This follows previous donations and aims to assist countries facing urgent vaccine supply needs. Taiwan is also set to receive additional AstraZeneca doses directly ordered by the government, with a goal to vaccinare 25% of its population by the end of the month.

title: Phase 1/2 Trial Shows Positive Data for Galinpepimut-S and Pembrolizumab Combination in WT1+ Ovarian Cancer
summary: A phase 1/2 clinical trial indicates that the combination of galinpepimut-S (GPS) and pembrolizumab shows promising antitumor activity for patients with Wilms Tumor–1 (WT1)–positive ovarian cancer. All 11 patients in the study group are still alive, with 5 continuing treatment, and the disease control rate was 63.6% with a median progression-free survival of 11.8 weeks. The combination also demonstrated initial immunobiological activity, increasing CD8-positive and CD4-positive T-lymphocytes, and had a safety profile similar to pembrolizumab alone.

title: 'This will shut us down': HIV prevention clinics brace for Gilead reimbursement cuts
summary: HIV prevention clinics, particularly those serving disadvantaged populations, are facing a severe financial crisis due to Gilead Sciences' decision to cut reimbursement for its patient assistance program. This change, expected to result in a loss of over $100 million annually, threatens the federal government's goal of ending the HIV/AIDS epidemic by 2030 and will disproportionately impact communities of color. The funding cuts stem from a complex issue involving the 340B federal drug pricing law and Gilead's decision to alter its reimbursement policy for free antiretrovirals.

title: Catalyst Pharmaceuticals Inc. stock outperforms competitors on strong trading day
summary: Catalyst Pharmaceuticals Inc. (CPRX) saw its stock rise by 2.05% to $5.48 on a tough trading day, outperforming major indices and competitors like Johnson & Johnson, Pfizer Inc., and Abbott Laboratories. This increase broke a three-day losing streak for the company. The stock closed $0.74 below its 52-week high of $6.22, achieved on June 28th.

title: Tamura: 6-week period between Pfizer shots poses no problem
summary: Health minister Norihisa Tamura stated that the Pfizer COVID-19 vaccine remains effective even if the second dose is administered up to six weeks after the first, which is double the initial recommended period. This announcement came as some municipalities faced vaccine supply reductions, leading to booking cancellations. Tamura affirmed efforts to ensure a stable supply for those facing delays, referencing WHO and other international guidelines that support a six-week interval.

title: Collaboration Between AbbVie, Biogen and Pfizer Creates World’s Largest Browsable Resource Linking Rare Protein-Coding Genetic Variants to Human Health and Disease
summary: AbbVie, Biogen, and Pfizer have collaborated to launch the world's largest browsable resource linking rare protein-coding genetic variants to human health and disease. Managed by the Broad Institute, this resource provides access to whole exome sequencing data from 300,000 UK Biobank participants, combined with their detailed health information. This initiative aims to accelerate scientific understanding of the human genome and identify therapeutic strategies for various diseases, fostering precompetitive collaboration within the industry.

title: Pfizer to seek US authorisation for third Covid-19 vaccine dose
summary: Pfizer plans to ask U.S. regulators to authorize a booster dose of its COVID-19 vaccine within the next month, citing evidence of increased reinfection risk six months post-inoculation and the spread of the Delta variant. Despite this, the FDA and CDC currently state that fully vaccinated Americans do not need a booster shot, with some scientists also questioning the necessity. Pfizer, along with BioNTech SE, stated that early data indicates a third booster dose significantly increases antibody levels, suggesting enhanced protection.

title: Experts differ on need for Johnson & Johnson COVID-19 booster shot
summary: Medical experts are divided on the necessity of a Johnson & Johnson COVID-19 booster shot, despite promising new data suggesting the single-dose vaccine holds up against the delta variant. While some experts advocate for a booster to ensure uniform protection levels across all vaccinated individuals, others, including the FDA and CDC, currently advise against it, citing a lack of formal studies and recommendations. The debate highlights the ongoing scientific deliberation regarding booster shots, especially for immunocompromised individuals.

title: 'Fight for vaccine': Thais snap up shots in seconds via Shopee sale
summary: In Thailand, a hospital sold out Moderna vaccine slots within minutes on the e-commerce platform Shopee, highlighting surging demand for mRNA vaccines amidst a worsening COVID-19 outbreak and concerns about locally available shot efficacy. The quick sell-out reflects a public "fight for vaccine," with private hospitals and the government working to secure more mRNA doses like Moderna and Pfizer-BioNTech for future delivery.

title: BioNTech COVID-19 vaccines coming to Taiwan, Chinese agent says
summary: Shanghai Fosun Pharmaceutical Group, the Chinese sales agent for BioNTech, announced a deal to provide 10 million COVID-19 vaccine doses to Taiwan. This agreement is part of a politically charged process for Taiwan to secure vaccines, with the island's government previously accusing China of blocking direct purchases from BioNTech. The vaccines will be purchased by Taiwan's Foxconn founder Terry Gou and TSMC, who are negotiating on behalf of the government.

title: One and Done: Why People Are Eager for Johnson & Johnson’s Vaccine (Published 2021)
summary: The Johnson & Johnson single-shot COVID-19 vaccine, despite a slightly lower efficacy rate than Moderna and Pfizer-BioNTech, is proving popular due to its convenience. Health officials are leveraging its "one and done" nature to streamline distribution, particularly in vulnerable communities, and reduce operational costs associated with second doses. States are strategically deploying the vaccine to pharmacies, urgent care clinics, and community health centers, recognizing its potential to reach more people faster.

title: Novavax COVID-19 Vaccine Less Likely to Cause Side Effects
summary: Novavax's COVID-19 vaccine has shown a significantly lower rate of side effects compared to the Pfizer-BioNTech and Moderna vaccines, which could encourage vaccination among individuals concerned about missing work due to post-vaccination sickness. The Novavax vaccine uses established protein-based subunit technology, making it potentially more appealing and easier to store than mRNA vaccines, without compromising efficacy against severe COVID-19. Its approval would offer another option, potentially boosting vaccination rates and ensuring vaccine supply for future booster shots.

title: Aptiv, Lear join Mexico's effort to ramp up vaccinations at border
summary: Auto parts suppliers Aptiv PLC and Lear Corp have transformed their facilities in Ciudad Juarez, Mexico, into COVID-19 vaccination centers to help ramp up inoculations along the northern border. This initiative aims to vaccinate thousands of workers and community members to curb the spread of the virus, which previously caused significant outbreaks in the city's factories, and to facilitate the reopening of the U.S.-Mexico border. The companies are working with the Mexican government, offering Pfizer shots to employees and the public, though vaccination is not mandatory.

title: Boosted by Earnings Reports, S&P and Nasdaq Hit New Heights
summary: The S&P and Nasdaq indices reached new record highs due to strong earnings reports and the performance of mega-cap stocks, particularly in the technology sector. The article highlights how declining Treasury yields bolstered the growth thesis for mega-cap stocks, and discusses the Principal U.S. Mega-Cap ETF (USMC) as a way to capture these market movements. USMC tracks a modified equal-weighted index of mega-cap companies, focusing on minimizing volatility while seeking optimal outcomes.

title: Moderna Joins Biotech Elite as Value Reaches $100 Billion
summary: Moderna (MRNA) briefly achieved a market valuation of over $100 billion, with its share price rising significantly. This milestone comes as global COVID-19 vaccination efforts accelerate, and Moderna's vaccine, which received emergency use authorization in December, continues to play a key role. The company's stock has surged over 220% in the last year due to the rapid development and deployment of its vaccine.

title: Novartis may have the most new drug approvals, but Roche, Lilly and AbbVie's launches win on value: report
summary: A report by Evaluate Vantage indicates that while Novartis leads in new drug approvals with a dozen green lights, Roche, Eli Lilly, and AbbVie are extracting the most value from their recent drug launches. This success is attributed to blockbuster drugs like Tecentriq, Verzenio, Rinvoq, and Skyrizi, which significantly contribute to their respective net present values. The analysis emphasizes that approval volume doesn't always correlate with therapeutic or financial impact, as these companies demonstrate strong market performance from fewer, high-value introductions.

title: GlaxoSmithKline To Spin-Off Consumer Healthcare Business By Mid-2022
summary: GlaxoSmithKline (GSK) announced plans to spin off its Consumer Healthcare division into a separately listed company by mid-2022, creating a focused biopharma company and a leading consumer healthcare business. The transaction, described as tax-efficient, will demerge at least 80% of GSK's 68% holding in the Consumer Healthcare business to shareholders. This move is accelerated by activist investor Elliott Management Corp., which had pushed for changes and a potential sale of the consumer unit.

title: Amgen’s Neulasta Ad Indirectly Targeting Biosimilars Draws US FDA Rebuke
summary: The US FDA has issued a rebuke against Amgen for an advertisement promoting its drug Neulasta. The FDA objects to the ad because it indirectly targets biosimilars, a practice the regulatory body has previously scrutinized. This incident follows a pattern of FDA objection to Amgen's promotional activities for other drugs as well.

title: Pfizer Agrees to Pay $345M to Settle EpiPen Price Hike Case
summary: Pfizer Inc. and two of its subsidiaries have agreed to pay $345 million to settle lawsuits alleging anticompetitive pricing and marketing of EpiPen auto-injectors. This proposed settlement, if accepted by a U.S. federal court, would resolve consumer litigation against Pfizer while Mylan NV (now Viatris) still faces trial in 2022 over antitrust claims. Pfizer denies wrongdoing, stating the settlement avoids litigation distraction and allows focus on medical breakthroughs.

title: Canada will soon allow vaccine mixing for second doses. (Published 2021)
summary: Canada's immunization advisory body is recommending that some Canadians receive a different vaccine for their second dose, particularly for those who initially received the AstraZeneca shot. This decision comes amidst vaccine shortages and aims to provide maximum protection as the country ramps up second doses. Several studies have shown that mixing vaccines is safe and effective, and many provinces will allow this practice.

title: New Thermo Fisher Scientific Facility in Carlsbad Will Make Vital Component for RNA Vaccines
summary: Thermo Fisher Scientific has opened a new 67,000-square-foot manufacturing facility in Carlsbad to produce plasmid DNA, a vital component for RNA-based vaccines and gene therapies. This expansion addresses the increasing global demand for these materials, creating 150 new jobs and reinforcing San Diego County's reputation as an innovation hub.

title: Bristol Myers Squibb's Opdivo and Yervoy combo falls short in first-line squamous head and neck cancer
summary: Bristol Myers Squibb's combination therapy of Opdivo and Yervoy failed to demonstrate a statistically significant advantage over the Extreme regimen in a phase 3 trial for first-line platinum-eligible recurrent or metastatic squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck (SCCHC). While the combo showed a positive overall survival trend, the control arm performed better than anticipated. This outcome highlights the challenges in treating this particular cancer, despite Opdivo and Yervoy showing success in other tumor types.

title: $345 Million Settlement Proposed in EpiPen Lawsuits
summary: Pfizer Inc. has agreed to a $345 million proposed settlement to resolve lawsuits concerning steep price increases for EpiPens. The lawsuits alleged anticompetitive conduct by Pfizer and its subsidiaries related to EpiPen, a device that delivers epinephrine for severe allergic reactions. This settlement is subject to court approval, with Pfizer denying wrongdoing but seeking to avoid further litigation.

title: Pfizer agrees to pay $345 mln to resolve EpiPen pricing lawsuit
summary: Pfizer Inc. has agreed to a $345 million settlement to resolve a class-action lawsuit alleging anticompetitive practices led to inflated EpiPen prices. The settlement, filed in federal court in Kansas, addresses claims from consumers who overpaid for the emergency allergy treatment. This agreement does not include Mylan, the company responsible for marketing and distributing EpiPens, which is still facing related litigation.

title: Pfizer (PFE) Covid-19 Vaccine Granted Priority Review for Full U.S. Approval
summary: Pfizer Inc. announced that its Covid-19 vaccine has been granted priority review by U.S. regulators, setting the stage for potential full approval by early next year. The FDA is expected to decide on the vaccine's approval for individuals aged 16 and older by January 2022. This move could lead to broader acceptance and mandates for the vaccine in the United States.

title: Close to the Edge: Regeneron’s George Yancopoulos and Aris Baras Discuss Company, COVID-19
summary: This article features an interview with Regeneron's George Yancopoulos and Aris Baras, discussing the company's growth, its role in developing COVID-19 therapeutics like REGEN-COV, and its leadership in genomic medicine. They also explore future drug development technologies and provide advice for the Biden Administration on fostering innovation. Regeneron, founded in 1988, has grown significantly with a market cap over $50 billion.

title: Gelesis, a Consumer-Focused Biotherapeutics Company and the Maker of Plenity®, to Become a Publicly Traded Company via Merger with Capstar Special Purpose Acquisition Corp.
summary: Gelesis, a biotherapeutics company known for its weight management product Plenity®, announced its merger with Capstar Special Purpose Acquisition Corp. The transaction values the combined company at an implied market value of approximately $1.3 billion and an enterprise value of $1.0 billion, aiming to fund the full commercial launch of Plenity and expand manufacturing. The combined company's securities are expected to trade on the NYSE under the symbol "GLS."

title: Fabry Disease Treatment (2021-2030) | Potential growth, attractive valuation make it is a long-term investment | Top Key Players: Sanofi S.A., Shire Plc, Amicus Therapeutics Inc.
summary: The global Fabry disease treatment market is projected to grow from approximately USD 2.7 million in 2020 to USD 3.2 million by 2025, at a CAGR of 7.7%. This growth is driven by the adoption of new therapies like chaperone treatment and messenger RNA (mRNA) as well as technological advancements and developing healthcare infrastructure. Key players in this fragmented and competitive market include Sanofi S.A., Shire Plc, and Amicus Therapeutics Inc.

title: Novavax’s Effort to Vaccinate the World, From Zero to Not Quite Warp Speed
summary: Novavax's efforts to bring its COVID-19 vaccine to market have been slower than anticipated despite significant financial backing and promising trial results. The company, which had no products on the market prior to the pandemic, faced challenges in scaling up manufacturing, securing supplies, and transferring technology globally. Despite these delays, Novavax's vaccine is seen as crucial for global vaccination efforts, especially in developing countries, due to its high efficacy and established technology.

title: Human Growth Hormone Market Is Seeing Phenomenal Growth
summary: The Human Growth Hormone (HGH) market is experiencing significant growth, driven by new mergers, acquisitions, and a robust drug pipeline. Key players like Pfizer Inc. and Novo Nordisk are developing innovative treatments, with somapacitan and MOD-4023 showing promise in clinical trials. Despite strong growth, strict regulations on HGH use by athletes and sports professionals are expected to temper market expansion.

title: US Supreme Court ruling did not allow patenting of vaccinated people
summary: Social media posts falsely claim a 2013 US Supreme Court ruling allows for the patenting of people vaccinated against Covid-19, asserting they are no longer legally human. This article debunks the claim, explaining that the Supreme Court decision in Association for Molecular Pathology v. Myriad Genetics Inc. concerned the patenting of isolated DNA segments, not vaccinated individuals, and confirmed that naturally occurring things, including humans, cannot be patented. Experts emphasize that the case has no relation to vaccines or human legal status.

title: Pfizer halts distribution of anti-smoking drug Chantix after finding carcinogen
summary: Pfizer has paused the distribution of its anti-smoking drug Chantix due to the discovery of high levels of cancer-causing nitrosamines. While the levels exceed FDA standards, the agency states there is "no immediate risk" to patients and that the benefits of quitting smoking outweigh the potential cancer risk from long-term impurity exposure. The FDA initially alerted consumers to a voluntary recall on July 2, 2021.

title: Vedanta raises $68M, reveals setback to Bristol Myers alliance
summary: Vedanta Biosciences secured $68 million in a Series D funding round to advance its microbiome candidate, VE303, into a phase 3 trial for Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI). The funding will also support a phase 2 trial for VE202 in ulcerative colitis. Concurrently, the company disclosed that its alliance with Bristol Myers Squibb for the checkpoint inhibitor combination (VE800) did not meet expansion criteria following a phase 1 trial.

title: Boston Scientific heart implant linked to steep drop-off in afib-related stroke risk: study
summary: New clinical trial data for Boston Scientific's Watchman FLX heart implant shows a significant reduction in stroke risk for atrial fibrillation patients. The device demonstrated a two-year stroke and systemic embolism rate of just 3.4%, well below the success endpoint of 8.7%. This data reinforces the Watchman FLX as a safe and effective alternative to long-term blood thinner medications, especially for elderly patients with complex cardiac conditions.

title: Gavreto is FDA-approved for RET-altered thyroid cancers
summary: The FDA has approved Gavreto (pralsetinib) from Blueprint Medicines for adult patients with metastatic RET fusion-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). This approval follows its initial FDA nod in September 2020. CStone has also secured approval for the drug in China, marking it as a novel therapy for advanced RET fusion-positive NSCLC following platinum-based chemotherapy.

title: Animal health companies can do more to fight antibiotic resistance, says FAIRR
summary: A new report by the sustainability-focused investor network FAIRR highlights that animal health companies are not doing enough to combat antibiotic resistance in animal agriculture supply chains. The report, "Feeding resistance: Antimicrobial stewardship in the animal health industry," found that none of the 10 largest publicly-listed animal health companies have a comprehensive policy to address this issue, despite 70% of global antimicrobial use occurring in animal farming. FAIRR urges investors, policymakers, and companies to collaborate for greater transparency and improved antibiotic stewardship to prevent a potential "trillion-dollar antimicrobial resistance crisis."

title: Global Apixaban {Eliquis} Market is expected to grow significantly with a CAGR of 7.5% during the forecast period
summary: The global Apixaban (Eliquis) market is projected to grow at a CAGR of 7.5% through 2030, driven by the increasing prevalence of venous thromboembolism-related illnesses and more therapeutic indications for the drug. Key market segments include tablets and capsules, various distribution channels like hospitals and online pharmacies, and oral or injectable administration. North America is expected to lead this market, with major players including Abbott, Bristol-Myers Squibb, and Pfizer.

title: In venue fit for head of state, Suga seeks vaccine from Pfizer CEO
summary: Japanese Prime Minister Yoshihide Suga met with Pfizer CEO Albert Bourla in a high-profile setting to secure vaccine deliveries amid concerns about supply and a growing outbreak in Japan. Suga requested Bourla to accelerate the delivery of 20 million doses planned for October, thanking him for vaccine donations for Olympic participants. Japan is facing a resurgence of COVID-19 cases and a lagging vaccination rate, especially among younger people, despite criticism for prioritizing the Olympics.

title: Arvinas and Pfizer enter up to $2.4bn deal to develop breast cancer drug
summary: Arvinas and Pfizer have formed a global partnership to develop and commercialize ARV-471, an investigational breast cancer therapy. The deal includes an upfront payment of $650 million from Pfizer, a $350 million equity investment, and up to $1.4 billion in milestone payments for Arvinas. The companies will equally share development costs and profits for ARV-471, which is an oral PROTAC estrogen receptor protein degrader currently in Phase II trials.

title: As Olympics begin, Japan rolls out red carpet for Pfizer CEO
summary: Japan's Prime Minister Yoshihide Suga met with Pfizer CEO Albert Bourla to secure COVID-19 vaccine deliveries amid concerns over dwindling supply and a surging outbreak, coinciding with the start of the Olympics. Japan's vaccination rate lags, with only 23% of its population fully vaccinated, prompting Suga to request accelerated delivery of 20 million doses. Bourla, in Tokyo for the Olympics opening, also discussed with Suga the donation of Pfizer vaccines for Olympic participants.

title: Pfizer, Johnson & Johnson settle high-profile Remicade biosim lawsuit on undisclosed terms
summary: Pfizer and Johnson & Johnson have settled their nearly four-year legal battle over the competitive practices surrounding J&J's immunology blockbuster Remicade and Pfizer's biosimilar, Inflectra. The terms of the settlement, which ended a groundbreaking case that was expected to be a bellwether for the biosimilar industry, remain undisclosed. Pfizer had accused J&J of using "exclusionary contracts" to stifle competition for Inflectra, though both companies released statements affirming their commitment to patient access and a competitive market.

title: Pfizer Inks Second Collaboration with Arvinas, Makes Billion-Dollar Investment on a Novel Agent for Breast Cancer Therapy
summary: Pfizer and Arvinas have entered a second collaboration, with Pfizer investing over a billion dollars in Arvinas' lead immuno-oncology candidate, ARV-471, for breast cancer therapy. The deal includes a $650 million upfront payment and a $350 million equity investment from Pfizer. This partnership aims to accelerate the development and commercialization of ARV-471, a targeted protein degrader for ER-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer, building on a previous 2018 collaboration.

title: WORLD – Covid vaccine maker BioNTech attempts shot for malaria next
summary: BioNTech, the company behind a successful Covid-19 vaccine, is now venturing into developing a malaria vaccine using mRNA technology. This initiative marks BioNTech's first solo project and new infectious disease effort since the pandemic, aiming to start patient trials by late next year. The project also focuses on building manufacturing infrastructure in Africa for future mRNA vaccines, addressing the significant global health burden of malaria.

title: Pfizer says 2021 COVID-19 vaccine sales to top $33.5 bln, sees need for boosters
summary: Pfizer has increased its 2021 sales forecast for its COVID-19 vaccine to $33.5 billion and believes a third booster dose will be necessary to maintain high protection against the virus, especially the Delta variant. The company also suggested filing for emergency use authorization for a booster as early as August, citing data showing significantly increased antibody levels after a third dose. This comes amidst declining vaccine efficacy over time and ongoing discussions with regulators about booster shots for certain populations, while billions globally still await their first dose.

title: Driven by Profits from Antibiotics, Animal Health Industry Is Feeding Risks of ‘Superbugs’ & Next Pandemic
summary: A new report by the FAIRR Initiative warns that the animal health industry's uncontrolled use of antibiotics in intensively farmed livestock is fueling a global "superbug" crisis and increasing the risk of the next pandemic. The report criticizes 10 major animal health companies for marketing critical drugs as growth promoters and preventative medications, contributing to misuse and overuse in livestock. It highlights that 70% of global antibiotics are given to animals and calls for better stewardship, alternative treatments like vaccines and probiotics, and clearer labeling to prevent antibiotic resistance.

title: GSK and Vir Biotechnology announce Joint Procurement Agreement with European Commission for COVID-19 treatment, sotrovimab
summary: GSK and Vir Biotechnology have signed a Joint Procurement Agreement with the European Commission to supply up to 220,000 doses of sotrovimab, an investigational single-dose COVID-19 treatment. This agreement will allow participating EU Member States to purchase sotrovimab for high-risk patients following local or EU-level emergency authorization. Sotrovimab demonstrated a 79% reduction in hospitalizations or death in the Phase 3 COMET-ICE trial and has shown activity against circulating variants, including Delta and Lambda.

title: Sanofi raises profit forecast after second quarter beat
summary: Sanofi has increased its 2021 profit forecast after exceeding second-quarter expectations, driven by strong sales of its vaccines and eczema treatment, Dupixent. The French drugmaker now targets an earnings per share growth of approximately 12% and remains confident in its COVID-19 vaccine project with GlaxoSmithKline, expecting regulatory approval by year-end. Despite its vaccine coming later than competitors, Sanofi believes it will play a significant role globally and as a potential booster shot.

title: Pfizer backs protein degrader drugs with Arvinas deal
summary: Pfizer is investing $1 billion in Arvinas, a Yale University spin-out, to commercialize ARV-471, a protein degrader drug for breast cancer. This significant investment comprises a $350 million equity investment and $650 million cash upfront, building on a previous licensing deal from 2018. ARV-471, a proteolysis targeting chimera (Protac), targets the oestrogen receptor and is currently in Phase 2 clinical trials, with Phase 3 studies planned for metastatic breast cancer.

title: 1.5 Million Pfizer Vaccine Doses, Donated by the United States, Arrive in Thailand
summary: The United States donated 1.5 million doses of Pfizer COVID-19 vaccine to Thailand, with an additional one million doses committed, reaffirming U.S. support and partnership in fighting the pandemic. This donation is part of President Biden's commitment to provide safe and effective vaccinations globally and help accelerate vaccination campaigns in the region. The Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine, developed by American and German companies, is 95 percent effective and was the first to receive WHO emergency use authorization.

title: New Harvard-MIT Biotech Center Appoints CEO, Begins Construction on Facility
summary: The newly named Landmark Bio, a Harvard-MIT biotech center, has appointed Ran Zheng as its inaugural CEO and begun construction on a 40,000 square-foot facility in Watertown, Mass. This public-private partnership aims to accelerate the production and delivery of new treatment technologies through collaborations between academics, biopharma, and medical leaders. The facility will focus on cell and gene therapy, gene editing, and messenger RNA products, partnering with several Harvard Medical School affiliates and the Massachusetts Life Science Center.

title: Pfizer and Moderna raise prices for COVID-19 vaccines in EU- FT
summary: Pfizer and Moderna have increased the prices of their COVID-19 vaccines for new supply contracts with the European Union, according to the Financial Times. Pfizer's shot rose to 19.50 euros from 15.50 euros, while Moderna's vaccine is now priced at $25.50, up from about 19 euros previously, though this is lower than an earlier agreed $28.50 due to a larger order volume. Both companies declined to comment on the confidential contract details.

title: Forecast: Analysts Think Pfizer Inc.'s (NYSE:PFE) Business Prospects Have Improved Drastically
summary: Analysts have significantly upgraded Pfizer Inc.'s revenue and earnings per share forecasts for 2021, indicating a drastic improvement in business fundamentals. Despite these optimistic revisions, the consensus price target remains largely unchanged, suggesting that the long-term impact on the stock's valuation is still uncertain. Pfizer is projected to grow much faster than in the past and outperform its industry competitors in revenue growth, although some warning flags related to its balance sheet have been identified.

title: Sanofi bets $3.2B on mRNA with deal to buy Translate Bio
summary: Sanofi is acquiring its research partner Translate Bio for $3.2 billion, signaling a major commitment to messenger RNA (mRNA) technology. This acquisition leverages the success of mRNA in COVID-19 vaccines and aims to expand its application to other vaccines, immunology, oncology, and rare diseases. The deal is expected to close in the third quarter of the year, with Sanofi already owning a 6.5% stake in Translate Bio.

title: With $3.2B, Sanofi takes in mRNA partner Translate Bio in buyout deal
summary: Sanofi is acquiring its mRNA partner Translate Bio for $3.2 billion, following an early investment in mRNA technology and plans to establish an mRNA Center of Excellence. This acquisition aims to accelerate Sanofi's mRNA vaccine programs for COVID-19 and influenza, bringing them in-house along with Translate Bio's lipid nanoparticle technology and other programs like a cystic fibrosis candidate. The deal solidifies Sanofi's position in the rapidly growing mRNA space, driven by CEO Paul Hudson's strategy to enhance R&D capabilities.

title: Sanofi is all in on mRNA, with $3.2 billion Translate Bio acquisition
summary: Sanofi is acquiring its mRNA partner, Translate Bio, for $3.2 billion, aiming to solidify its position in mRNA technology. This acquisition will bolster Sanofi's mRNA investments, adding experimental programs for COVID-19, influenza, and cystic fibrosis. Despite mixed early clinical trial results for some of Translate Bio's programs, Sanofi believes in the long-term potential of mRNA therapies and vaccines.

title: Pfizer to require U.S. workers receive COVID-19 vaccine or regular tests
summary: Pfizer will require all its U.S. employees and contractors to either get vaccinated against COVID-19 or undergo weekly testing. This policy aims to protect the health and safety of their staff and the community. Employees with medical or religious objections can seek accommodations, while international staff are strongly encouraged to get vaccinated where possible.

title: Moderna COVID-19 vaccine remains 93% effective after six months
summary: Moderna announced that its COVID-19 vaccine maintains 93% effectiveness six months after the second dose, generating over $4 billion in second-quarter sales and driving the company to a significant profit. The company is also developing other vaccines and a potential COVID-19 booster shot, with second-quarter earnings surpassing Wall Street expectations.

title: Moderna's Covid vaccine 93 percent effective six months after second dose, company says
summary: Moderna announced its Covid-19 vaccine maintained 93% effectiveness six months after the second dose, comparable to its initial clinical trial results. However, the company stated that a booster shot would likely be necessary before winter due to waning antibody levels, especially in light of the Delta variant. Moderna also confirmed robust antibody responses from its booster candidates against several variants and detailed significant vaccine contract sales for 2021 and 2022.

title: Gemcitabine and APG-1252, a novel small molecule inhibitor of BCL-2/BCL-XL, display a synergistic antitumor effect in nasopharyngeal carcinoma through the JAK-2/STAT3/MCL-1 signaling pathway
summary: This study investigates the synergistic antitumor effect of gemcitabine and APG-1252, a novel BCL-2/BCL-XL inhibitor, in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). The combination therapy demonstrated enhanced anti-proliferation, apoptosis induction, and suppression of invasion and migration in NPC cells both in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistically, this synergistic effect is attributed to the activation of caspase-dependent pathways and the blocking of the JAK-2/STAT3/MCL-1 signaling pathway.

title: Novavax’s Vaccine Works Well — Except on Variant First Found in South Africa (Published 2021)
summary: Novavax announced that its COVID-19 vaccine is highly effective, showing nearly 90% efficacy in a large trial in Britain. However, the vaccine's efficacy dropped significantly to just under 50% in a smaller South African trial, where the B.1.351 variant was prevalent. This finding highlights the challenge of mutating viruses and prompted Novavax to develop a new vaccine specifically targeting the South African variant.

title: Novavax CEO explains delay in COVID-19 vaccine EUA filing
summary: Novavax announced a delay in its COVID-19 vaccine emergency use authorization (EUA) filing with the FDA by about one month, primarily due to manufacturing quality concerns. CEO Stanley Erck attributed the delay to issues with outside firms, specifically Fujifilm Diosynth Biotechnologies, whose Texas facility had quality problems. Despite the U.S. government pausing manufacturing funding pending FDA alignment, Novavax remains optimistic about its global role, having filed for emergency use in India, the Philippines, and Indonesia.

title: Israeli survey finds 3rd Pfizer vaccine dose has similar side effects to 2nd
summary: An initial Israeli survey found that most people who received a third dose of Pfizer's COVID-19 vaccine experienced similar or fewer side effects compared to their second dose. The survey by Clalit, Israel's largest healthcare provider, involved about 4,500 people over 60 who received booster shots. The findings suggest the booster is well-tolerated, with soreness at the injection site being the most common side effect.

title: WSJ News Exclusive | RNA Tech Firm GreenLight Biosciences to Go Public in $1.5 Billion SPAC Deal
summary: GreenLight Biosciences Inc., an RNA-technology firm, is set to go public through a $1.5 billion SPAC deal, combining with Environmental Impact Acquisition Corp. The company is developing mRNA vaccines for Covid-19 and other diseases, including a seasonal flu shot and a treatment for sickle-cell disease. Additionally, GreenLight Biosciences is working on RNA-based sustainable alternatives to pesticides and herbicides.

title: Pfizer, BioNTech seek US COVID-19 vaccine clearance for children 5-11
summary: Pfizer Inc and BioNTech SE have requested emergency use authorization from US regulators for their COVID-19 vaccine for children aged 5 to 11. This age group currently has no approved COVID-19 vaccine. The FDA's advisory panel is scheduled to meet on October 26 to discuss the application, potentially paving the way for around 28 million children to receive the two-dose vaccine.

title: Sanofi, eyeing impurity concerns, pulls hypertension meds in Korea and the U.K. Could the next big 'sartan' recall be on the horizon?
summary: Sanofi has pulled several hypertension medications containing irbesartan in Korea and the U.K. due to concerns about azido impurities. This action follows similar sartan drug recalls triggered by regulatory bodies in Canada and Europe. The impurity, a potential mutagen, raises cancer risk concerns, and Sanofi's proactive recall in Korea is a precautionary measure while testing for azido impurities in older batches is ongoing.

title: Pfizer shares hit record high with COVID-19 vaccine stocks on a tear
summary: Shares of Pfizer Inc. reached a new record high on Tuesday, the first time in over 20 years, as investor interest in COVID-19 vaccine makers surged amidst rising coronavirus cases in the United States. Analysts suggest that investors are finally giving Pfizer credit for its vaccine, viewing it not just as a one-time cash infusion but as a durable business due to the ongoing pandemic and potential for vaccine technology in other diseases. This rally also coincides with strong performances from other vaccine companies like Moderna and BioNTech, with Pfizer forecasting $33.5 billion in COVID-19 vaccine sales for 2021.

title: India in talks to buy 50 million doses of Pfizer vaccine - WSJ
summary: India is reportedly in talks to acquire 50 million doses of the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine, as confirmed by the Wall Street Journal and a Pfizer spokesperson. This move aims to bolster India's vaccination efforts, which have primarily relied on the AstraZeneca vaccine and a home-grown shot, as the country seeks to vaccinate its entire adult population by December amidst concerns over the Delta variant. India has also approved other vaccines, including Johnson & Johnson's one-shot vaccine, and is engaging in advanced negotiations for its local manufacture.

title: Merck’s Best Seller Racks Up Another Regulatory Win
summary: Merck's Keytruda, in combination with Eisai’s Lemvima, received FDA approval as a first-line treatment for advanced renal cell carcinoma. This approval was based on Phase III study data showing significant improvements in progression-free survival, overall survival, and objective response rates compared to Pfizer’s Sutent. The decision highlights the potential of this combination therapy despite a high rate of serious adverse events.

title: Xywav Approved for Idiopathic Hypersomnia
summary: The FDA has approved Jazz Pharmaceuticals' Xywav (calcium, magnesium, potassium, and sodium oxybates) oral solution for the treatment of idiopathic hypersomnia in adults. This makes Xywav the first and only medicine indicated for this condition. The approval was based on a phase 3 study demonstrating Xywav's significant improvements in sleepiness and disease severity compared to placebo.

title: Focus: Pfizer, Moderna seen reaping billions from COVID-19 vaccine booster market
summary: Pfizer, BioNTech, and Moderna are poised to generate billions of dollars from COVID-19 vaccine booster shots, creating a market comparable to annual flu vaccine sales. Analysts predict substantial revenue for these companies in 2023, primarily from boosters, with the annual market potentially settling at $5 billion or higher as more drugmakers join. The need for boosters is supported by waning antibody levels and increased breakthrough infections due to the Delta variant, though the frequency and necessity are still being researched and debated by some scientists and the WHO.

title: China's Sinovac to invest $60 mln in vaccine facility in Chile
summary: Chinese pharmaceutical company Sinovac Biotech Ltd announced an investment of $60 million to build a fill-and-finish vaccine plant in Chile. This move aims to solidify Sinovac's presence in Latin America, particularly in Chile, which has extensively utilized its COVID-19 vaccine, CoronaVac. Chile has achieved one of the world's fastest vaccination campaigns, with over 60% of its population fully vaccinated using substantial doses from Sinovac.

title: Pfizer expands recall of anti-smoking drug over carcinogen presence
summary: Pfizer Inc. has expanded its recall of the anti-smoking drug Chantix, adding four more lots due to elevated levels of cancer-causing nitrosamines. This latest recall brings the total to 16 lots impacted, which were distributed across the U.S. and Puerto Rico. While no adverse events have been reported, Pfizer advises patients to consult their doctors for alternative treatment options if they have received an affected lot.

title: Explainer: Who is eligible for a third COVID-19 vaccine dose in the U.S.?
summary: U.S. health officials have authorized a third dose of COVID-19 vaccines from Pfizer and Moderna for individuals with compromised immune systems. This decision is based on evidence that the standard two doses offer less protection for these populations, which health officials estimate to be less than 3% of American adults. The article details who is considered immunocompromised, clarifies that a prescription is not needed, and outlines what other countries are doing regarding booster shots.

title: More venues, music acts move forward with COVID-19 requirements to attend shows
