summary: Acuitas Therapeutics Inc., a Canadian company that provides mRNA-delivery technology for Pfizer's COVID-19 vaccine, has sued Arbutus Biopharma Corp in Manhattan federal court. Acuitas is seeking to preemptively counter claims that the vaccine infringes on Arbutus' patents, stating that Arbutus and its partner Genevant Sciences have threatened to sue for billions in "unjustified royalties." This lawsuit is part of a growing number of patent disputes surrounding COVID-19 vaccine technology, with other companies also facing similar legal challenges.

title: Effectiveness of 2-Dose BNT162b2 (Pfizer BioNTech) mRNA Vaccine in Preventing SARS-CoV-2 Infection Among Children Aged 5–11 Years and Adolescents Aged 12–15 Years — PROTECT Cohort, July 2021–February 2022
summary: A prospective cohort study looked at the effectiveness of two doses of the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine in preventing SARS-CoV-2 infection in children aged 5–11 years and adolescents aged 12–15 years from July 2021 to February 2022. The study found that vaccination reduced the risk of Omicron infection by 31% in children aged 5–11 and by 59% in adolescents aged 12–15. Participants who were fully vaccinated and still contracted Omicron experienced less severe illness, suggesting the importance of maintaining up-to-date vaccinations for eligible children and adolescents.

title: A Spotlight on Our Oncology Research Hub in La Jolla, California
summary: Pfizer's Global Oncology Research and Development site in La Jolla, California, is dedicated to discovering and developing new therapies for various cancers, including breast cancer. Scientists at the site focus on understanding how tumor cells mutate to find targeted therapies that overcome resistance, aiming to impact patients, their families, and communities. Pfizer currently has an industry-leading portfolio of 24 approved cancer medicines and biosimilars, with expectations of up to 14 potential approvals by 2025 or 2026.

title: Western companies wrestle with Russia 'half-exits'
summary: Western companies providing essential goods like food and medicine in Russia are caught between balancing the Russian government's demands and calls from Ukraine supporters to fully withdraw. While over 400 companies have exited Russia, about 80, including consumer and pharmaceutical giants, maintain a presence, citing humanitarian concerns and potential repercussions for their employees. These firms are devising strategies like donating Russian profits to humanitarian aid or seeking buyers for local operations, as they face growing pressure to fully disengage while navigating legal, operational, and ethical dilemmas.

title: Here’s the latest on possible 4th COVID-19 vaccine shot for Americans
summary: Moderna has requested FDA authorization for a fourth COVID-19 vaccine booster for all adults, while Pfizer and BioNTech sought approval for seniors aged 65 and older, citing data from Israel showing reduced infection and severe disease rates. U.S. health officials are considering additional booster doses and seeking funding to secure more vaccines, amidst ongoing studies on omicron-specific and hybrid shots. Experts like Dr. Paul Offit question the necessity of a fourth shot for most people, emphasizing that protection against severe illness should be the primary goal.

title: Pfizer recalls some lots of blood pressure drug due to potential carcinogen
summary: Pfizer Inc. announced the recall of certain lots of its blood pressure drug Accuretic and two generic versions due to elevated levels of a potential carcinogen called nitrosamine. While Pfizer has not received reports of adverse events, long-term exposure to these impurities above acceptable levels could increase cancer risk. Patients are advised to consult their doctors for alternative treatments.

title: Pfizer to Sell Up to 4 Million Paxlovid Doses to Poorer Nations
summary: Pfizer Inc. has agreed to sell up to 4 million doses of its Covid-19 antiviral pill, Paxlovid, to 95 low- and middle-income countries through an agreement with Unicef. The terms of the deal were not disclosed, but Pfizer expects to begin supplying the drug in April and continue throughout the year. The agreement also includes some upper-middle-income countries in Africa.

title: UMass Chan and Moderna to study cytomegalovirus transmission in young children
summary: UMass Chan Medical School and Moderna, Inc. are collaborating on a comprehensive study called CMV TransmIT to investigate cytomegalovirus (CMV) transmission in young children and households. Led by Dr. Laura Gibson, the research aims to understand how CMV spreads and characterize immune responses to inform the design of prevention strategies and a potential vaccine. CMV is the most common infectious cause of birth defects, and the study will utilize public and private daycare centers in Cambridge and Worcester to identify transmission patterns.

title: Al Sandrock takes on CEO role at gene therapy developer
summary: Al Sandrock, former head of clinical development at Biogen, has been appointed CEO of gene therapy company Voyager Therapeutics. Sandrock's illustrious career at Biogen involved the discovery and development of blockbuster multiple sclerosis treatments, and he now brings his expertise to Voyager, which focuses on neurological diseases. His appointment follows recent strategic shifts at Voyager and major deals with Pfizer and Novartis to utilize its gene therapy technology.

title: COVID vaccine maker Moderna flags Japan ambition with sumo sponsorship
summary: Moderna is sponsoring sumo flags in Japan for the first time, signaling its ambition to expand its market share and public appeal in the country beyond COVID-19 vaccines, particularly as the government plans a fourth-dose vaccination program. This move comes after initial setbacks, including contaminated doses, but Moderna has since clawed back market share and is now looking ahead to combination vaccines for COVID-19 and influenza. The company aims to compete with Pfizer and establish a stronger presence in Asia, including opening a new office in Japan and expanding production capabilities.

title: UPDATED: AstraZeneca and Sanofi tweak stances on Russian operations as pharma contends with war in Ukraine
summary: Several major pharmaceutical companies, including Roche, Teva, Novartis, AstraZeneca, Sanofi, and Merck & Co., are adjusting their operations in response to the war in Ukraine. These companies are providing significant humanitarian aid to Ukraine, including donations of medicines, financial contributions, and support for their employees, while also suspending new investments and promotional activities in Russia, aligning with international sanctions. They have condemned the conflict and are working to ensure the continued supply of essential medicines to those in need.

title: Pfizer to deliver Covid-19 oral therapy courses to UNICEF
summary: Pfizer has signed an agreement with UNICEF to supply up to four million courses of its oral Covid-19 therapy, Paxlovid, to 95 low and middle-income countries. The therapy will be provided at a not-for-profit rate for lower-income nations and through a tiered pricing model for upper-middle-income countries. This initiative aims to accelerate access to Paxlovid to help reduce the strain on healthcare systems and save lives in these regions.

title: Pfizer, Moderna and J&J Face Shareholder Pressure to Broaden Covid-19 Vaccine Access
summary: Socially conscious investors and global health activists are pressuring Pfizer, Moderna, and Johnson & Johnson to broaden access to their Covid-19 vaccines in poorer countries. These groups have placed resolutions on annual proxy ballots, urging drugmakers to explore technology transfer to other manufacturers. This shareholder activism is the latest attempt to push vaccine makers to share technology and boost supplies in lower-income nations.

title: Pfizer, BioNTech obtain EU authorization for 2nd COVID-19 booster
summary: Pfizer and BioNTech have received emergency use authorization from the FDA for a second COVID-19 booster dose. This booster is approved for adults aged 50 and older, and for immunocompromised individuals aged 12 and older, who have previously received a first booster. The authorization is based on studies showing improved antibody titers against variants and increased protection against severe disease for vulnerable populations.

title: Pfizer tells Michigan workers to refund company after hack causes some to be overpaid
summary: Pfizer employees in Michigan are being asked to refund the company after a payroll mistake, caused by a ransomware attack on Ultimate Kronos Group in December 2021, led to overpayments. Employees expressed frustration and felt taken advantage of, especially since many had already spent the extra money and Pfizer had record profits in 2021. Pfizer is offering payment plans and will contribute $250 towards each worker's overpayment balance, stating it's taking a fair approach to the unforeseen situation.

title: U.S. authorizes second COVID booster for Americans 50 and older
summary: U.S. health officials have authorized a second COVID-19 booster dose for individuals aged 50 and older, and for younger immunocompromised people, citing waning immunity and the risks of Omicron variants. The FDA and CDC recommend these additional shots of Pfizer/BioNTech and Moderna vaccines at least four months after the previous dose to provide more protection against severe disease and hospitalization. This decision comes amidst concerns about the highly contagious BA.2 Omicron subvariant and discussions about a broader booster campaign targeting new variants in the future.

title: Pfizer Is one of the 2022 TIME100 Most Influential Companies | TIME
summary: Pfizer has been recognized as one of TIME's 100 Most Influential Companies of 2022 for its critical role in curbing COVID-19. The company developed a vaccine and later introduced an oral antiviral therapy, Paxlovid, which significantly reduces the risk of hospitalization or death from the virus. Pfizer's contributions have made it a key player in the global fight against the pandemic.

title: Pfizer Is one of the 2022 TIME100 Most Influential Companies
summary: Pfizer has been recognized as one of the 2022 TIME100 Most Influential Companies for its pivotal role in combating COVID-19. The company not only developed a highly effective vaccine but also introduced the first oral antiviral therapy, Paxlovid, which significantly reduces the risk of severe illness, hospitalization, or death. This dual contribution highlights Pfizer's impact on global health during the pandemic.

title: CureVac launches Phase 1 study for next-gen mRNA COVID-19 vaccine
summary: CureVac and GSK have initiated a Phase 1 study for CV2CoV, a next-generation mRNA COVID-19 vaccine candidate. This new vaccine aims to provide broader efficacy against SARS-CoV-2 variants, following disappointing results from CureVac's first-generation vaccine. The study will test doses between 2 and 20µg in up to 210 healthy adults in the U.S.

title: Sanofi API spinout takes step toward market listing
summary: Sanofi is moving forward with the market listing of its drug manufacturing spinout, EUROAPI, on the French stock exchange on May 6. Sanofi will retain a 30% ownership stake, distribute 58% to its shareholders, and a French government fund will own 12%. This restructuring is part of a broader trend among large pharmaceutical companies to focus on branded prescription drugs.

title: The power of mRNA
summary: This article from Moderna explains the science behind mRNA, highlighting its fundamental role in the human body and its potential to revolutionize medicine. It details how mRNA provides instructions for protein synthesis, which is crucial for maintaining health and fighting diseases. The article also describes how mRNA vaccines work, from preparation and delivery to protein creation and eventual degradation without altering DNA.

title: Women Manufacturing Leaders Earn National Recognition
summary: Employees from nine CBIA member companies were recognized in the Manufacturing Institute’s 2022 STEP Ahead Awards, honoring 130 outstanding women in science, technology, engineering, and production fields. The awards also acknowledged emerging leaders, highlighting the industry's need to close both the 800,000 open job gap and the gender gap. This recognition aims to inspire the next generation of female leaders to pursue careers in manufacturing.

title: iRhythm builds case for wearable cardiac monitor with data in fainting, TAVR patients
summary: iRhythm Technologies presented new data at the American College of Cardiology's 71st Annual Scientific Session & Expo, strengthening the clinical case for its Zio wearable cardiac monitoring devices. Studies showcased the Zio AT device's ability to reduce hospital stays for fainting patients and identify arrhythmias more effectively, while the Zio XT device was used for atrial fibrillation screening in older, low-risk patients. Analysts believe these presentations will lead to increased adoption and market expansion for iRhythm's technology, particularly in the underpenetrated asymptomatic monitoring market.

title: Supporting Cambridge’s Life Sciences Ecosystem: Q&A with James Seppala and Tim Schoen
summary: This article features a Q&A with James Seppala (Blackstone) and Tim Schoen (BioMed Realty) discussing the growth of the life sciences industry, particularly in the UK, and BioMed Realty's role. They highlight Cambridge's significance as a hub for innovation due to government investment, private capital, and top-tier universities. The discussion also covers BioMed's portfolio, sustainability efforts, and future growth strategy in the region.

title: Dr. Pieter Cullis named 2022 Canada Gairdner Award laureate
summary: Dr. Pieter Cullis, a professor at UBC Medicine, has been named a 2022 Canada Gairdner International Award laureate for his groundbreaking work on lipid nanoparticle delivery technology. This technology is crucial for mRNA therapeutics, including the COVID-19 mRNA vaccines. The Gairdner Awards are highly prestigious, often precursors to the Nobel Prize, recognizing scientists whose discoveries significantly impact biomedical and global health research.

title: Pfizer boosts respiratory drug portfolio with ReViral purchase
summary: Pfizer Inc. announced its acquisition of ReViral Ltd for up to $525 million, including milestone payments, to enhance its respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) drug pipeline. This marks Pfizer's second major acquisition in under six months, following a $6.7 billion deal for Arena Pharmaceuticals. The acquisition will add ReViral's four RSV therapies, including lead candidate sisunatovir, to Pfizer's portfolio, complementing its late-stage RSV vaccine candidate.

title: Pfizer Takeover Makes Dent in a $32 Billion Stock-Market Slump
summary: Pfizer Inc.'s shares gained 4.3% after announcing the acquisition of ReViral Ltd. for up to $525 million. This gain helped mitigate the drug maker's stock-market slump, which has been impacted by expiring patents and the Covid outlook. Despite the day's rise, Pfizer's stock remained down almost 7% for the year.

title: Vertex CEO Kewalramani nabs more than $15M in 2021 pay, rivaling some male Big Pharma peers
summary: Vertex Pharmaceuticals CEO Reshma Kewalramani earned over $15 million in total compensation in 2021, a 50% increase from the previous year. This pay package positions her compensation favorably against that of several male Big Pharma CEOs. The company praised her leadership for achieving financial goals and expanding its cystic fibrosis business.

title: Cytokinetics Announces Changes to Board of Directors
summary: Cytokinetics (Nasdaq: CYTK) announced changes to its Board of Directors. L. Patrick Gage, Ph.D., will retire as Chairman, and John T. Henderson, M.B., Ch.B. will replace him as Chairman. Additionally, Robert A. Harrington, M.D., Arthur L. Bloomfield Professor and Chair of the Department of Medicine at Stanford University, has been appointed to the Board.

title: US Department of Labor renews ‘Star Level’ designation of Pfizer Andover for workplace safety, health achievements
summary: The US Department of Labor has renewed the "Star Level" designation for Pfizer Andover, recognizing its continued achievements in workplace safety and health. This designation, awarded by OSHA's Voluntary Protection Programs, acknowledges Pfizer Andover's exemplary safety management systems and its consistent commitment to protecting its 1700 employees since 2007. The Andover site, which produces biotherapeutic pharmaceuticals, was evaluated in October 2021 by OSHA experts for its comprehensive hazard assessment and control tools.

title: Pfizer, Moderna name new finance chiefs amid surging revenue
summary: Pfizer and Moderna, two leading COVID-19 vaccine manufacturers, have both appointed new Chief Financial Officers. These new CFOs will manage the substantial revenue generated from their respective COVID-19 vaccines and antiviral treatments. They will be responsible for allocating these funds towards research, strategic acquisitions, and balancing investor expectations with pipeline development, with each company facing unique financial challenges and opportunities.

title: James MacIntosh appointed VP, global sales at Playtex Baby
summary: James MacIntosh has been appointed as the vice president of global sales at Playtex Baby. He brings decades of industry experience from previous roles at companies such as Angelcare, Edgewell Personal Care, Energizer, Pfizer, and Procter & Gamble. The article announces this leadership change in the people news section.

title: Pfizer Appoints David M. Denton as Chief Financial Officer
summary: Pfizer Inc. has announced the appointment of David M. Denton as its new Chief Financial Officer (CFO) and Executive Vice President, effective May 2, 2022. Denton, who previously served as CFO for Lowe’s Companies, Inc. and CVS Health, brings over 25 years of finance and operational expertise, with significant experience in the healthcare sector. He will succeed Frank D’Amelio, who is retiring after a 15-year career with Pfizer.

title: Increased focus on health and sustainability in Novo Nordisk Foundation’s new 2030 plan
summary: The Novo Nordisk Foundation has unveiled its new 2030 plan, emphasizing a strengthened commitment to addressing global societal challenges through increased focus on people's health, sustainability, and boosting Denmark's life science ecosystem. The Foundation plans to increase its international focus and annual grants, expecting to exceed DKK 10 billion (€1.3bn) by 2030. Key areas of focus include preventing and treating cardiometabolic diseases, improving pandemic preparedness, accelerating green transformation in agriculture and food production, and fostering a world-class life sciences environment in Denmark.

title: Pfizer to acquire ReViral and its respiratory syncytial virus therapeutic candidates
summary: Pfizer has announced its acquisition of ReViral, a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing antiviral therapeutics for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). This acquisition aims to advance disease research and development, complementing Pfizer's existing efforts in infectious diseases and its investigational RSV vaccine programs. The deal, valued at up to $525 million, includes ReViral's lead candidate, sisunatovir, which is in Phase 2 clinical development for RSV treatment.

title: Shionogi COVID pill: Investors flee drugmaker on news of birth defect risk
summary: Shionogi & Co. shares plummeted after the drugmaker reported that animal studies of its experimental COVID-19 pill showed it disturbed fetal development. This news, which analysts believe significantly reduces its commercial success potential, raises concerns about its approval despite similar risks with rival COVID-19 treatments for pregnant women. The company's stock experienced its largest intraday decline in over a decade following the report.

title: Halozyme, doubling down on a licensing strategy, buys a drug delivery biotech for nearly $1B
summary: Halozyme Therapeutics, a San Diego-based company known for its drug delivery technology, is acquiring Antares Pharma for nearly $1 billion. This acquisition will expand Halozyme's offerings, particularly with Antares' auto-injector technology, which Halozyme plans to leverage for new licensing deals. The deal is expected to be immediately accretive to Halozyme's revenue, reinforcing its successful licensing-focused business model.

title: John and Pat Hume honoured at 47th annual Business & Finance Awards
summary: The 47th annual Business & Finance Awards honored John and Pat Hume with the TK Whitaker Award for their significant contributions to public life, accepted by their grandchildren. The event also recognized several leading Irish-based companies and individuals across various categories, including Business Person of the Year, Company of the Year, and awards for FDI, Elevation, Diversity, Equality & Inclusion, and ESG. KPMG, as an associate of the awards, praised the resilience, innovation, and ambition demonstrated by the honored companies and their leaders.

title: Halozyme to Acquire Antares Pharma in $960M Deal
summary: Halozyme Therapeutics, Inc. has agreed to acquire Antares Pharma, Inc. for approximately $960 million. This acquisition will create a leading drug delivery and specialty product company, enhancing Halozyme's revenue, cash flow, and long-term growth opportunities. Antares brings a differentiated auto-injector platform and commercial products that will complement Halozyme's ENHANZE platform.

title: PYXS Stock Price and Chart — NASDAQ:PYXS
summary: This article provides a comprehensive overview of Pyxis Oncology, Inc. (PYXS) stock, including its current price, historical performance, key financial stats, upcoming earnings, and analyst consensus. It also details the company's business activities, related ETFs, and answers frequently asked questions about the stock.

title: BeiGene nabs another PD-1 approval in China. Can partner Novartis carry the success to US and Europe?
summary: BeiGene secured another PD-1 approval in China for its antibody tislelizumab in second-line esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC), marking its eighth approval in its home country. This approval follows Novartis's $650 million upfront payment and commitment of $1.55 billion in milestone payments to partner with BeiGene for tislelizumab, after its own PD-1 candidate spartalizumab had limited success. While tislelizumab is under review in the U.S. and Europe for the same indication, it faces steep competition from established drugs like Merck’s Keytruda and BMS’s Opdivo, suggesting pricing strategy may be crucial for market entry outside of China.

title: US Food and Drug Administration accepts New Drug Application for daprodustat
summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has accepted GSK's New Drug Application (NDA) for daprodustat, an oral treatment for anaemia of chronic kidney disease (CKD). This submission is based on positive results from the ASCEND phase III clinical trial programme, which demonstrated the drug's efficacy and safety in both non-dialysis and dialysis patients. Daprodustat is already approved in Japan and is currently under review by the European Medicines Agency.

title: Novavax’s COVID vaccine becomes 4th available for use in Japan
summary: Japan's health ministry officially approved Novavax Inc.'s COVID-19 vaccine, making it the fourth vaccine available in the country. This recombinant protein vaccine offers an alternative for individuals with allergies to mRNA vaccines and can be manufactured domestically. Shipments are expected to begin in May for first, second, or third doses for people aged 18 and older, enhancing Japan's vaccine supply security.

title: BioXcel will use $260M finance deal to expand indications for schizophrenia drug
summary: BioXcel Therapeutics secured a $260 million financing agreement with Oaktree Capital Management and Qatar Investment Authority to accelerate growth and commercially launch their new schizophrenia drug, IGALMI. The funds will also support the expansion of IGALMI's clinical development, including a phase 3 program for Alzheimer's agitation, and other neuroscience and immuno-oncology programs, providing the company with a cash runway into 2025. This deal positions BioXcel to realize its vision of becoming a leading AI-enabled neuroscience company.

title: Mayor Adams and Attorney General James Fight Opioid Crisis With First of $286 Million in Payments for New York City
summary: New York City Mayor Eric Adams and Attorney General Letitia James announced the first installment of $286 million in payments to combat the opioid crisis in New York City. The city will receive $88.9 million this year, with $11.5 million already distributed, to fund opioid prevention and treatment programs across all five boroughs. These funds are part of approximately $1.5 billion secured by Attorney General James from historic settlements with opioid manufacturers and distributors, addressing record overdose rates in the city.

title: A psychedelic pill for alcoholism? The CEO of Clearmind Medicine says ‘Yes.’
summary: Clearmind Medicine CEO Adi Zuloff-Shani is optimistic about MEAI, a psychoactive compound being developed into CMND-100 for alcohol use disorder and other binge behaviors. The company has raised $9.4 million CAD and completed successful preclinical trials on mice, showing reduced alcohol consumption. Clearmind is preparing to meet with the FDA, believing psychedelics offer a promising solution to the unmet need in mental health treatments.

title: WHO backs Pfizer's oral COVID therapy for high-risk patients
summary: The World Health Organization (WHO) has recommended Pfizer's oral COVID-19 antiviral treatment, Paxlovid, for high-risk patients, citing its effectiveness in reducing hospitalization risk by 85%. While acknowledging its potency, the WHO highlighted challenges to widespread adoption, including the need for early testing, potential drug interactions, and limited data for certain populations. The organization also updated its recommendation for Gilead's remdesivir, suggesting its use for mild or moderate COVID-19 patients at high risk of hospitalization.

title: Dr Reddys unveils Posaconazole delayed-release tablets in US
summary: Dr. Reddy's Laboratories has launched Posaconazole Delayed-Release Tablets, 100 mg, in the U.S. market. This generic equivalent to NOXAFIL is an azole antifungal indicated for the prophylaxis of invasive Aspergillus and Candida infections in severely immunocompromised patients. The NOXAFIL brand and its generic had U.S. sales of approximately $140.8 million MAT for the twelve months ending February 2022.

title: Pfizer Paxlovid Covid Pill Will Soon Be Available Across the U.S.
summary: The U.S. government is finalizing plans to make Pfizer Inc.'s Covid-19 pill, Paxlovid, available at any pharmacy nationwide as supplies increase. This initiative comes as the BA.2 sub-variant leads to a rise in Covid-19 cases and hospitalizations. President Biden is expected to announce a plan to boost awareness and access to the drug.

title: Pfizer recalls Accupril tablets due to presence of cancer-causing impurity
summary: Pfizer is voluntarily recalling five lots of its blood pressure drug, Accupril tablets, after recent testing revealed elevated levels of N-nitroso-quinapril, a potential cancer-causing impurity, above the Acceptable Daily Intake level. The recalled products were distributed nationwide between December 2019 and April 2022, but Pfizer states no adverse reports have been received and there is no immediate risk to patients. Patients are advised to consult their doctors and can contact Sedgwick for return and reimbursement information.

title: Zentalis Pharmaceuticals Announces $25 Million Equity Investment from Pfizer
summary: Zentalis Pharmaceuticals announced a $25 million equity investment from Pfizer through the sale of common shares. This investment, along with budget reallocation, extends Zentalis' cash runway into Q1 2024 and supports the clinical development of their Wee1 inhibitor, ZN-c3, and BCL-2 inhibitor, ZN-d5. Pfizer will also collaborate on the clinical advancement of ZN-c3 and have a representative join Zentalis' Scientific Advisory Board.

title: Spying synthetic lethal promise, Pfizer bets $25M on Zentalis, will support cancer trials
summary: Pfizer has invested $25 million in Zentalis Pharmaceuticals to support the clinical development of its synthetic lethality candidate, ZN-c3. The investment involves Pfizer buying nearly 1 million Zentalis shares and collaborating on clinical trials for ZN-c3 in solid tumors and ZN-d5 in blood cancers, extending Zentalis' cash runway into 2024. This partnership leverages Pfizer's oncology expertise and continues its strategy of investing in biotechs with programs of strategic interest.

title: Pfizer and Biohaven’s VYDURA® (Rimegepant) Granted First Ever Marketing Authorization by European Commission for Both Acute Treatment of Migraine and Prophylaxis of Episodic Migraine
summary: The European Commission has granted marketing authorization for VYDURA® (rimegepant) to Pfizer Inc. and Biohaven Pharmaceutical Holding Company Ltd. This approval makes VYDURA® the first medicine in the EU to be approved for both acute treatment and prophylaxis of episodic migraine in adults. The drug targets CGRP receptors, offering significant relief and reduced migraine attacks, representing a major advancement in migraine treatment for European patients.

title: COVID-19 Vaccine for Kids: Moderna seeks emergency use authorization for Covid-19 vaccine for children ages 6 months to 5 years
summary: Moderna has submitted an emergency use authorization request to the FDA for its Covid-19 vaccine for children aged 6 months through 5 years. The company's clinical trial results showed a robust neutralizing antibody response and a favorable safety profile with two 25-microgram doses, demonstrating efficacy against symptomatic Covid-19. This development comes as Pfizer/BioNTech also awaits FDA review for its vaccine for young children and is testing booster doses for older children.

title: Watkins Advises Zentalis Pharmaceuticals on US$25 Million Equity Investment from Pfizer
summary: Latham & Watkins advised Zentalis Pharmaceuticals on a US$25 million equity investment from Pfizer, which purchased 953,834 common shares at US$26.21 per share in a direct offering. The proceeds will fund clinical trials and general corporate purposes. Additionally, the companies will collaborate to advance the clinical development of ZN-c3, a selective Wee1 inhibitor.

title: Merck raises 2022 forecast as COVID pill, cancer drug fuels profit beat
summary: Merck & Co reported stronger-than-expected quarterly profit and sales, raising its full-year forecasts due to robust demand for its cancer drug Keytruda, Gardasil vaccine, and the COVID-19 antiviral pill molnupiravir. The company's shares increased, and revenue surged 50% to $15.9 billion, primarily driven by molnupiravir sales. Despite some waning enthusiasm for molnupiravir's efficacy, strong sales across its key products contributed to the optimistic outlook and potential acquisition plans before Keytruda's patent expiration.

title: Pfizer says COVID treatment Paxlovid fails to prevent infection of household members
summary: Pfizer announced that its COVID-19 antiviral treatment Paxlovid was not effective in preventing coronavirus infection among household members exposed to an infected individual. A large trial involving 3,000 adults showed that while those taking Paxlovid were less likely to get infected, the results were not statistically significant. Despite this outcome, Pfizer reiterated the strong efficacy of Paxlovid in treating high-risk COVID-19 patients, as demonstrated in earlier trials, and projects $24 billion in sales for the drug this year.

title: SK bioscience and GSK’s adjuvanted COVID-19 vaccine candidate meets coprimary objectives in a phase III study; Biologics License Application submitted for SKYCovione™(GBP510/GSK adjuvant) in South Korea
summary: SK bioscience and GSK announced that their adjuvanted COVID-19 vaccine candidate, SKYCovione™, met its coprimary objectives in a Phase III study, demonstrating superior neutralizing antibody titres compared to AstraZeneca's Vaxzevria™ and a clinically favorable safety profile. Following these positive results, SK bioscience has submitted a biologics license application to the Korean Ministry of Food and Drug Safety. The companies also plan to apply for emergency use listing with the WHO and authorizations globally, with an advanced purchase agreement already in place with the Korea CDC for 10 million doses.

title: Novo Nordisk’s Pinder Sahota appointed President of the ABPI
summary: Pinder Sahota, General Manager and Corporate Vice President of Novo Nordisk UK, has been appointed as the new President of the Association of the British Pharmaceutical Industry (ABPI). He will focus on ensuring that innovative medicines reach patients and supporting the NHS, building on his previous roles including Chair of the CBI’s Health Council. Sahota emphasized the importance of medicines and vaccines and the opportunity for the UK to leverage its scientific excellence to improve healthcare.

title: Pfizer’s Covid-19 Pill Failed Study Testing Its Preventive Use
summary: Pfizer's Covid-19 pill, Paxlovid, failed a late-stage study designed to test its effectiveness in preventing symptomatic infections in adults exposed to the virus. The drug, which is authorized for early treatment of high-risk individuals, did not significantly reduce the risk of confirmed and symptomatic Covid-19 in household contacts. This finding indicates that Paxlovid may not be suitable for pre-exposure prophylaxis.

title: Innovator Spotlight: How biosimilars can fuel a health care revolution
summary: Sonia T. Oskouei, Vice President of Biosimilars at Cardinal Health, discusses the transformative potential of biosimilars in healthcare. She highlights how these medications drive competition, lower costs, increase patient access to critical treatments, and free up funds for future healthcare innovations. The article also provides a progress report on biosimilars in 2021, detailing key approvals and regulatory activities that are expanding their reach and impact.

title: Pfizer’s Covid Drug Fails to Show Benefit as Preventive Therapy
summary: Pfizer's Covid-19 antiviral drug, Paxlovid, failed to meet its primary goal in a late-stage study designed to test its effectiveness as a preventive treatment. The study aimed to see if Paxlovid could significantly reduce the risk of Covid-19 infection in adults exposed to the virus through household contact. While it reduced risks by about a third compared to a placebo, this result did not achieve statistical significance.

title: ABBV CLASS ACTION: Kessler Topaz Meltzer & Check, LLP Reminds AbbVie, Inc. Shareholders of Securities Fraud Class Action Lawsuit
summary: Kessler Topaz Meltzer & Check, LLP has filed a securities class action lawsuit against AbbVie, Inc. (NYSE: ABBV) on behalf of investors who purchased shares between April 30, 2021, and August 31, 2021. The lawsuit alleges that AbbVie made misleading statements regarding the safety of its drug Rinvoq, particularly concerning its similarities to Pfizer's Xeljanz and potential regulatory risks. Investors suffered losses after the FDA delayed reviews and later mandated stronger warnings for Rinvoq due to serious side effects observed with JAK inhibitors.

title: Sema4 Acquires GeneDx
summary: Sema4 (Nasdaq: SMFR), an AI-driven genomic and clinical data intelligence platform company, announced its acquisition of GeneDx, LLC, a leader in genomic testing for rare disorders, from OPKO Health, Inc. (Nasdaq: OPK). This acquisition positions Sema4 as a prominent provider of genomic testing in the U.S., enhancing its health information database and accelerating precision medicine efforts. Katherine Stueland, former President and CEO of GeneDx, will now lead Sema4 as CEO.

title: PFE Earnings: All you need to know about Pfizer’s Q1 2022 earnings results
summary: Pfizer Inc. reported strong first-quarter 2022 earnings, with total revenues increasing by 77% year-over-year to $25.7 billion. Both reported and adjusted EPS also saw significant growth, beating analyst estimates. For the full year 2022, Pfizer anticipates revenues between $98-102 billion and adjusted EPS of $6.25-6.45.

title: Pfizer keeps 2022 COVID-19 vaccine, pill sales outlook unchanged
summary: Pfizer maintained its 2022 sales outlook for its COVID-19 vaccine, Comirnaty ($32 billion), and antiviral pill, Paxlovid ($22 billion), disappointing investors who anticipated increased projections. The company's shares fluctuated as its Covid-fighting products already account for a significant portion of its total revenue, despite concerns about tapering demand. Pfizer plans further studies and regulatory submissions for its products to expand their market and address investor anxieties about growth.

title: Pfizer Sales Soar on Covid-19 Vaccine Sales
summary: Pfizer's sales have significantly increased due to demand for its Covid-19 vaccine and antiviral pill, Paxlovid. The company expects continued high demand as governments replenish supplies and combat evolving virus strains. In the first quarter, Paxlovid generated $1.5 billion in sales, while the vaccine brought in $13.2 billion.

title: Nonstimulant ADHD Treatment Option Approved for Adults
summary: The FDA has approved Qelbree (viloxazine extended-release) for the treatment of ADHD in adults aged 18 and older, expanding its previous approval for pediatric patients. This nonstimulant treatment's approval is based on a phase 3 trial showing significant reduction in ADHD symptoms compared to placebo. Qelbree carries a Boxed Warning for suicidal thoughts and behavior, and patients should be screened for relevant history before starting treatment.

title: Pfizer sees strong demand for COVID pill as profits surge
summary: Pfizer anticipates strong demand for its COVID-19 antiviral treatment, Paxlovid, as pandemic restrictions ease, even as the company reported a significant increase in first-quarter profits driven by its vaccine sales. CEO Albert Bourla also highlighted efforts to develop a longer-lasting COVID-19 vaccine booster. The company forecasts full-year revenues of about $100 billion, with more than half expected from its COVID-19 vaccine and therapeutic, and expects $22 billion in Paxlovid sales for 2022.

title: Takeda spinout Phathom clinches FDA twin nods for GI infection combos—plus timely capital infusion
summary: Phathom Pharmaceuticals, a Takeda spinout, has received FDA approval for two vonoprazan-based combinations, Voquezna Dual Pak and Voquezna Triple Pak, to treat Helicobacter pylori infection. These approvals are accompanied by a financing deal of up to $260 million to support the drug's launch and further development, including for non-erosive reflux disease. Analysts project significant peak sales due to the drug's efficacy and extended market exclusivity.

title: Moderna sees higher COVID vaccine sales later this year
summary: Moderna forecasts higher COVID-19 vaccine sales in the second half of the year, expecting the virus to become seasonal and require fall booster shots. The company is developing a next-generation booster targeting both Omicron and the original strain. Moderna projects $21 billion in 2022 vaccine sales, potentially higher if more countries contract for fall doses, but cautioned sales could be lower if the COVAX program faces demand issues.

title: FDA limits use of Johnson & Johnson’s Covid-19 vaccine, citing clotting risk
summary: The FDA has limited the use of Johnson & Johnson's single-dose Covid-19 vaccine due to a rare but serious blood clotting disorder, TTS, which has been linked to nine deaths in the U.S. The vaccine will now only be available to adults 18 and older who cannot receive or decline mRNA vaccines. The decision reflects the FDA's caution given the availability of effective alternative vaccines with lower risks, though the practical impact in the U.S. is expected to be minimal due to already low demand and stock of the J&J vaccine.

title: Evidence mounts for need to study Pfizer's Paxlovid for long COVID - researchers say
summary: New case studies suggest Pfizer's oral antiviral treatment, Paxlovid, may be beneficial for long COVID patients, prompting researchers to call for clinical trials. While not definitive, these observations provide a strong rationale for systematic studies, including randomized trials, to investigate Paxlovid's potential to treat this debilitating condition. Pfizer, however, currently has no long COVID studies underway.

title: FDA puts strict limits on Johnson & Johnson Covid-19 vaccine
summary: The FDA has limited the emergency use authorization for the Johnson & Johnson/Janssen Covid-19 vaccine to individuals 18 and older for whom other vaccines are not appropriate or accessible, or for those who would otherwise remain unvaccinated. This decision was made due to the rare but dangerous risk of thrombosis with thrombocytopenia syndrome (TTS) associated with the vaccine. Despite the limitations, the FDA maintains that the vaccine still has a role in the pandemic response for specific populations where the benefits outweigh the risks.

title: FDA limits J&J COVID-19 vaccine use to certain adults
summary: The FDA has revised its emergency use authorization for the Johnson & Johnson COVID-19 vaccine, limiting its use to adults 18 and older who cannot access or are not clinically appropriate for other vaccines, or who choose it otherwise. This decision was based on an updated analysis of the risk of thrombosis with thrombocytopenia syndrome (TTS), a rare but potentially life-threatening blood clotting condition. The agency determined that this risk warrants restrictions on the vaccine's authorized use.

title: FDA PLACES NEW RESTRICTIONS ON JOHNSON & JOHNSON’S COVID-19 VACCINE
summary: The FDA has placed new restrictions on Johnson & Johnson's COVID-19 vaccine, limiting its emergency use authorization to individuals 18 and older for whom other vaccines are not appropriate or accessible, or who would otherwise remain unvaccinated. This decision is due to the rare risk of thrombosis with thrombocytopenia syndrome (TTS), a dangerous clotting condition. Despite this, the FDA maintains that the vaccine's benefits still outweigh its risks for certain populations.

title: COVID vaccine makers shift focus to boosters
summary: COVID-19 vaccine manufacturers like Pfizer and Moderna are shifting their strategy to focus on the booster shot market, recognizing that most people who desired initial vaccinations have already received them. While overall demand for COVID-19 vaccines is projected to decline, these companies anticipate a competitive market centered on booster doses for vulnerable populations and potentially annual reformulated shots to combat new strains. Companies like Johnson & Johnson and AstraZeneca are expected to see a reduced role in this evolving market due to lower efficacy or side effect concerns.

title: Informa Connect’s Hub and Specialty Pharmacy Models East
summary: Informa Connect is hosting its Hub and Specialty Pharmacy Models East event as a hybrid conference from June 28-30, 2022, in Parsippany, NJ. The event will gather key stakeholders from manufacturers, specialty pharmacies, and hub providers to discuss innovative strategies for optimizing patient access and enhancing hub effectiveness. Attendees can choose from two content streams and several breakout sessions, and will have the opportunity for shared learning with the co-located PAP – Patient Assistance & Access Programs event.

title: Pfizer to spend $11.6B on migraine treatment maker Biohaven
summary: Pfizer announced it will acquire Biohaven Pharmaceuticals for $11.6 billion, expanding its presence in the migraine treatment market. This move allows Pfizer to leverage its significant cash reserves from COVID-19 vaccine sales to diversify its portfolio, especially as patent protections for existing key drugs are set to expire. The acquisition includes Nurtec ODT and other migraine treatments, with Biohaven's remaining pipeline forming a new publicly traded company.

title: Pfizer to Acquire Biohaven Pharmaceuticals
summary: Pfizer Inc. is set to acquire Biohaven Pharmaceutical Holding Company Ltd. for approximately $11.6 billion in cash, expanding its portfolio with Biohaven's CGRP migraine programs, including the approved NURTEC ODT. Biohaven shareholders will also receive shares in a new publicly traded company, "New Biohaven," which will retain Biohaven's non-CGRP development pipeline. This acquisition aims to leverage Pfizer's global capabilities to maximize the reach of Biohaven's innovative migraine therapies.

title: Pfizer to Acquire Biohaven Pharmaceuticals
summary: Pfizer is set to acquire Biohaven Pharmaceuticals for approximately $11.6 billion in cash, significantly expanding its Internal Medicine pipeline with Biohaven's CGRP programs including NURTEC ODT for migraine. Biohaven shareholders will receive $148.50 per share in cash and 0.5 shares of a new publicly traded company, "New Biohaven," which will retain Biohaven's non-CGRP pipeline compounds. This acquisition builds on a previous collaboration and aims to enhance Pfizer's growth through 2030 and beyond, leveraging NURTEC ODT's market leadership.

title: Pfizer’s Biohaven Deal May Open an Era of Smarter Pharma Acquisitions
summary: Pfizer's acquisition of Biohaven Pharmaceutical for $11.6 billion, a company specializing in migraine treatments, is seen as a positive development for the struggling biotech sector. The deal allows Pfizer to utilize its Covid-19 cash effectively by acquiring an oral drug already on the market and a nasal spray nearing commercialization. This acquisition is anticipated to be a harbinger of increased M&A activity in the biotech industry.

title: Pfizer to acquire Biohaven in $11.6B bet on biotech’s migraine drugs
summary: Pfizer is set to acquire Biohaven Pharmaceuticals for $11.6 billion, gaining full rights to the migraine drug Nurtec ODT and other migraine-related assets. The deal represents a significant bet on the future growth of oral CGRP antagonists for migraines, with Pfizer planning to expand sales efforts for Nurtec ODT. Biohaven's non-migraine assets will be spun out into a new company, retaining Biohaven's name and led by its current CEO.

title: Pfizer to Buy Rest of Biohaven for $11.6 Billion - WSJ
summary: Pfizer Inc. has agreed to acquire the remaining shares of Biohaven Pharmaceutical Holding Co. for approximately $11.6 billion, utilizing cash from its Covid-19 vaccine sales. This move will give Pfizer full ownership of Biohaven's Nurtec migraine drug franchise. The acquisition price of $148.50 per share represents a nearly 79% premium over Biohaven's closing price on the Monday prior to the announcement.

title: Pfizer to pay $11.6 bln for Biohaven to tap migraine market
summary: Pfizer Inc announced its acquisition of Biohaven Pharmaceutical Holding Co for $11.6 billion, aiming to bolster its presence in the migraine drug market with Biohaven's Nurtec ODT and other developing migraine treatments. The deal, approved by both companies' boards, is Pfizer's largest since 2016 and is expected to significantly increase its annual sales through the migraine franchise. Pfizer plans to double Nurtec's sales force and spin off Biohaven's non-migraine drugs into a new publicly traded company.

title: Moderna CFO Jorge Gomez exits after one day as old company launches probe
summary: Moderna's new CFO, Jorge Gomez, resigned after just one day on the job due to an internal investigation launched by his former employer, Dentsply Sirona, into financial reporting matters. Gomez will receive a year's salary of $700,000 but forfeits his signing bonus and equity awards. Retired CFO David Meline will return to Moderna temporarily.

title: Biohaven (BHVN) Up on PFE's Buyout Offer, Q1 Loss Wider
summary: Pfizer announced an agreement to acquire Biohaven for $148.50 per share, totaling $11.6 billion, primarily for Biohaven's CGRP migraine programs, including Nurtec ODT. This acquisition represents a 78.6% premium to Biohaven's previous closing price. Concurrently, Biohaven reported a wider-than-expected Q1 2022 loss, despite a significant increase in total revenues, largely driven by Nurtec ODT sales and collaboration revenues from Pfizer.

title: Moderna CFO exits abruptly amid probe at former company
summary: Moderna's newly appointed CFO, Jorge Gomez, abruptly departed the company after just one day, following a public disclosure by his former employer, Dentsply Sirona, of an internal investigation into financial reporting matters. Gomez will receive 12 months' salary and COBRA coverage as severance but forfeits other new-hire benefits. Moderna's former CFO, David Meline, will return to the role while the company searches for a new finance chief.

title: Explainer: Some patients reporting COVID rebounds after taking Pfizer pills
summary: Some patients have reported a recurrence of COVID-19 symptoms after completing treatment with Pfizer's antiviral pill, Paxlovid, despite initial improvement. While Pfizer suggests these "rebounds" are rare, the cause is still unknown, with theories ranging from muted immune responses to inherent viral characteristics. The U.S. FDA currently advises against a second course of Paxlovid for rebounds, though Pfizer's CEO has suggested it could be beneficial for some patients.

title: Rheumatoid Arthritis Treatment Market 2022 Global Projection
summary: The global Rheumatoid Arthritis Treatment Market is projected to reach US$ 40.5 billion by 2022 and expects a CAGR of 6% over the forecast period (2021-2031). The growth is driven by increasing RA prevalence, R&D for better therapies, and strategic collaborations among market players. DMARDs hold the largest value share, and North America leads the market.

title: Amgen Inc. stock falls Friday, underperforms market
summary: Amgen Inc. (AMGN) stock fell 0.54% on Friday, closing at $243.40 and underperforming broader market gains seen by the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average. The company's stock finished $15.05 below its 52-week high and showed mixed performance against competitors like Johnson & Johnson, Roche Holding AG, and Pfizer Inc. Trading volume was also below its 50-day average.

title: Sanofi ordered by French court to compensate for epilepsy drug side effect: report
summary: A French court has ordered Sanofi to pay over 400,000 euros to a family whose child developed autism, linking it to the epilepsy drug valproate (Depakine). The court found that Sanofi failed to adequately warn consumers about the drug's risks, an accusation the company denies and plans to appeal. This ruling is the first in France to directly connect the drug to autism in an individual patient case, following previous estimates of thousands of physical and neuro-developmental defects caused by the medication.

title: Explore partnering with Sanofi’s vaccines business
summary: Sanofi's vaccines business is actively seeking collaborations with partners who share its commitment to innovation and excellence in vaccine development and production. They are looking for technologies related to human vaccines, both prophylactic and therapeutic, including those for chronic infectious diseases. The company emphasizes its strong track record of successful partnerships and its focus on expanding immunization across all age groups.

title: UPDATE: Pfizer, Sarepta team with fellow DMD gene therapy makers to get to the bottom of adverse events
summary: Pfizer, Sarepta, Genethon, and Solid Biosciences have collaborated on a pooled safety analysis of Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) gene therapies after multiple patients experienced similar serious adverse events. The analysis, presented at the American Society of Gene and Cell Therapy meeting, identified a likely class effect involving a T-cell-mediated immune response to a specific region of the mini-/micro-dystrophin, exacerbated by certain patient genotypes. The companies are continuing their investigation to better understand these immune mechanisms and risk factors to improve future gene therapy studies for DMD.

title: Scientists home in on cause of Duchenne gene therapy side effect
summary: An unusual collaboration between competing gene therapy developers for Duchenne muscular dystrophy has identified a potential cause for a worrisome side effect observed in clinical trials. Patients who experienced accelerated muscle weakness shared similar genetic mutations that triggered an immune response to the therapy's genetic material, a "class effect" across similar treatments. Companies are now excluding patients with these mutations and increasing monitoring in trials.

title: Jumping into pharma with big plans at a small company
summary: This article profiles Jim Cassidy, Chief Medical Officer at SpringWorks Therapeutics, detailing his transition from a career as an academic physician and scientist to the pharmaceutical industry at age 50. It highlights his ambition and the company's focus on rare tumors and other cancers, discussing their lead programs nirogacestat and mirdametinib, and the advantages of working in a smaller, agile company to achieve significant medical advancements. Cassidy emphasizes the speed and direct impact possible in a smaller biotech setting compared to large pharmaceutical corporations.

title: As COVID cases rise, U.S. health officials mull widening additional booster eligibility
summary: U.S. health officials are considering expanding eligibility for a second COVID-19 vaccine booster dose to individuals under 50, amidst a significant increase in COVID-19 cases in the United States. Dr. Rochelle Walensky of the CDC stated that daily cases have risen threefold over the past month, with a concurrent increase in hospitalizations. The FDA had previously authorized booster doses for those 50 and older.

title: Global Process Analytical Technology (PAT) Market Growth Set to Rise Significantly of USD 7.19 billion by 2027 : Fior Markets
summary: The global Process Analytical Technology (PAT) market is projected to grow from USD 2.59 billion in 2019 to USD 7.19 billion by 2027, exhibiting a CAGR of 13.6% from 2020-2027. North America is expected to lead this growth due to a strong pharmaceutical industry and stringent government regulations. Key market segments include products (analyzers, probes, sensors) and services, with spectroscopy dominating techniques due to its broad application in pharmaceuticals.

title: Collaborative Analysis Reveals "Class Effect" in DMD Safety Issues
summary: Four companies—Pfizer, Sarepta Therapeutics, Genethon, and Solid Biosciences—are collaborating to investigate serious side effects observed in their Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD) gene therapy trials. They presented data suggesting a "class effect" due to a T-cell mediated immune response to the expressed transgene protein in CRIM-negative patients, primarily those with specific genomic deletions. This collaboration aims to understand and mitigate these risks in DMD gene therapy development.

title: Medication Shortages Imperil Hospice Access, Quality
summary: Nationwide drug shortages, particularly of essential pain and symptom management medications, are making it difficult for hospice providers to access necessary drugs, threatening quality of care and patient access to hospice services. These shortages are increasing in number and duration, driving up costs for providers, and exacerbating the challenges faced by hospice settings that require medications quickly. Industry experts point to factors like the pharmaceutical industry's complexity, reliance on single suppliers, and generic manufacturer consolidation as key contributors to the ongoing crisis, necessitating collaborative efforts and advocacy for solutions.

title: Is Pfizer Inc (PFE) A Great Value Stock?
summary: This article evaluates Pfizer Inc (PFE) as a potential value stock based on its improved performance metrics. It highlights Pfizer's position as one of the world's largest pharmaceutical firms and presents several financial metrics from The Acquirer's Multiple framework that suggest PFE could be undervalued.

title: Bayer backs out of Atara cell therapy deal
summary: Bayer will terminate its research collaboration deal with Atara Biotherapeutics, which focused on developing cancer cell therapies. Atara will regain the rights to the two CAR-T therapies in September, which had targeted mesothelin; a patient death in a study for one of these therapies previously led to a pause in enrollment. Bayer stated that the decision was made after a review of its pharmaceutical development projects to ensure resources are focused on assets with the most potential.

title: Pfizer Inc. stock rises Friday, outperforms market
summary: Pfizer Inc. (PFE) saw its stock rise by 3.59% on Friday, closing at $52.47 and outperforming the broader market. The S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average also experienced slight gains on the same day. Pfizer's stock reached its second consecutive day of gains, bringing it closer to its 52-week high.

title: AG Brnovich Obtains Over $90,000 In Restitution from Pfizer for Deceptive Advertising
summary: Arizona Attorney General Mark Brnovich announced a consent judgment with Pfizer Inc., obtaining over $90,000 in restitution for consumers due to deceptive advertising of its copayment coupon program. The investigation found that Pfizer's coupons, which stated consumers would "pay no more than" a certain amount, often led to higher out-of-pocket costs due to undisclosed limits. As a result, Pfizer will pay restitution to over 1,600 consumers, $30,000 to the state, and must cease using the "pay no more than" language in its marketing materials.

title: An unseen cost of the Ukraine war: Delays in potentially life-saving medical research
summary: The war in Ukraine has caused significant disruptions to potentially life-saving medical research, as the country was a global hub for clinical trials. Nearly 200 attacks on medical facilities shattered Ukraine’s healthcare infrastructure, leading to hundreds of crucial studies being abandoned or delayed. This has resulted in a critical slowdown in bringing new medicines to market, with global pharmaceutical companies like Pfizer and AstraZeneca pausing recruitment and facing immense challenges in continuing existing trials amidst the conflict.

title: Elicio Touts "Huge Potential" for Cancer Vaccine Following Preclinical Data
summary: Elicio Therapeutics has published promising preclinical data for its cancer vaccine, utilizing its proprietary Amphiphile (AMP) platform to deliver immunotherapeutics directly into lymph nodes. The company believes this platform has broad potential for cancer and infectious diseases, and its lead AMP vaccine, ELI-002, is currently in a Phase I/II clinical trial for KRAS-driven solid tumors. Elicio also recently partnered with Regeneron Pharmaceuticals to test ELI-002 in combination with Libtayo for KRAS-driven tumors.

title: Pfizer ulcerative colitis drug leads to remission in a third of patients -study
summary: Pfizer's experimental ulcerative colitis drug, etrasimod, led to clinical remission in nearly one-third of patients after a year of treatment in a clinical trial. The drug, acquired through a $6.7 billion deal for Arena Pharmaceuticals, is slated for U.S. approval seeking later this year and could generate over $3 billion in annual peak sales. Etrasimod, an S1P receptor modulator, would compete with Bristol Myers Squibb's Zeposia if approved.

title: Takeda and Daiichi Sankyo collaborate to create wearable device
summary: Takeda and Daiichi Sankyo are partnering with Tohoku University and MICIN to develop a wearable device for tracking lifestyle habits. The year-long study will involve 2,000 participants and aim to gather data on activity levels, heart rate, and sleep routines to contribute to personalized healthcare and new medical technologies. This project builds on data from Tohoku's Medical Megabank Project and a pilot study, with participants using a smartphone app, blood pressure monitor, and thermo-hygrometer.

title: Cibinqo From Pfizer Inc
summary: The FDA has approved abrocitinib tablets (Cibinqo; Pfizer) for the treatment of moderate-to-severe, refractory atopic dermatitis in adults. The article details the drug's pharmacology, dosage, administration, and efficacy based on phase 3 clinical trials (JADE MONO-1, JADE MONO-2, JADE COMPARE). It also highlights important contraindications, warnings, and precautions including a boxed warning regarding risks such as serious infections and cardiovascular events.

title: Pfizer says it will slash drug prices for the poorest nations. But the devil is in the details
summary: Pfizer plans to sell its entire portfolio of brand-name drugs at cost in up to 45 lower-income countries, starting with five African nations. This ambitious program aims to address non-infectious diseases like cancer and cardiovascular conditions in regions often overlooked. However, the success of the initiative hinges on overcoming significant challenges, including improving local health systems and ensuring drugs reach patients, amidst concerns about the high cost of even "at-cost" medicines for very poor nations.

title: $85K+ headed to Kansans after Pfizer settles deceptive marketing practice case
summary: Pfizer will pay over $85,000 in restitution to Kansas consumers after settling a case regarding deceptive marketing practices in its copayment coupon program for several products. Kansas Attorney General Derek Schmidt announced the settlement, stating that Pfizer's coupons promised consumers would pay "no more than $15 or $20" without adequately disclosing limits on total savings. The company has since updated the language on its coupons, and eligible Kansans will be contacted directly by Pfizer for restitution payments.

title: U.S. doctors reconsider Pfizer's Paxlovid for lower-risk COVID patients
summary: U.S. doctors are re-evaluating the use of Pfizer's COVID-19 antiviral Paxlovid for lower-risk patients due to concerns about symptom recurrence and the need for a second isolation period. While Paxlovid use has surged, driven by government promotion, reports of rebound symptoms have led the CDC to advise renewed isolation. Despite Pfizer stating that rebound is uncommon and not uniquely associated with Paxlovid, some doctors are now reserving it for high-risk individuals, especially those unvaccinated, boosted, or with significant health conditions, questioning its broad utility in a vaccinated and previously infected population.

title: Net Zero by 2040: How Pfizer is Fighting Climate Change with Ambitious Science Based Goals
summary: Pfizer announced its commitment to achieve Net Zero by 2040, a decade ahead of the standard's expectations, building on its earlier goal to be carbon neutral by 2030. The company emphasizes environmental sustainability due to its impact on public health and aims to reduce emissions throughout its value chain, including urging suppliers to adopt science-aligned reduction targets. Pfizer is also working towards 100% renewable electricity by 2030, with a significant virtual power purchase agreement already in place for North America.

title: How the next generation of immuno-oncology could help us get ahead of cancer
summary: This article discusses the potential of next-generation immuno-oncology to transform cancer treatment. It highlights how manipulating the immune system, specifically T and NK cells and their checkpoints, can improve outcomes for various cancer types. The article also introduces GSK's research into the CD226 axis and its portfolio of antibodies targeting specific checkpoints, aiming to enable the immune system to fight cancer more effectively.

title: Paxlovid Becomes Household Name for Covid-19 Patients
summary: Pfizer's antiviral drug, Paxlovid, has become the leading Covid-19 treatment in the U.S., with over 412,000 prescriptions. It has surpassed Merck's molnupiravir, which had around 110,000 prescriptions. Both drugs were approved by the FDA for high-risk individuals to prevent hospitalization, but Paxlovid demonstrated higher efficacy and improved supply.

title: BMS, Novartis and Roche Score New Approvals for Key Drugs
summary: Bristol Myers Squibb's Opdivo (nivolumab), Novartis's Kymriah (tisagenlecleucel), and Roche's Evrysdi (risdiplam) each received new FDA approvals for expanded indications. Opdivo was approved as a first-line therapy for esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, Kymriah for relapsed or refractory follicular lymphoma, and Evrysdi's label was extended to include pre-symptomatic infants with spinal muscular atrophy. These approvals provide new treatment options for patients across various serious conditions, demonstrating continued advancements in pharmaceutical development.

title: GSK to acquire clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company Affinivax, Inc.
summary: GSK has announced its definitive agreement to acquire Affinivax, a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company, for an upfront payment of $2.1 billion and up to $1.2 billion in potential development milestones. This acquisition aims to strengthen GSK's vaccines R&D pipeline by incorporating Affinivax's novel Multiple Antigen Presenting System (MAPS) technology, particularly its next-generation 24-valent pneumococcal vaccine candidate which is in phase II development and has received Breakthrough Therapy designation. The deal is expected to close in the third quarter of 2022, supporting GSK's medium-term outlook.

title: Pfizer to exit GSK consumer health joint venture after spinoff
summary: Pfizer plans to sell its 32% stake in the consumer health joint venture with GlaxoSmithKline after it spins off into a new standalone corporation called Haleon. GSK will contribute at least 80% of its 68% holding to Haleon, which is set to begin trading on the London Stock Exchange on July 18. Both companies aim to focus on vaccines and new medicine development, with Pfizer exiting in a "disciplined manner" to maximize shareholder value.

title: Pfizer to Sell Stake in Haleon
summary: Pfizer Inc. announced its intention to sell its 32% stake in Haleon PLC, a consumer healthcare joint venture with GSK plc, once Haleon lists on the London Stock Exchange in July. The sale will be executed in a "disciplined manner" to maximize shareholder value for Pfizer while avoiding destabilizing Haleon's shares. This move reflects Pfizer's strategic shift towards innovative medicines and vaccines, with vaccines contributing significantly to its Q1 2022 revenue.

title: Regulus Appoints Amin Kamel, Ph.D., as Vice President, DMPK
summary: Regulus Therapeutics Inc. has appointed Amin Kamel, Ph.D., as Vice President, DMPK. Dr. Kamel will support the clinical development of the company's lead candidate, RGLS8429, for autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD). His appointment includes an option to purchase 200,000 shares of Regulus' common stock, vesting over four years.

title: Moderna delays COVID vaccine deliveries to EU by several months
summary: Moderna Inc. has agreed to delay some COVID-19 vaccine deliveries to the European Union by several months, pushing them to late 2022 or early 2023. This decision comes as the EU is experiencing a drop in demand for COVID-19 vaccines and has also made similar arrangements with Pfizer and BioNTech. Despite the delay, Moderna maintains its $21 billion vaccine sales forecast for 2022, and the amended agreement will give EU countries access to a next-generation vaccine if approved.

title: Pfizer's Paxlovid reduces COVID risk in seniors regardless of vaccine status -study
summary: A new Israeli study found that Pfizer's antiviral treatment Paxlovid significantly reduces COVID-19 hospitalization and death rates in vaccinated and unvaccinated patients aged 65 and older, even during the Omicron variant's rise. However, the treatment did not show significant benefits in preventing severe illness or reducing mortality among younger adults aged 40-64. The study highlights Paxlovid's effectiveness in vulnerable older populations, regardless of their prior immunity status.

title: Novavax COVID Vaccine Efficacy In Omicron, Delta Variants Among Unknowns Ahead Of Advisory Cmte
summary: Ahead of the FDA's Vaccines and Related Biological Products Advisory Committee meeting on June 7, there are uncertainties regarding the efficacy of the Novavax COVID-19 vaccine against the Omicron and Delta variants. The committee will discuss Novavax's Emergency Use Authorization request. This article highlights the key issues and related content concerning COVID-19 vaccines and their approval process.

title: GSK to form consumer healthcare business ‘Haleon’
summary: GSK plc announced its intention to separate its consumer healthcare business to form an independent listed company, Haleon plc, through a demerger of at least 80% of GSK's 68% holding in the joint venture with Pfizer. This separation, expected to complete by July 18, 2022, will allow GSK to focus solely on biopharmaceuticals while Haleon becomes a world leader in consumer healthcare. The move is conditional on GSK shareholder and regulatory approvals, representing the most significant corporate change for GSK in 20 years.

title: Early Promise in Treating MS Seen With FibroBiologic's Fibroblast Therapy
summary: FibroBiologics' investigational cell therapy, CYMS101, showed early promise in treating multiple sclerosis (MS) by inhibiting disease activity in a mouse model and appearing safe in initial clinical trials. The therapy, which uses human dermal fibroblasts, is designed to be a more accessible and cost-effective alternative to stem cell treatments. Future studies, including a Phase 1/2 clinical trial, are planned to further evaluate its efficacy and safety.

title: ASCO22: J&J, Pfizer trade BCMA bispecific data in myeloma
summary: Johnson & Johnson and Pfizer presented new data for their BCMA-targeting bispecific antibodies, teclistamab and elranatamab, respectively, for relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma at ASCO. J&J's teclistamab showed an improved overall response rate of 63% and 39% complete responses with a median follow-up of 14 months, while Pfizer's elranatamab achieved a 60.6% ORR in preliminary phase 2 data. Both drugs are vying for market entry in an increasingly competitive landscape of BCMA-directed therapies, with teclistamab likely to reach the market sooner.

title: Pfizer to invest $120M at Kalamazoo area site to boost Paxlovid output, create 250 jobs
summary: Pfizer is investing $120 million at its Kalamazoo County facility, creating 250 jobs, to boost production of its COVID-19 oral treatment, Paxlovid. This investment will make the site one of the world's largest producers of active pharmaceutical ingredient for Paxlovid, with a capacity of 1,200 metric tons annually. Governor Gretchen Whitmer and U.S. Rep. Fred Upton praised the move for its economic impact and its contribution to fighting COVID-19.

title: Future Packaging to redefine India Pharm industry growth: InnoPack Pharma
summary: The 11th Annual InnoPack Pharma Confex, presented by West Pharma and CPhI Conferences India, aimed to showcase the latest packaging, labeling, and drug delivery device advancements for the Indian pharmaceutical industry. With India's pharmaceutical packaging market projected to reach $3.027 billion by 2030, the event provided a crucial platform for industry stakeholders to address challenges and foster growth, supported by government initiatives like the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme. The confex emphasized the role of innovative packaging in meeting healthcare demands and contributing to an "Atmanirbhar Bharat" (self-reliant India).

title: Pfizer to Invest $120 Million in Paxlovid Manufacturing
summary: Pfizer Inc. is investing $120 million in its Portage, Michigan facility to significantly increase the production of its COVID-19 antiviral treatment, Paxlovid. This investment aims to meet global demand, with the facility expected to become one of the world's largest producers of the active pharmaceutical ingredient for Paxlovid, creating 250 new jobs. The move highlights Pfizer's commitment to battling the pandemic and expanding manufacturing innovation in the U.S.

title: FDA advisers back Novavax COVID-19 shots as 4th US option
summary: FDA advisers have recommended Novavax's COVID-19 vaccine as a fourth option in the U.S., particularly for adults who have yet to be vaccinated. The protein-based vaccine uses a more traditional technology compared to mRNA vaccines and is already available in several other countries. While the panel noted its potential benefits and role in addressing vaccine hesitancy, questions remain regarding its efficacy against newer variants like Omicron and the long-term data on potential side effects like heart inflammation.

title: FDA advisers vote to recommend Novavax Covid-19 vaccine
summary: FDA advisers have recommended the Novavax Covid-19 vaccine for emergency use in adults, with a 21-0 vote and one abstention. This protein-based vaccine offers an alternative to mRNA shots, potentially appealing to vaccine-hesitant individuals. The committee acknowledged concerns about a possible link between the vaccine and heart inflammation, recommending further evaluation.

title: FDA committee OKs Novavax's late-to-the-game COVID-19 vaccine
summary: An independent FDA committee has voted to recommend Novavax's COVID-19 vaccine for emergency use authorization in the U.S. This vaccine, a protein-based shot, has already been approved in 41 other countries and could become the fourth FDA-approved coronavirus vaccine on the U.S. market. The decision aims to increase vaccine uptake, especially among those hesitant about mRNA technology.

title: Moderna says updated COVID shot boosts omicron protection
summary: Moderna announced that its experimental COVID-19 vaccine, which combines the original shot with protection against the omicron variant, appears to be effective. Preliminary study results indicate that individuals who received this combination shot experienced a higher boost in omicron-fighting antibodies compared to those who only received a fourth dose of the original vaccine. This development is significant as vaccine makers consider updating booster recipes to combat future coronavirus surges and new variants.

title: Dupilumab FDA Approved for AD Patients 6 months to 5 years
summary: The FDA has approved dupilumab (Dupixent) for children aged 6 months to 5 years with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis, marking it as the first biologic medicine for this age group. This approval is supported by data from the LIBERTY AD trial, which showed significant improvement in skin condition, itch, and quality of life for patients treated with dupilumab. The drug offers a new targeted treatment option for young children, addressing a significant unmet need.

title: Millions of COVID-19 shots ordered for nation's youngest, officials say
summary: White House officials have indicated that millions of COVID-19 vaccine doses have been ordered for young children ahead of potential federal authorization. Approximately 1.45 million Pfizer doses and 850,000 Moderna doses have been ordered from the initial 5 million available. This group of children under 5 is the last to become eligible for vaccination, though uptake among older children has been low, raising questions about demand for these new doses.

title: Alnylam follows rivals with new study results for kidney disease drug
summary: Alnylam Pharmaceuticals announced positive Phase 2 trial results for its genetic medicine, cemdisiran, for IgA nephropathy, showing a 37% reduction in urinary protein. While this positions Alnylam to enter a competitive market with other drugs already approved or in late-stage development, the company's investors are more focused on the upcoming APOLLO-B trial results for Onpattro, which could significantly expand its market. Alnylam, despite its product launches, continues to operate at a loss, but sees cemdisiran and the potential Onpattro expansion as keys to future profitability.

title: Big Tobacco Is Funding Opposition to Global Covid Vaccine Access
summary: Major tobacco companies, including British American Tobacco and Japan Tobacco International, are funding the Consumer Choice Center (CCC), an organization actively opposing a World Trade Organization proposal to suspend intellectual property rules for COVID-19 vaccines and treatments. Critics argue that the tobacco industry is undermining global public health efforts, driven by its reliance on intellectual property rules for profit, past use of these rules against public health measures, and even its own foray into COVID-19 vaccine development. This opposition highlights the industry's broader interest in protecting intellectual property, which it has historically used to fight regulations and secure its financial interests.

title: HPLC market to grow by $1.26bn in five years
summary: The high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) market is projected to grow by $1.26 billion, reaching a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 5.33 percent between 2022 and 2026. This growth is primarily driven by increasing uses of HPLC and rising healthcare investments. North America, particularly the US and Canada, is expected to lead this expansion, contributing a third of the market growth, despite the high cost of HPLC instruments acting as a restraint.

title: Regenxbio debuts $65M gene therapy manufacturing facility at its Maryland HQ
summary: Regenxbio has launched a new $65 million gene therapy manufacturing facility in Rockville, Maryland, enhancing its capacity for adeno-associated virus vector production up to 2,000 liters. This facility is part of a larger $100 million investment to establish end-to-end gene therapy capabilities. The company also joined a U.S. initiative for rare disease gene therapies and recently received $370 million from AbbVie for its eye disease gene therapy RGX-314.

title: Decoding Disease
summary: Amgen subsidiary deCODE genetics is celebrating its 25th anniversary, focusing on using population-scale genomic research to understand human diversity and disease. By studying large populations rather than preclinical models like mice, deCODE aims to improve drug discovery and development, with a substantial portion of Amgen’s R&D pipeline now supported by deCODE’s genetic insights. The company utilizes advanced techniques like Whole Genome Sequencing, Genome Wide Association Studies, and multi-omics data analysis to identify disease-associated variants and pathways, particularly benefiting from Iceland's unique population structure for extensive data collection.

title: FDA approves Lilly, Incyte drug for alopecia, but includes safety warning
summary: The FDA has approved Olumiant, developed by Eli Lilly and Incyte, as the first systemic therapy for severe alopecia areata, despite including a black box safety warning.
