summary: Moderna announced that its new updated Covid-19 booster shot for the U.S. produced a strong immune response against Omicron subvariants BA.4 and BA.5. A company-sponsored study showed people who received the new booster had more than five times the neutralizing antibodies compared to those who received Moderna's original booster. This development suggests a potential path towards annual Covid shots, similar to flu vaccine updates.

title: BioNTech Buys Novartis Singapore Plant for Asia HQ
summary: German Covid-19 vaccine specialist BioNTech has acquired a production facility in Singapore from Swiss drugmaker Novartis to serve as its Asia-Pacific headquarters and a manufacturing base. This purchase will establish Singapore's first dedicated mRNA production facility, with plans for it to be fully operational by late 2023 and capable of producing hundreds of millions of mRNA-based vaccine doses annually. The facility aims to expand beyond COVID-19 vaccines to include oncology product candidates, supported by funding from the Singapore Economic Development Board.

title: NYSE gala honors Pfizer, Teva Pharmaceuticals, Silverstein Properties, Azrieli Group
summary: The America-Israel Friendship League (AIFL) and Israeli Mapped in NY honored several companies and individuals at an annual gala in New York City for their contributions to strengthening economic and business ties between Israel and the U.S. Pfizer Inc. and Teva Pharmaceuticals Industries received the Kenneth J. Bialkin Leadership Award, while Danna Azrieli of Azrieli Group and Lisa Silverstein and Tal Kerret of Silverstein Properties received the Partners for Democracy Award. The event celebrated Israeli technology and the common foundations of the two countries, highlighting Israel's role in global health and crisis management during the pandemic.

title: Operation Eradication: The Global Health Community Comes Together to Defeat Meningitis by 2030
summary: The article discusses the global effort, spearheaded by the WHO and supported by companies like Pfizer, to eradicate bacterial meningitis by 2030. It highlights the devastating impact of meningitis, the importance of vaccines, and outlines a comprehensive plan with five pillars focusing on prevention, diagnosis, surveillance, patient care, and advocacy. The goal is to eliminate epidemics, significantly reduce cases and deaths, and improve the quality of life for survivors through increased vaccination coverage and strategic interventions.

title: Zanubrutinib Versus Ibrutinib in Relapsed/Refractory Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia and Small Lymphocytic Lymphoma: Interim Analysis of a Randomized Phase III Trial
summary: An interim analysis of the randomized Phase III ALPINE trial compared zanubrutinib and ibrutinib in patients with relapsed/refractory chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) and small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL). Zanubrutinib demonstrated a significantly higher overall response rate (ORR), improved progression-free survival (PFS), and a lower rate of atrial fibrillation compared to ibrutinib. These results suggest a more favorable efficacy and safety profile for zanubrutinib due to its increased selectivity in BTK inhibition.

title: Regeneron, CytomX Ink Potentially $2B Bispecific Immunotherapy Deal (Updated)
summary: Regeneron and CytomX Therapeutics have signed a deal worth up to $2 billion to develop next-generation bispecific immunotherapies for cancer. The collaboration will combine Regeneron's Veloci-Bi platform with CytomX’s Probody platform to create bispecifics that activate in the tumor microenvironment, aiming to widen the therapeutic window and minimize off-target effects. CytomX will receive an upfront payment of $30 million, with potential total payments reaching $2 billion based on research, development, regulatory, and sales milestones.

title: U.S. Supreme Court to Consider “Full Scope” Enablement of Claims
summary: The U.S. Supreme Court has granted certiorari to review the Federal Circuit's decision in *Amgen Inc., v. Sanofi*, focusing on whether patentees must enable the "full scope" of their claims or merely teach how to "make and use" the invention. This case, concerning Amgen's antibody patents for reducing LDL cholesterol, addresses a long-standing debate in patent law, particularly for broad "genus"-type claims in the biopharma industry. The outcome will clarify the standard for enablement under 35 U.S.C. § 112, with significant implications for innovation and patent strategy.

title: Bristol Myers CEO already reassessing portfolio in wake of US pricing law: report
summary: Bristol Myers Squibb CEO Giovanni Caforio has stated that the company expects to cancel some drug programs due to the Biden administration's Inflation Reduction Act (IRA), which grants Medicare power to control drug prices. A portfolio review is underway, with oncology expected to be the most affected area due to significant investment requirements. Pharmaceutical companies are concerned the IRA will negatively impact investment in clinical research and the development of new medicines.

title: Pacira survey finds knee pain hurts physically, socially and mentally
summary: A survey by Pacira BioSciences, "Standing Up to Knee Pain Survey: The Physical, Social, and Mental Impact of Knee OA," found that chronic knee pain significantly impacts physical, social, and mental aspects of life for sufferers, many of whom are under 50. Despite seeking various treatments like OTC medications, physical therapy, and even opioids, most patients reported little to no relief, indicating a need for new innovations like Pacira's Iovera device. The company aims to use these findings for marketing and patient empowerment, highlighting available non-opioid options.

title: With More than 150+ Molecules in Various Stages of Development, the Atopic Dermatitis Market to Witness Entry of New Drugs - Market Revenue to Cross USD 11 Billion by 2027 - Arizton
summary: The atopic dermatitis treatment market is projected to reach USD 11.34 billion by 2027, driven by increasing demand for biologics, a growing burden of allergic reactions, and the anticipated launch of over 150 emerging drugs. These new drugs, with novel mechanisms of action, are expected to offer improved safety and efficacy. Atopic dermatitis, a common skin disease especially in children, is characterized by a compromised skin barrier leading to inflammation, itching, and significant quality of life impairments.

title: 41 legal departments honored for their efforts to boost diversity
summary: Forty-one legal departments, including those from major corporations like McDonald’s and HP, have received Mansfield Rule certification from Diversity Lab for their commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion. This certification recognizes their efforts to ensure at least 50% underrepresented talent in senior leadership, career development, and external counsel roles. Many of these departments also achieved "certification plus" status, indicating significant representation of underrepresented lawyers in leadership.

title: California Needs a Lyme Disease Vaccine
summary: Researchers at UC Santa Barbara have studied the ecology of small mammals and their tick parasites, helping to explain the rates of human Lyme disease in California and predict future risk. A Lyme disease vaccine candidate, VLA15, developed by Valneva SE and Pfizer, Inc., is currently in human clinical development and aims to protect against Borrelia species. The article emphasizes the importance of a Lyme disease vaccine for California given increasing risks and the progress of vaccine candidates.

title: Vaccines delivered under COVAX sharing scheme for poorer countries
summary: The COVAX facility has delivered 1.83 billion COVID-19 vaccine doses to 146 countries. This initiative, backed by the WHO and GAVI, aimed to achieve 70% COVID-19 immunization coverage by mid-2022. The article provides tables listing countries that received vaccines across Africa, the Middle East, Europe, Asia & Pacific, and the Americas.

title: Valneva, Pfizer Report 6-Month Antibody Persistence Data For Lyme Disease Vaccine Candidate
summary: Valneva and Pfizer reported six-month antibody persistence data for their Lyme disease vaccine candidate, VLA15, in both children and adults. The data showed that antibody levels, while declining, remained above baseline, confirming persistence six months after vaccination. The three-dose schedule maintained higher antibody levels than the two-dose schedule, supporting its inclusion in Phase 3 protocols, and no safety concerns were observed.

title: With J&J's Gorsky departing, Duato adopts dual role as chairman and CEO
summary: Former Johnson & Johnson CEO Alex Gorsky is stepping down from his last remaining role at J&J in January 2023, passing the chairman baton to current CEO Joaquin Duato. Duato, who took over as CEO in January, will adopt the dual role of chairman and CEO, leading the company through its next phase, including the planned spinoff of Kenvue. Gorsky expressed confidence in Duato's leadership, highlighting his 30 years of service and his guidance during the pandemic.

title: Pfizer, Roivant set up new company around inflammation drug
summary: Pfizer and Roivant Sciences have partnered to create a new company focused on developing and commercializing RVT-3101, an experimental drug for inflammatory diseases like ulcerative colitis that blocks the TL1A protein. Despite Pfizer offloading the asset, it retains a 25% equity stake and commercial rights outside the U.S. and Japan. This move, similar to their prior collaboration on Priovant Therapeutics, aims to advance RVT-3101 and a next-generation TL1A antibody.

title: Pfizer to invest over $1.26 billion in Irish jobs boost
summary: Pfizer Inc. plans to invest over 1.2 billion euros ($1.26 billion) to expand its manufacturing plant in Dublin, creating 400 to 500 new jobs and doubling the capacity for biological drug substances. This significant investment is Pfizer's largest in Ireland to date, bringing its total staffing in the country to 5,500, amidst a period where other tech companies are laying off staff. The expansion will support the production of non-COVID licensed and pipeline products, further enhancing the site's capabilities.

title: What Are The Top Pfizer Government Contracts?
summary: Pfizer has secured several significant government contracts related to COVID-19 vaccines and treatments, playing a crucial role in the U.S. and international response to the pandemic. These contracts include agreements for the Paxlovid COVID-19 pill and billions of dollars in vaccine deals with the U.S. government and Army for both domestic use and international donations. The article highlights Pfizer's various business segments, its financial performance, and its role as a premier biopharmaceutical company.

title: Roivant, Pfizer team up on inflammatory disease drug
summary: Roivant Sciences and Pfizer Inc. have formed a new company to advance the experimental bowel disease treatment RVT-3101, which was originally developed by Pfizer. Pfizer will hold a 25% stake in the new venture, with Roivant holding the majority. An analyst suggests this deal highlights Pfizer's focus on its ulcerative colitis drug etrasimod, while RVT-3101 could represent a significant market opportunity for Roivant in the U.S.

title: European Medicines Agency accepts marketing authorisation application for momelotinib for the treatment of myelofibrosis
summary: GSK announced that the European Medicines Agency (EMA) validated the marketing authorisation application (MAA) for momelotinib, a new oral treatment for myelofibrosis. The application is supported by data from key phase III trials, including the pivotal MOMENTUM trial, which met all primary and key secondary efficacy endpoints. Momelotinib, if approved, would be the only medicine addressing key manifestations of myelofibrosis like anaemia, symptoms, and splenomegaly.

title: AFTX IPO News - Gene therapy biotech Affinia Therapeutics withdraws $100 million IPO
summary: Affinia Therapeutics, a preclinical biotech focused on gene therapies for rare diseases and cancer, has withdrawn its plans for a $100 million initial public offering. The company, which originally filed in January 2022, had not updated its prospectus since. It had planned to list on the Nasdaq under the symbol AFTX.

title: FDA Grants FTD to Pelareorep Plus Atezolizumab and Chemotherapy for Advanced PDAC
summary: The FDA has granted Fast Track Designation (FTD) to the combination of pelareorep and atezolizumab with gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel for advanced or metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). This designation was given following promising results from the phase 1/2 GOBLET study, which showed an objective response rate of 69% for the combination therapy. Oncolytics Biotech Inc. highlighted the importance of this designation in addressing the significant unmet need for improved standard of care in PDAC.

title: Pfizer’s €1.2 billion manufacturing site expansion
summary: Pfizer is investing €1.2 billion in its Grange Castle site in Dublin, marking its largest expansion in Ireland to date. This investment will double the plant's biologics manufacturing capacity, create 400-500 new jobs, and support the production of licensed and pipeline products in oncology, rare disease, inflammation & immunology, and internal medicines. Construction is expected to begin in 2024 and be completed by 2027.

title: The new "Big Three" of the 3D bioprinting industry
summary: The 3D bioprinting industry is seeing a consolidation around three major players: BICO, 3D Systems, and Desktop Metal (via Desktop Health), despite a vibrant community of smaller companies and startups. These "Big Three" are exploring new materials and opportunities, each approaching the commercialization of bioprinting from different strategic angles, focusing on areas like academic research expansion, drug development, and regenerative medicine. While the industry still heavily relies on university research, these companies are positioning themselves to capitalize on the shift towards commercial applications such as cosmetics testing, drug development, and ultimately, organ and tissue engineering.

title: Amgen, seeking to crash Novo's party, links bispecific to weight loss months after end of dosing
summary: Amgen is advancing its obesity treatment candidate, a bispecific GIPR antagonist and GLP-1 receptor agonist, showcasing promising durability data from its phase 1 trial. Participants maintained double-digit percentage weight loss 150 days after their last dose, with an 11.2% reduction in the high-dose group. This positions Amgen to enter a competitive market currently led by Novo Nordisk's Wegovy and Eli Lilly's Mounjaro, with Amgen planning a phase 2 dose-ranging trial early next year.

title: Pfizer Inc. to put $750M investment into Kalamazoo facility, creating 300 jobs
summary: Pfizer Inc. is investing $750 million into its Kalamazoo facility to make it one of the most technologically advanced in the world and ensure a steady supply of medicines and vaccines. This expansion is expected to create 300 well-paying jobs and builds on previous investments totaling $585 million this year. The Kalamazoo plant is one of Pfizer's largest, producing over 144 products globally and generating an estimated annual economic impact of $3 billion.

title: This Just In: Michigan Continues to Lead in Life Sciences with Latest $750M Investment from Pfizer
summary: Pfizer Inc. is investing an additional $750 million at its Kalamazoo facility in Michigan, further establishing it as a global leader in technologically advanced science facilities and ensuring the supply of essential medicines and vaccines. This builds on previous investments and underscores Michigan's growing prominence in the life sciences and medical device manufacturing sector, creating jobs and fostering economic opportunity. The investment follows other significant life sciences funding in Michigan, reinforcing its competitive position nationally.

title: Pfizer to invest $750M in Kalamazoo area facility, add 300 new jobs
summary: Pfizer Inc. is investing $750 million in its southwest Michigan facility to boost the manufacturing capacity for sterile injectable medications, leading to the creation of 300 new jobs. This investment comes in addition to previous significant investments in the Portage facility, enhancing its modular aseptic processing capabilities for pre-filled syringes. Governor Gretchen Whitmer praised the expansion, calling it a "game-changing" development for the state.

title: Pfizer, BioNTech countersue Moderna over COVID-19 vaccine patents
summary: Pfizer and its German partner BioNTech have countersued Moderna over COVID-19 vaccine patents, seeking dismissal of Moderna's lawsuit and an order that Moderna's patents are invalid. This countersuit comes after Moderna sued Pfizer and BioNTech in August, alleging patent infringement related to innovations it pioneered before the pandemic. Pfizer and BioNTech argue they developed their vaccine independently and that Moderna's patents "far exceed its actual contributions to the field."

title: GSK, Pfizer, Sanofi fend off thousands of U.S. lawsuits over alleged Zantac cancer link
summary: A U.S. judge has dismissed approximately 50,000 federal lawsuits against GSK, Pfizer, Sanofi, and Boehringer Ingelheim, which claimed the heartburn drug Zantac caused cancer. The court ruled that the plaintiffs' scientific claims were not supported by sound methodologies. While this impacts federal cases, tens of thousands of similar lawsuits are still pending in state courts.

title: Prometheus shares soar on new data for inflammation drug
summary: Prometheus Biosciences shares nearly tripled after its experimental inflammatory bowel disease drug, PRA023, showed positive results in studies for ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease. The drug achieved clinical remission in 26.5% of ulcerative colitis patients versus 1.5% for placebo, and higher endoscopic response rates in Crohn's disease compared to historical placebo rates. These strong results position PRA023 as a potential "game-changer," setting a high bar for competitors like Pfizer and Teva who are also developing anti-TL1A therapies.

title: Kite and Daiichi Sankyo Announce Changes to YESCARTA® CAR T-Cell Therapy Licensing Agreement in Japan
summary: Kite and Daiichi Sankyo have revised their 2017 licensing agreement for Yescarta (axicabtagene ciloleucel) in Japan. The Marketing Authorization for Yescarta will transfer to Gilead Sciences K.K. in 2023, with a new Kite Cell Therapy Business Unit managing sales and promotion. This change aims to increase capacity and broaden patient access to the CAR T-cell therapy for blood cancer in Japan.

title: Regulatory Affairs Market Size To Hold USD 31 Bn By 2030
summary: The global regulatory affairs market is projected to reach USD 31 billion by 2030, growing from USD 15.2 billion in 2022 at a CAGR of 9.32%. This growth is driven by changes in regulatory requirements, the emergence of specialized therapies like orphan drugs and immunotherapies, and the increasing prevalence of new diseases. The Asia Pacific region leads the market due to improving regulatory environments and a rise in clinical trials, while North America is expected to show the second-fastest growth due fueled by strong regulatory structures and increased biological approvals.

title: Stem Cell Therapy Market Size To Hold USD 18.7 Bn By 2030
summary: The global stem cell therapy market, valued at USD 10.51 billion in 2022, is projected to reach USD 18.7 billion by 2030, exhibiting a CAGR of 7.47%. This growth is driven by rising awareness, increased funding for research and development, and the growing prevalence of rare genetic diseases. However, ethical and safety concerns surrounding embryonic stem cells pose significant restraints on market expansion.

title: F.D.A. Authorizes Updated Covid Shots for Children as Young as 6 Months (Published 2022)
summary: The FDA has expanded eligibility for updated bivalent COVID-19 vaccines to children as young as 6 months old, broadening access to the retooled doses for more Americans. This decision comes amidst rising coronavirus cases and severe flu and RSV seasons, with officials encouraging parents to consider vaccination for their eligible children heading into winter. However, demand for these new shots among parents of young children has been low.

title: EU watchdog warns on waning effectiveness of antibody COVID drugs
summary: The European Union's health regulator, the EMA, has expressed concerns about the decreasing effectiveness of COVID-19 antibody therapies due to emerging virus variants. They suggest that healthcare professionals consider alternative antiviral treatments like Pfizer's Paxlovid and Gilead's remdesivir, which are expected to remain effective. This follows similar actions by the WHO and U.S. FDA, which have pulled recommendations for some monoclonal antibodies deemed obsolete against Omicron subvariants.

title: ASH: In next BCMA myeloma race, Gracell dazzles with 100% response rate as Pfizer, BMS place their bets
summary: Gracell Biotechnologies reported a 100% overall response rate for its BCMA/CD19 dual-targeting CAR-T therapy, GC012F, in newly diagnosed multiple myeloma patients during a phase 1 trial in China. This promising data, including high rates of stringent complete response and minimal residual disease negativity, positions Gracell to seek FDA approval for trials in previously treated patients in the U.S. and China. The article also details competing BCMA-targeted therapies from Pfizer, Bristol Myers Squibb, Regeneron, and Gilead Sciences, highlighting the intensifying race in multiple myeloma treatments.

title: How To Educate Regulators On What Matters To Patients
summary: This article discusses the importance of integrating the patient voice into medical product development and regulatory decision-making. Dr. Ebony Dashiell-Aje emphasizes that patients are experts in their own conditions and highlights various avenues such as patient listening sessions, Patient-Focused Drug Development meetings, and sponsor-led engagements to effectively educate regulators on patient priorities. The piece aims to guide stakeholders on how to systematically engage with regulatory bodies like the FDA to ensure patient perspectives influence drug development and review processes.

title: Nivolumab Plus Cabozantinib With or Without Ipilimumab for Advanced Hepatocellular Carcinoma: Results From Cohort 6 of the CheckMate 040 Trial | Journal of Clinical Oncology
summary: This study investigated the safety and efficacy of nivolumab plus cabozantinib, with or without ipilimumab, in patients with advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). The results from Cohort 6 of the CheckMate 040 trial showed encouraging preliminary antitumor activity and consistent safety profiles for both the doublet and triplet therapies. While the triplet arm exhibited numerically higher rates of treatment-related adverse events, both combinations provided durable responses, particularly with triplet therapy showing more frequent and longer-lasting effects.

title: Stocks Making the Biggest Moves Midday: Moderna, First Solar, Pinterest, Norwegian Cruise Line and More
summary: Several companies experienced significant stock movements midday, including Moderna due to positive cancer treatment data and First Solar after its inclusion in the S&P 500. Other firms like Pinterest, Amazon, and Meta saw gains following analyst upgrades or top picks status, while United Airlines and Norwegian Cruise Line saw declines.

title: Pfizer says it is working to improve supply of COVID drug Paxlovid in China
summary: Pfizer Inc. announced it is actively working to enhance the supply of its COVID-19 antiviral drug Paxlovid in China to meet rising demand as cases increase. The company is collaborating with stakeholders to ensure adequate access and remains committed to fulfilling treatment needs in the country. This effort follows the drug's conditional approval in China in February and a deal with Chinese drugmaker Zhejiang Huahai to produce Paxlovid for the local market.

title: Roche teams up with Pfizer on COVID-19 awareness campaign
summary: Roche and Pfizer have partnered for a U.S. campaign aimed at increasing awareness of COVID-19 testing and treatment options. Their initiative involves including a QR code on the Pilot COVID-19 At-Home Test, which directs users to a website providing information and guidance from health authorities. The campaign seeks to educate the public on the importance of testing and available treatments for COVID-19.

title: China Meheco to distribute Pfizer's COVID treatment in China
summary: China Meheco Group Co Ltd has signed an agreement with Pfizer Inc to import and distribute Paxlovid, Pfizer's oral COVID-19 treatment, in mainland China. This agreement comes as China faces a potential surge in COVID-19 cases after relaxing its "zero COVID" policy. The deal, valid until November 30, 2023, aims to meet growing demand for COVID treatments in the country.

title: Moderna Inc. stock outperforms competitors on strong trading day
summary: Moderna Inc. (MRNA) saw its stock rise by 5.78% to $208.95 on a generally down day for the stock market, outperforming the NASDAQ Composite and Dow Jones Industrial Average. This marks the second consecutive day of gains for Moderna, with the stock closing $112.36 below its 52-week high. The company also outperformed competitors like Johnson & Johnson and Pfizer Inc. on this trading day.

title: China health app starts online sales of Pfizer's Paxlovid for COVID treatment
summary: A Chinese healthcare platform, 111.inc, has begun selling Pfizer's oral COVID-19 treatment, Paxlovid, marking what appears to be the first retail sale of the drug in China. The medication sold out quickly, highlighting high demand as China pivots away from its "zero COVID" policy and anticipates a surge in cases. This retail availability could significantly boost Pfizer's earnings amidst concerns about declining vaccine demand.

title: China Meheco Group shares jump after agreement to import Pfizer's COVID treatment paxlovid
summary: Shares of China Meheco Group surged by 10% after the company signed an agreement with Pfizer Inc to import and distribute Paxlovid, Pfizer's oral COVID-19 treatment, in mainland China. The deal led to a significant jump in Meheco's stock in Shanghai.

title: US Parkinson's disease incidence far higher than earlier estimates
summary: A new study reveals that the annual number of new Parkinson's disease diagnoses in the United States is likely 50% higher than previously estimated, with roughly 86,000 cases in 2020 and approaching 90,000 in 2022, instead of the earlier 60,000. This increase, based on an analysis of insurance claims and population growth, highlights the urgent need for increased funding and care for the disabling illness. Researchers hope these updated figures will aid advocacy groups in securing more resources for research and patient access to care, especially as the U.S. population ages.

title: Life sciences software firm MasterControl gets $150M in its first funding round in 30 years
summary: MasterControl Inc., a life sciences software firm specializing in quality and manufacturing software, has secured $150 million in its first external funding round in nearly 30 years, led by Sixth Street Growth. This Series A funding values the company at $1.3 billion. MasterControl, which has been bootstrapped and profitable, plans to use the capital to accelerate the development of its software-as-a-service tools, including integrating AI and machine learning to predict and prevent quality problems for its pharmaceutical and medical-device clients.

title: Activist shareholders ask 9 big pharmas to consider whether 'excessive' patenting hurts access
summary: Activist shareholders from the Interfaith Center on Corporate Responsibility (ICCR) have requested nine major pharmaceutical companies to re-evaluate their patenting strategies, urging them to prioritize patient access alongside profit. The ICCR highlights "patent thickets" as a tactic that extends exclusivity, prevents generic competition, and keeps drug prices artificially high. The groups are asking these companies to create a transparent process that considers the impact of extended patent protections on patient access, noting examples like AbbVie's Humira and Amgen's Enbrel.

title: Anti-Inflammatory Therapeutics Market Size To Hold USD 127.5 Bn By 2030
summary: The global anti-inflammatory therapeutics market is projected to reach USD 127.5 billion by 2030, growing at a CAGR of 4.5% from 2022. This growth is driven by increasing prevalence of chronic inflammatory diseases, rising government initiatives, and the development of novel drugs. North America holds a significant market share due to biologics demand and government support for biosimilars, while Asia-Pacific is growing due to population boom and increased healthcare spending.

title: The top 10 pharma M&A deals of 2022
summary: In 2022, despite recession fears and inflation, the pharmaceutical and life sciences sector saw significant M&A activity, with Amgen and Pfizer leading the way with multi-billion dollar acquisitions. This article details the top 10 pharma M&A deals of the year, each worth at least $1 billion, highlighting major transactions involving companies like Horizon Therapeutics, Biohaven Pharmaceuticals, and Global Blood Therapeutics. These deals aimed to expand pipelines in areas like rare diseases, oncology, and neurological disorders, demonstrating continued strategic investments within the industry.

title: Arvinas Appoints Everett Cunningham to Board
summary: Arvinas, Inc. (Nasdaq: ARVN) announced the appointment of Everett Cunningham to its Board of Directors, succeeding Brad Margus. Cunningham brings over 25 years of pharmaceutical and medical services experience, previously serving as Chief Commercial Officer at Exact Sciences and President & CEO of GE Healthcare's U.S. & Canada regions. His expertise in strategic leadership and commercialization is expected to be valuable as Arvinas advances its clinical-stage programs.

title: NeoCart’s Revival Continues as FDA Approves Ocugen’s Phase III Trial Design (Updated)
summary: The FDA has approved Ocugen's Phase III trial design for its regenerative cell therapy, NeoCart, which was acquired in a 2019 reverse merger with Histogenics. NeoCart aims to repair full-thickness lesions in knee cartilage and will be tested against the current standard of care, chondroplasty. Ocugen plans to initiate the Phase III trial in late 2023/early 2024 and is also building a GMP cell therapy manufacturing facility.

title: Pfizer defeats race-bias lawsuit over minority fellowship program
summary: A federal judge has dismissed a lawsuit against Pfizer Inc.'s Breakthrough Fellowship Program, which aimed to increase diversity within its leadership. The lawsuit, brought by "Do No Harm," alleged racial discrimination against white and Asian-American applicants, but the judge ruled the group lacked legal standing to sue. Pfizer welcomed the decision, reaffirming its commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion.

title: GSK, Wave Life Sciences collaborate to drive development of oligonucleotide therapeutics focusing on novel genetic targets
summary: GSK plc and Wave Life Sciences Ltd. have announced a strategic collaboration to advance oligonucleotide therapeutics, including Wave's preclinical RNA editing program targeting alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency (AATD), WVE-006. The four-year research collaboration combines GSK's genetic insights and capabilities with Wave's PRISM discovery and drug development platform. This partnership aims to accelerate drug discovery for newly identified targets and expand GSK's pipeline with novel oligonucleotide therapies.

title: Madrigal Phase III Success In NASH Spurs Buyout Speculation
summary: Madrigal Pharmaceuticals' recent positive Phase III data for its NASH drug has led to increased speculation about a potential buyout of the company. The success in the late-stage trial positions Madrigal as a significant player in the competitive NASH therapeutic landscape, potentially attracting larger pharmaceutical companies. This development could reshape the competitive dynamics among firms like Novartis, Pfizer, Gilead, and Viking Therapeutics who are also pursuing NASH treatments.

title: After Novo's Wegovy supply woes, rival Lilly sees shortages for Mounjaro, Trulicity
summary: Eli Lilly is experiencing supply shortages for its diabetes medications Mounjaro and Trulicity, mirroring earlier issues faced by Novo Nordisk with its obesity drug Wegovy. The FDA has reported scarcity for several dosages due to high demand, particularly following the launch of Mounjaro. Lilly attributes the high demand partly to the scarcity of rival drugs and is working to maximize production to meet the expanding market.

title: Story from Pacira BioScience: Local surgeon enhances mastectomy patients’ recovery with non-opioid options
summary: This article highlights how Dr. Quintessa Miller in Destin, Florida, is improving mastectomy patients' recovery by using non-opioid pain management options. She incorporates EXPAREL into her Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) protocols, significantly reducing the need for opioids post-operatively. The article emphasizes the importance of non-opioid options in mitigating the risks associated with the opioid epidemic while enhancing patient recovery.

title: Relief Therapeutics Holding SA and NRx Pharmaceuticals, Inc. Announce Close of Definitive Settlement Agreements
summary: Relief Therapeutics Holding SA and NRx Pharmaceuticals, Inc. have announced the close of definitive settlement agreements to resolve their pending litigation. Under the terms, NeuroRx, a subsidiary of NRx Pharmaceuticals, has transferred all aviptadil development assets to Relief, granting Relief exclusive rights and obligations for its development and commercialization. Relief will also pay NeuroRx milestone payments and royalties on future aviptadil sales, up to $30 million.

title: Formulated Solutions inks deal to buy former Merck, Bayer manufacturing facility
summary: Formulated Solutions has agreed to purchase a former Merck & Co. and Bayer manufacturing facility in Cleveland, Tennessee, for an undisclosed sum. The 455,000-square-foot plant, previously operated by Beiersdorf Inc., has undergone significant improvements and offers expanded product and packaging capabilities. This acquisition follows Bayer's takeover of the facility in 2014 as part of its acquisition of Merck's consumer care business.

title: Drug price group slashes suggested price of Pfizer COVID treatment by 80%
summary: An influential drug pricing research group, ICER, has significantly cut its suggested price for Pfizer's COVID-19 antiviral treatment Paxlovid by over 80%. This reduction is due to the decreased disease burden associated with the Omicron variant. The new suggested price range is $563 to $906 per course, down from a previous assessment of $3,600 to $5,800.

title: Hospira, Inc. Issues A Voluntary Nationwide Recall For One Lot of Vancomycin Hydrochloride Injection, USP 1.5g/vial, Due To The Presence of Visible Glass Particulates
summary: Hospira, Inc., a Pfizer company, is voluntarily recalling one lot of Vancomycin Hydrochloride Injection, USP, 1.5 g/vial due to the presence of visible glass particulates. If administered, these particulates could lead to adverse events such as local irritation, allergic reactions, or microvascular obstruction. The recalled product was distributed nationwide to wholesalers and hospitals between June 23, 2022, and September 19, 2022, and patients and healthcare professionals are advised to discontinue use and report any adverse events.

title: How Pfizer Delivered the COVID-19 Vaccine in Record Time
summary: This article features an interview with Michael Ku, VP of global clinical supply at Pfizer, who discusses how the company delivered the COVID-19 vaccine in record time. He emphasizes the importance of a purpose-driven culture, a robust digital strategy, and a specific set of five mindsets—Caring, Curiosity, Collaboration, Creativity, and Courage—that enabled Pfizer to overcome challenges and achieve rapid development and distribution. The discussion also highlights the critical role of digital technologies in data-informed decision-making and streamlining the supply chain process.

title: Pfizer gives ORIC shares big boost with multiple myeloma collab, $25M investment
summary: Pfizer has invested $25 million in ORIC Pharmaceuticals and formed a clinical partnership for ORIC-533, an oral small molecule inhibitor for multiple myeloma. This collaboration will extend ORIC's cash runway through the first half of 2025 and allow Pfizer to integrate ORIC-533 development with its BCMA bispecific antibody, elranatamab. The news led to a significant jump in ORIC's share price.

title: U.S. FDA approves Gilead's long-acting HIV drug Sunlenca
summary: The U.S. FDA has approved Gilead Sciences Inc's Sunlenca therapy for HIV infections, offering a less frequent dosing option compared to existing treatments. The long-acting drug, anticipated to cost $42,250 in the first year, is for heavily pre-treated patients whose HIV-1 has become resistant to multiple drugs. This approval is expected to boost Gilead's HIV portfolio, with Morningstar estimating peak sales at around $1.5 billion.

title: Merck Announces Collaboration with Mersana Therapeutics to Develop Novel Immunostimulatory Antibody-Drug Conjugates
summary: Merck announced a research collaboration and commercial license agreement with Mersana Therapeutics to discover novel immunostimulatory antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs). The collaboration will leverage Mersana’s proprietary Immunosynthen platform to develop STING-agonist ADCs against up to two targets, with the potential to activate STING signaling locally in tumors. Mersana will receive an upfront payment of $30 million and is eligible for up to $800 million in milestone payments and royalties on net sales.

title: Pfizer Inc. stock rises Friday, still underperforms market
summary: Pfizer Inc. (PFE) shares rose 0.37% on Friday, closing at $51.83, but still underperformed the broader market, as the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average both saw larger gains. The stock remained $7.97 below its 52-week high. Competitors Johnson & Johnson, Eli Lilly & Co., and Abbott Laboratories also experienced gains on the same day.

title: Top 3 Government Contracts Won by Merck & Co. Inc
summary: Merck & Co. Inc. secured several significant government contracts, primarily related to the COVID-19 pandemic. These include a $1.2 billion contract for 1.7 million courses of the COVID-19 drug Molnupiravir and a subsequent $1 billion option for an additional 1.4 million courses. Additionally, Merck received a $136.7 million contract to build a new lateral flow membrane production facility in Germany to enhance pandemic preparedness.

title: Subversive Launches ETF to Focus on Mental Health
summary: Subversive Capital Advisor has launched three new actively managed ETFs, including the Subversive Mental Health ETF (SANE), the Subversive Decarbonization ETF (DKRB), and the Subversive Food Security ETF (KCAL). Each fund has an expense ratio of 0.75% and aims to address overlooked sectors. SANE, in particular, focuses on companies developing tools, treatments, and medications for mental health issues, an area Christian Cooper, Subversive's Portfolio Manager, believes is a neglected subsector requiring urgent attention and capital.

title: Aduhelm: House investigation says FDA approval process of Alzheimer’s drug was ‘rife with irregularities’
summary: A House investigation found that the FDA's approval process for Biogen's Alzheimer's drug, Aduhelm, was "rife with irregularities" and criticized the company for its "unjustifiably high price." The report detailed an "atypical collaboration" between the FDA and Biogen, including numerous meetings and the agency's shift to an accelerated approval pathway for a broader patient population than was studied. Both the FDA and Biogen issued statements defending their actions while acknowledging they are reviewing the committees' findings.

title: China Approves Merck’s Covid Therapy Amid Shortage of Drugs
summary: China has approved Merck & Co.'s Covid-19 antiviral drug, molnupiravir, for emergency use to treat mild and moderate infections in adults at risk of severe disease. This approval comes as China faces a surge in infections and aims to expand access to treatments after shifting away from its "Covid Zero" policy. It is the second foreign Covid-19 treatment cleared for use in China, following Pfizer Inc.'s Paxlovid.

title: Exclusive: Drugmakers to raise prices on at least 350 drugs in U.S. in January
summary: Major drugmakers, including Pfizer, GSK, Bristol Myers Squibb, AstraZeneca, and Sanofi, are set to increase prices on over 350 unique drugs in the U.S. in early January. These price hikes come as the pharmaceutical industry prepares for the Biden Administration's Inflation Reduction Act, which will allow Medicare to negotiate drug prices starting in 2026. Companies are also citing inflation and supply chain constraints as factors influencing these price adjustments.

title: Block on Blood-Plasma Donors From Mexico Threatens Supplies
summary: U.S. officials are blocking Mexican nationals from crossing the border on visitor visas to donate blood plasma for a fee, a practice that has supplied up to 10% of U.S. plasma. This decision stems from viewing the donations as "labor for hire," which is prohibited under visitor visas, and is causing concern among pharmaceutical companies about critical plasma supplies for treatments of neurological and autoimmune diseases. The coronavirus pandemic has already led to shortages in the blood supply, exacerbating the potential impact of this new policy.

title: America’s largest hospital company is booming. So why is one community trying to run it out of town?
summary: HCA Healthcare, the largest for-profit hospital operator in the U.S., has reported record profits during the pandemic, but its acquisition of Mission Hospital in Asheville, NC, has sparked significant community backlash. Patients and former staff accuse HCA of understaffing, compromising care quality, and prioritizing profits over community health, leading to an antitrust lawsuit and widespread distrust despite the company's financial success and investments.

title: Incredible Growth of HER2 (Human Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor 2) Inhibitors Market 2022 by Share, Size, Growth, Segments, Revenue and Top Manufacturers Analysis F. Hoffmann-La Roche Ltd, Merck & Co. Inc, Novartis AG
summary: This report from Stratagem Market Insights (SMI) offers an in-depth analysis of the HER2 (Human Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor 2) Inhibitors Market, covering its size, statistics, and competitive landscape. It highlights growth factors, future trends, consumption, production volume, and CAGR values while segmenting the market by top companies (F. Hoffmann-La Roche Ltd, Merck & Co. Inc, Novartis AG, Pfizer Inc, Puma Biotechnology Inc), product types (Monotherapy, Combination Therapy), and applications (Breast Cancer, Gastric Cancer, Ovarian Cancer). The report aims to help market participants understand the evolving business environment, identify new revenue sources, and strategize for continuous success in the HER2 Inhibitors market.

title: Aditxt forms Adimune to focus on immune modulation therapies
summary: Aditxt, Inc. has established a U.S. subsidiary, Adimune, Inc., to advance its immune modulation technology. Adimune plans to submit a clinical trial application for ADI-100, a drug candidate for psoriasis, with studies anticipated to begin in the second half of 2023, and a second study for type 1 diabetes is also planned. Joachim-Friedrich Kapp, former president of Schering AG's therapeutics business, will lead Adimune as CEO.

title: FDA Grants Fast Track Status to BT8009 for Previously Treated Locally Advanced or Metastatic Urothelial Cancer
summary: The FDA has granted Fast Track designation to BT8009 as a monotherapy for adult patients with previously treated locally advanced or metastatic urothelial cancer. This investigative agent, a bicycle peptide toxin conjugate targeting Nectin-4, has shown promising preclinical activity in various solid tumor models and is designed for reduced systemic toxicity. The designation reflects the urgent need for new therapies for urothelial cancer and will aid in its clinical and regulatory development.

title: Johnson & Johnson sets up mega-IPO for consumer health unit
summary: Johnson & Johnson has filed IPO registration papers for its consumer health unit, Kenvue, which is expected to be a mega-IPO. This move follows similar spin-offs by other pharmaceutical companies and could be the largest U.S. IPO since Rivian in late 2021, potentially raising up to $5 billion. Kenvue includes well-known brands such as Tylenol, Band-Aid, and Listerine.

title: ZyVersa Therapeutics Appoints Gregory G. Freitag, J.D., CPA; Katrin Rupalla, PhD; And James Sapirstein To Board
summary: ZyVersa Therapeutics, a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company, has appointed three new independent members to its board of directors: Gregory G. Freitag, J.D., CPA; Katrin Rupalla, PhD; and James Sapirstein. These additions increase the board membership to seven individuals. The company expects their extensive experience in the biopharmaceutical industry to be invaluable as ZyVersa continues to develop its lead renal and anti-inflammatory assets.

title: China Approves Merck’s Covid Therapy Amid Shortage of Drugs
summary: China has granted emergency approval to Merck & Co.'s COVID-19 antiviral molnupiravir (Lagevrio) to address the severe shortage of drugs following its abrupt shift from "COVID Zero" policies. This marks the second foreign COVID-19 treatment approved in China, following Pfizer's Paxlovid, which has also been in short supply. The approval comes as China faces a massive wave of infections, prompting increased demand for effective treatments and leading to deals with foreign pharmaceutical companies for import and distribution.

title: BioNTech signs deal with UK for personalised cancer therapies
summary: BioNTech has signed a multi-year deal with the UK government to enroll up to 10,000 patients in clinical trials for personalised cancer therapies by the end of 2030. The collaboration, which also covers infectious disease vaccines and BioNTech's expansion in the UK, plans to use the UK's clinical trial network and health data, aiming to enroll the first cancer patient in the latter half of 2023. BioNTech, known for its COVID vaccine partnership with Pfizer, will also establish a research and development hub in Cambridge with over 70 scientists.

title: Herpes Vaccine Candidate Advances in 2023
summary: BioNTech's BNT163, an mRNA herpes vaccine candidate for HSV-1 and HSV-2, entered a Phase 1 clinical trial in December 2022, generating significant interest. This vaccine is unique as an mRNA candidate encoding three HSV-2 glycoproteins to prevent viral entry and counteract immunosuppression. Alongside this, other treatments like United BioPharma's UB-621 monoclonal antibody are also in development, addressing the considerable market for herpes treatments.

title: China Says Talks to Cover Paxlovid Under State Insurance Fail
summary: Negotiations between China and Pfizer regarding covering the COVID-19 antiviral pill Paxlovid under state insurance have failed. This comes amidst a widespread COVID outbreak in China, posing a challenge for the government in providing access to the medication. The disagreement centered on the price of the drug.

title: Illumina and Nashville Biosciences Announce Sequencing Agreement with Amgen
summary: Illumina and Nashville Biosciences have partnered with Amgen to sequence 35,000 whole-genomes, primarily from African Americans, to address the underrepresentation of diverse populations in genomic data. This initiative is part of the larger Alliance for Genomic Discovery (AGD), aiming to sequence 250,000 samples to accelerate therapeutic development and promote equitable access to precision health. deCODE genetics, an Amgen subsidiary, will perform the sequencing, with data contributing to drug discovery and academic research.

title: Bristol Myers Squibb, Pfizer turned away from SCOTUS in high-profile cases
summary: Bristol Myers Squibb and Pfizer both lost their high-profile cases at the U.S. Supreme Court. BMS was denied a rehearing in its patent infringement case against Gilead Sciences for Yescarta, reinforcing an earlier decision against it. Pfizer's attempt to have its program to help Medicare patients with out-of-pocket costs for its tafamidis drugs reviewed was also rejected by the Supreme Court, as it was deemed to violate federal anti-kickback laws.

title: C-suite changes at Biogen, Bluebird, Novavax give insight into 2023 business plans
summary: This article details significant C-suite changes at Biogen, Bluebird Bio, and Novavax, offering insights into their strategic plans for 2023. Biogen has restructured its R&D division following FDA approval of a new Alzheimer's drug, while Novavax welcomes a new CEO amidst its ongoing vaccine efforts. Bluebird Bio has appointed a new chief business and legal officer as it navigates the launch of two recently approved gene therapies and aims to advance a third candidate.

title: Pfizer CEO rules out generic COVID drug Paxlovid for China
summary: Pfizer CEO Albert Bourla stated that the company is not in talks with Chinese authorities to license a generic version of its COVID-19 treatment Paxlovid in China. Instead, Pfizer is discussing pricing for the branded product and has an existing agreement for local manufacturing of Paxlovid in China with a local partner. Bourla emphasized that China, as the world's second-largest economy, should not pay less for Paxlovid than most lower-middle-income countries, leading to failed negotiations to include the drug in China's state health insurance.

title: Zotatifin With Fulvestrant and Abemaciclib Shows Favorable Activity in ER+ Breast Cancer
summary: In a phase 1/2 study, the investigational drug zotatifin, combined with fulvestrant and abemaciclib, demonstrated favorable activity and tolerability in 7 heavily pretreated patients with ER-positive breast cancer. This triplet combination resulted in 2 partial responses and 1 patient with stable disease extending beyond 24 weeks, achieving an objective response rate of 29% and a clinical benefit rate of 43%. eFFECTOR Therapeutics plans to continue dose escalation for zotatifin, expecting more data in 2023 for its various clinical programs, including the ongoing study in ER+ breast cancer.

title: Obesity Treatments Catch Drugmakers’ Eyes as Sales Seen Soaring
summary: Major pharmaceutical companies like Eli Lilly (LLY), Pfizer (PFE), and Amgen (AMGN) are increasingly focusing on the obesity drug market, following the success of Novo Nordisk's Wegovy. These companies are developing new treatments that aim for greater weight loss, less frequent dosing, or non-injectable options. The industry sees a significant market opportunity as attention shifts from the COVID-19 pandemic to addressing the "older pandemic" of obesity.

title: Pfizer Bivalent Vaccine Linked to Strokes in Preliminary Data
summary: Preliminary data from one US vaccine safety database has indicated a potential link between Pfizer's bivalent Covid-19 shot and stroke in individuals aged 65 and older. This potential risk has not been observed in other safety databases or with Moderna's Covid vaccine. Health officials emphasize that the finding requires further investigation, and current vaccine recommendations remain unchanged.

title: U.S. FDA, CDC see early signal of possible Pfizer bivalent COVID shot link to stroke
summary: U.S. health authorities are investigating a possible link between Pfizer and BioNTech's updated COVID-19 booster shot and ischemic stroke in individuals 65 and older. While a CDC vaccine database flagged this issue, other monitoring systems globally have not, and Pfizer, BioNTech, CDC, and FDA reiterate that there is no definitive evidence associating the bivalent shot with an increased risk of stroke. Both the CDC and FDA continue to recommend COVID-19 vaccination for eligible individuals.

title: AbbVie and Eli Lilly snub drug pricing agreement
summary: Global pharmaceutical companies AbbVie and Eli Lilly have withdrawn from the UK's Voluntary Scheme for Branded Medicines Pricing and Access (VPAS), citing increasingly punitive revenue clawbacks. This decision, impacting the long-standing agreement between industry and government, highlights concerns that the current voluntary scheme is detrimental to the UK's life sciences sector and innovation. Both companies will now operate under the Statutory Scheme, expressing hopes for a new, more sustainable pricing settlement in the future.

title: Dr Reddy's Labs acquires trademark rights of breast cancer drug from Pfizer
summary: Dr. Reddy's Laboratories has acquired the trademark rights for the breast cancer drug PRIMCYV (palbociclib) from Pfizer Products India Pvt Ltd for the Indian market. Following this acquisition, Dr. Reddy's will manufacture the drug in-house and retail it at an 85% reduction from the current MRP, aiming to improve affordability and access. The company also plans a Patient Assistance Programme for long-term therapy support.

title: Dr. Reddy’s buys trademark rights for Primcyv from Pfizer for domestic market
summary: Dr. Reddy's Laboratories has acquired the trademark rights for the breast cancer drug Primcyv from Pfizer Products India for the Indian domestic market. The drug, a first-in-class CDK 4/6 inhibitor, will be retailed at an 85 percent reduction from its current MRP to improve patient access and affordability. Dr. Reddy's will now manufacture the active pharmaceutical ingredient and finished drug at its USFDA-approved facilities.

title: Johnson & Johnson cuts production of underperforming COVID vaccine: WSJ
summary: Johnson & Johnson is significantly scaling back its COVID-19 vaccine production due to low demand, ending partnerships with manufacturers like Catalent and Sanofi. The company's single-dose vaccine, initially seen as a promising alternative, struggled with public perception after a temporary pause for blood clot investigations and failed to meet sales expectations, falling far behind mRNA vaccine uptake. J&J's pivot includes arbitrating a deal with Merck and temporarily shifting production at a Dutch plant to an RSV shot.

title: Pfizer to sell all its drugs in low-income countries at non-profit price
summary: Pfizer announced that it will sell its entire portfolio of drugs, including off-patent medicines, at a non-profit price to 45 low-income countries. This expands its "An Accord for a Healthier World" program, which initially offered only patented medicines at cost to combat limited access to treatments in the world's poorest nations. The program will now include a total of 500 products.

title: Fibroblast Activation Protein Inhibitors Market Growth
summary: This report from Quince Market Insights provides a comprehensive analysis of the Fibroblast Activation Protein Inhibitors Market, forecasting its growth until 2032. It covers market scope, overview, key players like F. Hoffmann-La Roche Ltd and BioXcel Therapeutics, Inc., drivers, restraints, segmentation by indication and end-users, regional analysis, and the impact of COVID-19. The study aims to offer qualitative and quantitative insights for strategic decision-making in the industry.

title: EU drug regulator has not seen signal of possible Pfizer COVID shot stroke link
summary: The European Union's drug regulator, the EMA, stated that it has not identified any safety signals in the region linking Pfizer and BioNTech's updated COVID-19 shot to a possible brain stroke in older adults. This comes after U.S. health authorities (FDA and CDC) flagged such a potential link based on preliminary data from a safety monitoring system. The EMA indicated it would continue to evaluate all available data for any similar signals in the EU, while Pfizer and BioNTech affirmed no evidence suggests an association with their vaccines.

title: The Future of Eye Care: Ophthalmic Drugs Market Analysis and Forecast by 2030
summary: Allied Market Research has published a new study analyzing the global Ophthalmic Drugs Market with a forecast from 2023-2030. The report provides an in-depth analysis of market definitions, classifications, manufacturing processes, cost structures, development policies, and plans, alongside key statistics and trends. It also highlights major players, market segmentation by indication, type, dosage form, distribution channel, and therapeutic class, and includes regional analysis, revenue estimation, and a Five Forces analysis.

title: Potential CF Gene Therapy KB407 Now an Orphan Drug in Europe
summary: Krystal Biotech's potential inhaled gene therapy for cystic fibrosis, KB407, has been granted orphan drug designation by the European Commission. This designation, previously received in the U.S. in 2020, offers benefits like 10 years of market exclusivity and encourages the development of therapies for rare conditions. KB407 aims to deliver healthy CFTR genes to lung cells to restore normal function, with Phase 1 clinical trials currently underway in the U.S. and Australia to assess its safety and tolerability.

title: Mangoceuticals Launches ED Drug, Telemedicine Platform For Men 01/19/2023
summary: Mangoceuticals Inc. has launched a direct-to-consumer telemedicine platform for men's health, focusing on treating erectile dysfunction with a fast-dissolving Tadalafil-based pill called Mango. The company aims to compete with other men's wellness brands like Hims & Hers and Roman, offering physician-approved orders through its website and planning to expand with additional products and subscription services. Mango is designed for rapid absorption, bypassing the stomach and liver, and is marketed with the tagline "Orange is the new blue," referencing Viagra.

title: Procter & Gamble revenue and profit fall as company looks to higher prices to offset declining sales
summary: Procter & Gamble (PG) saw its revenue and profit decline in the fiscal second quarter of 2023, as increased prices were not enough to fully offset falling sales volumes and foreign exchange headwinds. All divisions experienced declining sales volume, but organic revenue still rose by 5% due to higher pricing. Despite these challenges, the company slightly increased its sales growth outlook for 2023 to between 4% and 5%, while remaining cautious about the macroeconomic environment.

title: AOC 1020 Now on FDA’s Fast Track as FSHD Treatment
summary: The U.S. FDA has granted fast-track designation to AOC 1020, an investigational therapy by Avidity Biosciences for facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy (FSHD). This designation aims to accelerate the development and review process for the therapy, which is designed to treat the abnormal expression of the DUX4 gene, a cause of FSHD. Avidity is currently conducting a Phase 1/2 clinical trial (FORTITUDE) to assess its safety and activity, with preliminary results expected in early 2024.

title: Pfizer Acquires Abzena’s Biologic Manufacturing Facility
summary: Pfizer has acquired Abzena's biologics manufacturing facility in Sanford, North Carolina, through an agreement with Abzena and Pfizer's CDMO arm, CenterOne. This acquisition will expand Pfizer's capacity for manufacturing biological pharmaceuticals and support its growing pipeline of biologic therapies. The company plans to increase its North Carolina workforce to 4,500 employees by 2025 as a result of this expansion.

title: Amgen Inc. stock falls Thursday, underperforms market
summary: Amgen Inc. (AMGN) stock fell 0.89% on Thursday, closing at $262.03, underperforming the broader market which also experienced a downturn. This marked the third consecutive day of losses for Amgen, with the stock trading $34.64 below its 52-week high. The company also underperformed competitors like Johnson & Johnson and Pfizer.

title: Israel says has not found a link between Pfizer COVID shot and stroke
summary: Israel has not found any evidence linking strokes to the updated Pfizer COVID-19 vaccine, despite preliminary data from the U.S. FDA and CDC suggesting a possible connection in older adults. The head of Israel's coronavirus task force, Salman Zarka, stated that their data was rechecked after the FDA announcement and no such finding was made among the nearly 390,000 people who received the shot in Israel. Pfizer and BioNTech affirmed they hadn't observed such findings in other monitoring systems and found no evidence to suggest an association.

title: Collaboration with Janssen and Eli Lilly to address lack of paediatric medications
summary: Janssen and Eli Lilly have partnered to establish a master protocol for paediatric inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) trials, aiming to streamline the evaluation of their respective drugs, mirikizumab and Tremfya (guselkumab). This collaboration seeks to overcome challenges in paediatric drug development, such as small patient populations and ethical considerations, which often lead to delays and increased costs. If successful, this pilot study could accelerate approval processes for paediatric therapies and provide Lilly a competitive edge with mirikizumab in the CD paediatric market.

title: Tislelizumab regimen new first-line option for gastric, gastroesophageal cancer subgroup
summary: The RATIONALE 305 study found that tislelizumab combined with chemotherapy significantly improved overall survival and progression-free survival in patients with PD-L1-positive advanced gastric or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma. The combination treatment also maintained or improved patients' quality of life with a comparable safety profile to chemotherapy alone. These findings suggest tislelizumab plus chemotherapy as a new first-line treatment option for this patient population.

title: Sanofi and CytoReason Target IBD in Expanded Collaboration (Updated)
summary: Sanofi has expanded its collaboration with CytoReason, licensing the latter's inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) model in a multi-million-dollar deal. This partnership aims to identify new precision therapies for IBD, Crohn's disease, and ulcerative colitis, leveraging CytoReason's computational disease models. The collaboration builds on a previous agreement focused on asthma heterogeneity and seeks to address the significant unmet medical needs of IBD patients by transforming chronic diseases into curable, or even preventable, conditions.

title: Catalyst Pharmaceuticals Inc. stock falls Monday, underperforms market
summary: Catalyst Pharmaceuticals Inc. (CPRX) stock significantly fell by 29.04% on Monday, closing at $14.76, despite a positive trading session for the broader market. The company's shares closed well below its 52-week high and underperformed compared to competitors like Johnson & Johnson, Pfizer Inc., and Abbott Laboratories. Trading volume for CPRX also substantially exceeded its 50-day average.

title: Something New: PTAB Tackles Section 101 Patent Eligibility
summary: This article discusses a recent PTAB decision regarding Section 101 patent eligibility, specifically concerning a pharmaceutical patent for treating Alzheimer's Disease. It analyzes how the PTAB applied the Alice standard and distinguished the challenged claims from those deemed ineligible in INO Therapeutics LLC v. Praxair Distribution Inc., emphasizing the role of surprising efficacy and obviousness considerations in these determinations. The article highlights the increasing relevance of PTAB decisions on Section 101 as more patents become eligible for post-grant review.

title: Takeda One Ups Pfizer, Moderna with 600,000 SF R&D Office in Cambridge
summary: Takeda is building a 600,000-square-foot R&D office and laboratory space in Cambridge's Kendall Square, slated for completion by 2026. This new facility will be double the size of Pfizer's R&D hub and larger than Moderna's offices in the same area. The workspace aims to unify Takeda's global research and development efforts, enhance collaboration, and support scientific discovery across key therapeutic areas.

title: U.S. CDC still looking at potential stroke risk from Pfizer bivalent COVID shot
summary: The U.S. CDC is investigating a potential link between Pfizer's bivalent COVID-19 booster shot and stroke risk in older adults, though a new data analysis shows a weaker signal than previously identified. While other safety databases haven't detected this link, experts suggest further investigation is needed. Both the CDC and FDA still recommend the booster shots for older adults due to known benefits.

title: Sanofi offers refunds for Cablivi in novel model for rebates
summary: Sanofi has launched a new warranty program for its rare blood disorder drug Cablivi, offering refunds if patients do not respond effectively to treatment or if their disease worsens. This initiative represents a novel approach to value-based agreements and risk-sharing, aiming to minimize financial and clinical risk for providers and patients, especially for expensive, highly innovative therapies. The program's unique aspect lies in its focus on individual clinical outcomes rather than population-based measures.

title: EMA Says Yes To BMS’ Sotyktu But Turns Down Ipsen’s Sohonos
summary: The European Medicines Agency (EMA) has approved Bristol Myers Squibb's plaque psoriasis drug Sotyktu, marking a significant win for BMS. In contrast, Ipsen's drug Sohonos for Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva (FOP) was rejected, despite the lack of alternative disease-modifying treatments in the EU for this rare condition. This decision highlights the EMA's ongoing evaluations of various pharmaceutical products.

title: How a Drug Company Made $114 Billion by Gaming the U.S. Patent System (Published 2023)
summary: AbbVie maintained a monopoly on its blockbuster drug Humira for six years past its initial patent expiration, generating $114 billion in revenue by exploiting the U.S. patent system. This strategy involved building intellectual property protections and settling with competitors to delay their market entry until 2023. The monopoly is now ending, with several rival drugs expected to enter the market and lower prices.

title: Exclusive: Sanofi to let go of staff at vaccine plants in India as part of review
summary: French drugmaker Sanofi SA plans to dismiss all employees at two vaccine manufacturing facilities in India due to a functional review, affecting about 800 employees. The decision follows the company's failure to secure a UNICEF contract and increased competition from other drugmakers. While no asset sale is planned currently, it remains a future possibility as Sanofi re-evaluates its strategy.

title: Paxlovid sales forecasts may change with Pfizer view on China
summary: Pfizer's Paxlovid sales forecasts for 2023 could be significantly impacted by clearer information regarding demand from China, following the relaxation of its Zero-COVID policy. While Pfizer has already distributed millions of Paxlovid courses in China, future sales depend on ongoing price negotiations with the Chinese government and its national health insurer. Analysts currently estimate 2023 Paxlovid sales at over $10 billion, a significant drop from 2022, but a strong performance in China could help offset declines in other markets where governments have built up inventories.

title: Thrombocytopenia Pipeline Experiences Momentum: DelveInsight Estimates a Diverse Pipeline Comprising 27+ Companies Working in the Domain
summary: The thrombocytopenia pipeline is experiencing momentum with over 27 companies developing 30+ pipeline therapies, driven by the rising prevalence of the condition. Key companies like Takeda, argenx, and HUTCHMED are in advanced stages of development, with recent positive results from clinical trials for therapies such as TAK-755, sovleplenib, and efgartigimod alfa. DelveInsight's report highlights a robust and diverse pipeline with significant future growth potential for thrombocytopenia treatments.

title: At the head of the biosimilar pack, Amgen’s challenger to Humira launches in the US
summary: Amgen Inc. has launched its biosimilar, Amjevita, to challenge Humira (adalimumab) in the U.S. market, leading a pack of at least six other biosimilars expected to launch in July 2023. Amjevita is priced at two levels, both significantly lower than Humira's list price. This move marks a major development in the biosimilar market for the top-selling drug.

title: PrescriberPoint Raises Significant Growth Investment from Lilly, Pfizer, Adobe, and Mastercard with a Mission to Reimagine the Traditional HCP-Pharmaceutical Company Engagement Model
summary: PrescriberPoint, a digital marketplace connecting healthcare providers with resources for patient therapy, has secured a significant Series Seed investment from Eli Lilly and Company, Pfizer Inc., Adobe Inc., and Mastercard Incorporated. This investment aims to reimagine the traditional HCP-pharmaceutical company engagement model by providing a "one-stop" digital ecosystem. The platform seeks to streamline prescribing workflows, address coverage and affordability challenges, and ultimately help patients access necessary medications more efficiently by reducing administrative burden on medical practices.

title: One Common Mission to Serve Patients: Amgen Operations Shine with U.S. Biosimilar Launch
summary: Amgen has launched AMJEVITA™ (adalimumab-atto), the first biosimilar to HUMIRA® in the U.S., highlighting its expertise in biologics manufacturing and strong supply chain. The company emphasizes its vertical integration, which allows it to apply learnings from innovative product development to biosimilars, ensuring reliable and high-quality medicines for patients. Amgen currently has one of the largest biosimilar portfolios, with 11 biosimilars in market or development globally.

title: Pfizer Loses $40 Billion of Value in Worst Month Since 2020
summary: Pfizer Inc. experienced its worst monthly stock decline since June 2020, losing $40 billion in market value. This downturn, reflecting a 14% drop in share price, was primarily driven by a weaker-than-expected sales outlook for its COVID-19 vaccine and antiviral pill, Paxlovid, as revealed in its latest earnings report. Despite an initial fluctuation, shares ended January 31st higher amid a broader market rally.

title: Pfizer sees steep 2023 fall in COVID sales, aims to bolster pipeline
summary: Pfizer anticipates a significant decline in COVID-19 vaccine and treatment sales for 2023, projecting sales between $67 billion and $71 billion, down from over $100 billion in 2022. The company views 2023 as a transition year for its COVID products and plans to bolster its pipeline by launching up to 14 new products and pursuing strategic acquisitions to offset impending patent expirations on key drugs after 2025. Pfizer also expects to shift its COVID vaccine sales to commercial channels in the U.S. and re-enter the private market in China for Paxlovid.

title: Operation Warp Speed Is Using a CIA-Linked Contractor to Keep COVID-19 Vaccine Contracts Secret
summary: Operation Warp Speed is utilizing a secretive government contractor called Advanced Technology International (ATI), with deep ties to the CIA and DHS, to award $6 billion in COVID-19 vaccine contracts. This approach bypasses traditional regulatory oversight and FOIA requests, leading to concerns about transparency and accountability. The article highlights the significant military involvement in Operation Warp Speed and questions the lack of oversight given the controversial history of some recipient companies and the liability exemptions granted to vaccine manufacturers.

title: Execs at Pfizer, Novartis, Amgen and GSK tackle shifting priorities — reflecting the state of Big Pharma
summary: Top executives at Pfizer, Novartis, Amgen, and GSK held earnings calls discussing their companies' priorities, reflecting the current state of the pharmaceutical industry. Pfizer is aggressively pursuing M&A to generate $25 billion in new revenue by 2030 and offset patent cliffs. Novartis is divesting its Sandoz generics unit and focusing heavily on oncology R&D, while GSK is also shifting its R&D investments towards cancer while continuing to build strength in vaccines and HIV. Amgen is integrating recent large acquisitions, Horizon Therapeutics and ChemoCentryx, and has launched its Humira biosimilar, Amjevita.

title: BioNTech to invest $43 mln in German facility for mRNA vaccine building block
summary: BioNTech announced it will invest 40 million euros ($43 million) in a new German facility to produce plasmid DNA, a key component for mRNA-based drugs. German Chancellor Olaf Scholz visited the Marburg site and emphasized the importance of building local supply chains and speeding up approval processes for pharmaceutical companies in Germany. This investment aims to give BioNTech greater control over its supply chain, which was rapidly established during the pandemic for COVID-19 vaccine production.

title: Is A Rise Imminent For Johnson & Johnson Stock After An 8% Fall In A Month?
summary: Johnson & Johnson stock (JNJ) has fallen 8% in the last month, underperforming the S&P 500. This decline follows a U.S. appeals court rejecting J&J's bankruptcy strategy for talc lawsuits and mixed Q4 results, although the company projects mid-single-digit sales and earnings growth for 2023. Historical analysis suggests a high probability (76%) of JNJ stock rising in the next month after such a drop.

title: Ada Health and Pfizer collaborate to launch a nationwide online COVID-19 Care Journey, operated by Ada, to help connect patients with timely treatment
summary: Ada Health and Pfizer are collaborating to launch a nationwide online COVID-19 Care Journey, operated by Ada, starting the week of February 6th. This platform aims to help connect high-risk individuals with timely COVID-19 treatment by identifying those at risk of severe illness and facilitating access to independent telehealth providers for evaluation and treatment options. The initiative seeks to reduce barriers to care and improve health outcomes for millions of Americans, particularly considering that nearly 200 million Americans have risk factors for severe COVID-19.

title: Bristol Myers' profit beats on better-than-feared Revlimid sales
summary: Bristol Myers Squibb reported better-than-expected fourth-quarter earnings, attributed to a smaller-than-anticipated drop in sales of its cancer drug Revlimid, despite facing generic competition. The company's sales of $11.41 billion also surpassed analysts' expectations, fueled by a strong performance from newer products like Opdualag and Abecma, which are expected to nearly double sales in 2023. Bristol Myers forecast 2023 earnings of $7.95 to $8.25 per share, with revenue increasing by about 2% from the previous year.

title: China's CanSino confident its mRNA COVID vaccine as good as Moderna, Pfizer shots
summary: CanSino Biologics CEO Yu Xuefeng expressed confidence that his company's experimental mRNA COVID-19 vaccine is as effective as those from Moderna and Pfizer-BioNTech, despite not being able to conduct direct head-to-head trials due to lack of availability in China. CanSino is in discussions with Chinese regulators for a late-stage study of its vaccine, CS-2034, which is expected to be more affordable than its Western counterparts. China is racing to develop domestic mRNA vaccines after previously declining foreign ones and relaxing its zero-COVID policy.

title: Korea's New Fast Track Scheme A GIFT For High-Need Drugs
summary: Korea has introduced a new "Global Innovative products Fast Track" (GIFT) scheme to accelerate the launch and export of innovative drugs, particularly those addressing high unmet medical needs. The program has already selected Nefecon and Pegcetacoplan, indicating a strategic effort to streamline regulatory processes for such therapies. This initiative aims to provide strategic support for the rapid market entry of crucial pharmaceuticals.

title: FDA Approves Pfizer’s Supplemental New Drug Application for CIBINQO® (abrocitinib)
summary: The FDA has approved Pfizer's supplemental New Drug Application for CIBINQO® (abrocitinib), extending its indication to include adolescents aged 12 to less than 18 years with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis. This approval offers a new oral treatment option for younger patients whose condition is not adequately controlled by other systemic drug products. The decision is supported by data from the JADE TEEN clinical trial, which demonstrated significant improvements in skin clearance, itch, and disease severity.

title: PrescriberPoint Raises Significant Growth Investment from Lilly, Pfizer, Adobe, and Mastercard with a Mission to Reimagine the Traditional HCP-Pharmaceutical Company Engagement Model
summary: PrescriberPoint, a digital marketplace connecting healthcare providers with resources for patient therapy, announced a significant Series Seed investment from Eli Lilly and Company, Pfizer Inc., Adobe Inc., and Mastercard Incorporated. This investment aims to support PrescriberPoint's mission to transform the traditional HCP-pharmaceutical company engagement model into a "pull" rather than "push" system. The platform seeks to streamline prescribing workflows and reduce administrative burdens for healthcare providers by providing centralized access to product information, coverage, and affordability details for medications.

title: Pfizer and BioNTech mRNA shingles vaccine study begins
summary: Pfizer and BioNTech have initiated a Phase I/II trial for their first mRNA-based shingles vaccine program. The study, aiming to enroll up to 900 healthy volunteers aged 50-69 in the US, will assess the safety, tolerability, and immunogenicity of the mRNA vaccine candidates. This collaboration leverages Pfizer's antigen technology and BioNTech's mRNA platform, with the goal of addressing the significant global health priority of shingles vaccination given the aging population.

title: US government buying another 1.5M doses of Novavax COVID vaccine
summary: The US government has modified its contract with Novavax to acquire an additional 1.5 million doses of its COVID-19 vaccine, bringing the total purchased from the company to 3.2 million. This move aims to provide a diverse vaccine portfolio for Americans, especially since the Novavax vaccine is a protein-based, more traditional form of immunization. The acquisition comes as previous doses are nearing expiration, and the new purchase leverages existing contract funding.

title: Inside the NASH drug boom: New drugs for a ‘silent’ liver disease that affects millions near FDA approval
summary: The article discusses the potential FDA approval of new drugs for nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH), a severe form of fatty liver disease. Madrigal Pharmaceuticals' stock has surged, highlighting growing interest in treatments for this condition.
