Researchers discovered a molecule, now called resmetirom, that removes fat from the liver, offering hope for millions affected by NAFLD and its more severe form, NASH.

title: Merck & Co. Inc. stock falls Tuesday, underperforms market
summary: Shares of Merck & Co. Inc. (MRK) decreased by 0.74% on Tuesday, closing at $108.74, while the broader market indices, S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average, also experienced slight declines. This drop ended a six-day winning streak for Merck, and the stock underperformed compared to competitors like Johnson & Johnson and Pfizer. The trading volume was also below its 50-day average.

title: ABCOTV App Shell
summary: Moderna has announced it will continue to provide its COVID-19 vaccine for free in the United States, even after the federal government stops covering the cost. This decision comes after the company faced criticism for considering a significant price increase for the vaccine. Moderna stated that the vaccine will be available at no cost for both insured individuals and the uninsured through a patient assistance program.

title: Myotonic Dystrophy Pipeline Appears Robust With 25+ Key Pharma Companies Actively Working in the Therapeutics Segment | DelveInsight
summary: The Myotonic Dystrophy (DM) pipeline shows significant activity with over 25 pharmaceutical companies developing 28+ therapies, as detailed in DelveInsight's 'Myotonic Dystrophy Pipeline Insight – 2023' report. Recent advancements in gene therapy and drug repurposing, alongside promising clinical trials for drugs like ATX-01 and DYNE-101, highlight a robust effort to address this common adult-onset muscular dystrophy. The report provides a comprehensive overview of therapies in various development stages and key companies involved in enhancing the treatment landscape for DM.

title: Basketball Legend Kareem Abdul-Jabbar Joins No Time to Wait Campaign to Raise Awareness of Atrial Fibrillation (AFib) and its Symptoms
summary: Basketball legend Kareem Abdul-Jabbar has teamed up with Bristol Myers Squibb and Pfizer for the "No Time to Wait" campaign to raise awareness about atrial fibrillation (AFib) and its symptoms. Abdul-Jabbar shares his personal experience with AFib and encourages others to seek medical attention for symptoms, as AFib increases the risk of stroke by approximately five times. The campaign aims to educate the public on AFib symptoms and the importance of early diagnosis and treatment.

title: Celldex Therapeutics Appoints Rita Jain, M.D. to Board of Directors
summary: Celldex Therapeutics (NASDAQ:CLDX) announced the appointment of Dr. Rita Jain to its Board of Directors. Dr. Jain brings extensive experience in drug development and will contribute to advancing Celldex's programs, particularly with their emerging data on barzolvolimab for inflammatory diseases. Her background includes leadership roles at various pharmaceutical companies and a strong focus on immunology and inflammation.

title: Blood disorder startup Hemab Therapeutics raises $135M
summary: Hemab Therapeutics, a startup focused on treating blood disorders, has successfully raised $135 million. CEO Benny Sorensen aims to revolutionize treatment options for patients who previously had limited choices beyond traditional blood transfusions. This funding will support their efforts to develop new therapies for these conditions.

title: Merck’s COVID-19 treatment falls short in prevention study
summary: Merck's COVID-19 antiviral pill, Lagevrio, failed to meet its primary endpoint in a large clinical trial designed to prevent infections in household contacts of recently diagnosed COVID-19 patients. The drug reduced the risk of infection by only 23.6% compared to a placebo, which was not statistically significant. Despite this setback, Merck plans to continue marketing Lagevrio for treatment in high-risk COVID-19 patients and is exploring its potential for other infectious diseases, such as RSV.

title: Clinical Trial: ARV-471 or Anastrozole in ER+, HER2- Localized Breast Cancer
summary: Researchers are conducting a phase 2 clinical trial to evaluate ARV-471 or anastrozole in postmenopausal women with ER+, HER2- localized breast cancer. The study has two arms, with patients receiving either ARV-471 or anastrozole daily until surgical resection, approximately 5.5 months after treatment initiation. Primary outcomes include the effects on Ki-67 expression after two weeks, with secondary outcomes focusing on safety, tolerability, and pathological and clinical responses.

title: Pfizer/BioNTech apply for full FDA approval of updated COVID vaccine
summary: Pfizer and BioNTech have submitted an application to the U.S. FDA for full approval of their Omicron-adapted COVID-19 vaccine for individuals aged 12 and above, to be used as both a primary course and a booster dose. This move aims to simplify the vaccination regimen, allowing the updated vaccine to be used for initial doses instead of the original one. The vaccine is currently available under emergency-use authorization for specific groups and is already approved in Europe for those 12 and older.

title: Paraguay's Chikungunya Outbreak Intensifies
summary: The U.S. CDC has issued a Level 1 Watch for a chikungunya outbreak in Paraguay, advising travelers to practice usual precautions. Brazil reported the highest number of chikungunya cases in the Americas in 2022, followed by Belize and Paraguay. There is no antiviral treatment or licensed vaccine currently available, but a promising chikungunya vaccine candidate, Valneva SE's VLA1553, is undergoing regulatory review.

title: WSJ News Exclusive | Pfizer in Talks to Acquire Seagen in Deal Likely Valued at More Than $30 Billion
summary: Pfizer is reportedly in early-stage discussions to acquire biotechnology company Seagen Inc. The potential deal, likely valued at over $30 billion, would significantly expand Pfizer's cancer treatment portfolio. However, the talks face hurdles, including a stringent antitrust review.

title: Pfizer in talks to acquire Seagen in deal likely valued at more than $30B
summary: Pfizer is reportedly in early-stage discussions to acquire biotech company Seagen Inc. in a deal potentially exceeding $30 billion. This acquisition would strengthen Pfizer’s cancer treatment portfolio, particularly in targeted cancer therapies, and help offset projected revenue losses from patent expirations by 2030. Seagen specializes in antibody drug conjugates, a promising class of cancer therapy.

title: Merck reports two Phase 3 study misses for Keytruda
summary: Merck's cancer immunotherapy, Keytruda, failed to meet its primary endpoints in two Phase 3 trials: one for advanced prostate cancer and another for advanced lung cancer. In prostate cancer, Keytruda combined with Xtandi and hormone therapy did not show improved progression-free survival or overall survival compared to Xtandi and hormone therapy alone. Similarly, in advanced lung cancer patients with a specific mutation, Keytruda plus chemotherapy did not improve overall survival. These misses are setbacks for Merck's strategy to expand Keytruda's indications as the drug approaches patent expiration.

title: Cancer drug startup Cargo raises $200M to solve CAR-T relapse
summary: Cargo Therapeutics, a cancer drug startup, has raised $200 million from investors to advance its CAR-T cell therapy, CRG-022, into a Phase 2 study. This therapy targets the CD22 protein, offering a new approach for lymphoma patients whose cancer has relapsed or become resistant to existing CD19-directed CAR-T treatments. Early Phase 1 results for CRG-022 showed promising response rates in large B cell lymphoma.

title: Johnson & Johnson logs 57 layoffs in Pennsylvania as Kenvue spinoff nears
summary: Johnson & Johnson is cutting 57 consumer branch positions in Lancaster County, Pennsylvania, as part of its plan to spin off its consumer health business into the new company Kenvue. These layoffs coincide with J&J's previously announced intention to close its Greenfield plant, which produces over-the-counter products like Pepcid and Imodium. The move is part of a larger consolidation effort and a global overhaul by the company.

title: Eli Lilly slashes insulin prices by 70%, caps out-of-pocket costs in major access overhaul
summary: Eli Lilly announced a significant overhaul of its insulin pricing, cutting the cost of its most commonly prescribed insulins by 70% and capping patient out-of-pocket costs at $35 or less per month through its Insulin Value Program. This move, which takes effect from May 1, 2023, for some products and Q4 2023 for others, positions Lilly ahead of federal calls to cap insulin prices and follows similar actions by competitors like Novo Nordisk and Sanofi. The company hopes this will encourage other healthcare industry participants and lawmakers to develop comprehensive solutions for insulin access and affordability.

title: Company picked by Ottawa to produce made-in-Canada vaccines warns it may go out of business
summary: Novavax, the company chosen by the Canadian government to produce made-in-Canada COVID-19 vaccines, has warned it may go out of business within a year due to financial uncertainty. This news impacts Canada's vaccine manufacturing strategy, which has already seen previous partnerships fail, including deals with CanSino and Medicago. Despite the challenges, the National Research Council facility in Montreal, intended for Novavax production, may be used for other vaccine manufacturers.

title: CARGO Therapeutics Raises $200 Million in Oversubscribed, Upsized Series A Financing to Advance its Pipeline of Next Generation CAR T-Cell Therapies
summary: CARGO Therapeutics has successfully raised $200 million in an oversubscribed and upsized Series A financing round. This funding will be used to advance their pipeline of next-generation CAR T-cell therapies, including their lead candidate CRG-022 (CD22 CAR) for large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL) patients who have relapsed after CD19 CAR T-cell therapy. The company plans to commence a pivotal Phase 2 trial for CRG-022 in mid-2023, building on promising initial Phase 1 results and a Breakthrough Therapy Designation from the FDA.

title: Eli Lilly to cut insulin prices, cap costs at $35 for many people with diabetes
summary: Eli Lilly announced significant price cuts for its insulin products, reducing the cost of its most-used insulins by 70%. The company will also cap out-of-pocket insulin costs at $35 for privately insured individuals using participating pharmacies and for uninsured patients through its Insulin Value Program. President Joe Biden lauded the move and urged other pharmaceutical companies to follow suit, highlighting the long-standing issue of high insulin costs in the US.

title: Biogen Inc. stock outperforms market on strong trading day
summary: Biogen Inc. (BIIB) shares rose 0.87% to $272.21, outperforming a mixed market on Wednesday. The stock closed $39.67 below its 52-week high and surpassed competitors like Johnson & Johnson and Pfizer Inc. Trading volume for Biogen also exceeded its 50-day average.

title: Cargo Therapeutics Raises $200M in Series A
summary: Cargo Therapeutics, a biotechnology company based in San Mateo, CA, announced the closure of an oversubscribed $200 million Series A financing round. The funding, co-led by Third Rock Ventures, RTW Investments, LP, and Perceptive Xontogeny Venture Fund, will be used to advance their autologous CD22 CAR T-cell therapy candidate, CRG-022, through a pivotal Phase 2 trial for patients with LBCL, and support proprietary platform technologies and discovery-stage programs. Cargo Therapeutics was launched in 2021 by Samsara BioCapital with CAR T pioneers and a cancer advocate, and is led by CEO Gina Chapman, focusing on next-generation CAR T-cell therapies.

title: Eli Lilly Slashed Insulin Prices. This Starts a Race to the Bottom.
summary: Eli Lilly's decision to slash insulin prices has initiated a "race to the bottom" in the insulin market, with drug pricing experts believing this will not undermine efforts by nonprofit drugmakers, newfound companies, and states like California to offer lower-cost insulin. This increased competition is expected to keep prices down and benefit people with diabetes. The price cuts may also be influenced by looming Medicaid rebate policies starting in 2024.

title: ACTRIMS 2023: TG aims to make Briumvi accessible to patients
summary: TG Therapeutics is committed to making its new multiple sclerosis (MS) treatment, Briumvi, the most accessible anti-CD20 therapy on the market. They have set a competitive annual list price of $59,000 and implemented a comprehensive patient support program. This program helps patients navigate insurance, provides a quick-start option for immediate access, offers co-pay assistance for commercial insurance, and provides the drug for free to Medicare, Medicaid, or uninsured patients who cannot afford it.

title: ACTRIMS 2023: Novel RRMS therapy offers safety and efficacy
summary: New data from Immunic Therapeutics' Phase 2 EMPhASIS clinical trial and its open-label extension for vidofludimus calcium, an oral treatment candidate for relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS), demonstrate promising safety and efficacy. The therapy reduced brain lesions and prevented disability progression in most RRMS patients, with a safety profile potentially superior to many currently approved drugs. Vidofludimus calcium works by selectively interfering with immune cell metabolism, offering a "new category of oral drugs" that may be particularly effective in slowing disability progression with fewer side effects.

title: Amphastar Gets FDA Approval for Intranasal Naloxone Product
summary: Amphastar Pharmaceuticals has received FDA approval for its naloxone hydrochloride nasal spray 4mg. This product is designed for the emergency treatment of known or suspected opioid overdose in both adult and pediatric patients, utilizing Amphastar's proprietary nasal delivery device. The approval is seen as a significant step in addressing the opioid crisis by increasing access to this critical emergency medication.

title: US FDA approves Pfizer's nasal spray for migraine
summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Pfizer Inc.'s nasal spray, Zavzpret, for the treatment of acute migraine. This drug, a calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) inhibitor, offers a fast-acting pain-relief option for migraine sufferers, particularly benefiting those who cannot swallow pills and addressing concerns about cardiovascular risks and medication overuse headache. Pfizer aims to capture a significant share of the migraine drug market with Zavzpret, forecasting peak sales of around $6 billion.

title: Why Eli Lilly’s Insulin Price Cap Announcement Matters
summary: Eli Lilly announced a 70% reduction in insulin list prices and a $35 co-pay cap for commercially insured and uninsured patients, a move highlighted as a significant shift in manufacturer behavior to improve insulin affordability. This decision, influenced by government pressure and anticipated generic competition, aims to maintain market share while still ensuring profitability for the company. Following Lilly’s announcement, Novo Nordisk also declared similar price cuts, potentially setting a new standard for insulin manufacturers and impacting pharmacy benefit managers.

title: Informa Connect’s Medicaid & Government Pricing Congress
summary: Informa Connect is hosting its Medicaid & Government Pricing Congress from May 16-18, 2023, in Washington, D.C., inviting life science professionals to navigate complex Medicaid regulations. Attendees can save 10% on registration with code 23DRCH10 by April 7, 2023. The event will cover topics such as the Inflation Reduction Act, 340B updates, and market access strategies, featuring speakers from numerous pharmaceutical companies and government agencies.

title: Pfizer Agrees to Buy Seagen for $43 Billion
summary: Pfizer Inc. has announced its agreement to acquire biotech company Seagen Inc. for $43 billion, aiming to strengthen its drug pipeline with Seagen's targeted cancer therapies. Under the deal, Pfizer will pay $229 per share in cash, with the acquisition expected to close by late this year or early next. This strategic move is intended to help Pfizer counter the challenges of an aging drug portfolio.

title: Pfizer (PFE) to Purchase Cancer Drugmaker Seagen (SGEN) for $43 Billion
summary: Pfizer Inc. is acquiring cancer-drug maker Seagen Inc. for an enterprise value of $43 billion, making it the largest deal of the year. This move is intended to reposition Pfizer's pipeline post-pandemic, with Seagen recognized as a leader in developing cancer-fighting ADC drugs. Pfizer will pay $229 a share in cash, expecting the deal to close by late 2023 or early 2024.

title: Pfizer buys Seagen for $43 billion, seeks new cancer treatments
summary: Pfizer is acquiring Seagen Inc. for $43 billion to expand its presence in cancer treatments, particularly in antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) technology. Seagen's specialized treatments target tumor cells while sparing healthy tissue, and the acquisition aims to significantly boost Pfizer's oncology portfolio and future revenue. This deal is part of Pfizer's strategy to utilize its substantial cash reserves for acquisitions that will generate significant incremental revenue by 2030.

title: Pfizer Looks Past COVID With $43 Billion Deal for Cancer Drug Innovator Seagen
summary: Pfizer Inc. has acquired Seagen Inc. for $43 billion to bolster its cancer treatment portfolio. This acquisition aims to offset an anticipated decline in COVID-19 product sales and patent expirations, adding four approved cancer therapies and leveraging Seagen's innovative antibody-drug conjugates. The deal is expected to contribute over $10 billion in sales from Seagen products by 2030 and is part of Pfizer's strategy to move into more protected therapeutic areas.

title: Pfizer to buy Seagen in $43B cancer drug deal
summary: Pfizer has agreed to acquire Seattle-based Seagen for $43 billion, marking its largest acquisition since 2009. This deal gives Pfizer control of the top-selling lymphoma medicine Adcetris and a pipeline of cancer treatments, with Pfizer aiming to replicate its COVID-19 success in oncology and projecting Seagen's medicines to generate over $10 billion annually by 2030. The acquisition comes as Seagen navigates a transition period and Pfizer seeks to offset declining COVID-19 revenue.

title: Bristol Myers, Pfizer, AbbVie drugs likely to face U.S. price negotiation
summary: The blood thinner Eliquis from Bristol Myers Squibb, Pfizer's breast cancer drug Ibrance, and AbbVie's leukemia treatment Imbruvica are expected to be among the first 10 drugs selected for price negotiations under the U.S. Inflation Reduction Act. These drugs are key revenue drivers for their manufacturers and will be subject to government negotiation for Medicare health programs by September. The nonpartisan Congressional Budget Office estimates that these negotiations will save the government approximately $4.8 billion in 2026 and nearly $25 billion annually by 2031, with drugmakers pushing for transparency in the pricing process.

title: Pfizer’s $43B Seagen acquisition doubles early-stage oncology clinical pipeline
summary: Pfizer is set to acquire Seagen for $43 billion, aiming to significantly bolster its oncology portfolio and pipeline. This acquisition will leverage Seagen's expertise in antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) technology, expecting to generate over $10 billion in risk-adjusted revenues by 2030 and doubling Pfizer's early-stage oncology clinical pipeline. The deal highlights a trend of larger pharmaceutical companies acquiring innovative biotech firms to expand their therapeutic offerings and drive growth in key areas like cancer treatment.

title: UK Cialis Rx-To-OTC Switch World-First For Sanofi, H2 2023 Launch Planned
summary: Sanofi is planning a world-first Rx-to-OTC switch for Cialis in the UK, targeting a launch in the second half of 2023. This move follows other developments in the OTC erectile dysfunction market, including similar switches and new product launches by competitors. The article details how Sanofi's Cialis switch will contribute to the evolving consumer health landscape in the UK.

title: Following Eli Lilly, drugmaker Novo Nordisk announces cuts to insulin prices
summary: Novo Nordisk announced it will cut the U.S. list price of some of its insulin products by up to 75%, effective January 1, 2024. This decision follows a similar move by Eli Lilly and affects popular insulins like NovoLog, NovoLog Mix 70/30, and Levemir. While advocacy groups welcome the move, they note that prices are still high compared to production costs, urging further reductions and pointing out that Sanofi is now the only major insulin maker in the U.S. yet to announce similar price cuts.

title: Pfizer's COVID drug data supports use in high-risk patients - FDA staff (March 14)
summary: FDA staff reviewers have stated that data from Pfizer's COVID-19 drug trials support its use in adults at high risk of progressing to severe disease, bringing the antiviral pill, Paxlovid, closer to full approval. This assessment comes ahead of a meeting where external advisers will discuss and vote on the drug's full approval. Despite reports of COVID rebound in some patients, trials showed similar rebound rates between those who received the drug and placebo.

title: Early Launch Metrics for TG Therapeutics' Briumvi in RMS Trail Those of Novartis' In-Class Competitor Kesimpta, According to Spherix Global Insights
summary: A new report from Spherix Global Insights indicates that early launch metrics for TG Therapeutics' Briumvi, a relapsing multiple sclerosis (RMS) treatment, are trailing those of Novartis' Kesimpta. Despite lower initial enthusiasm for Briumvi compared to its competitor, half of the surveyed neurologists anticipate trying the drug in the next six months. The report suggests that Briumvi's success will depend on its value proposition resonating with prescribers.

title: Pharmaceutical Engineering Workshop Fosters Partnerships with Industry
summary: The Department of Chemical and Biological Engineering at Illinois Institute of Technology hosted a workshop to foster collaboration between students, faculty, and pharmaceutical companies such as AbbVie, Baxter, Roche, and Pfizer, along with Brazilian organizations. The event showcased cutting-edge research in biotechnology and biopharmaceutical manufacturing, and highlighted the university's Master of Pharmaceutical Engineering program. Industry leaders and alumni provided insights into digital transformation, biomanufacturing advancements, and the multidisciplinary skills required in the pharmaceutical sector.

title: Pfizer Recalls Nurtec ODT Prescription Drugs Due to Failure to Meet Child Resistant Packaging Requirement; Risk of Poisoning | CPSC.gov
summary: Pfizer is recalling approximately 4.2 million units of Nurtec ODT (rimegepant) 75mg orally disintegrating tablets because the packaging is not child-resistant, violating the Poison Prevention Packaging Act (PPPA). This poses a poisoning risk to young children if the contents are ingested. Consumers are advised to secure the product immediately and contact Pfizer for a free child-resistant pouch.

title: Sanofi Plans to Cut the Price of Insulin (Published 2023)
summary: Sanofi announced it would reduce the sticker price of its most commonly used insulin by 78 percent and cap out-of-pocket costs at $35 per month for privately insured patients. This move follows similar actions from Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk, the other major insulin manufacturers, and will take effect at the start of next year. The price cuts are expected to alleviate financial burdens for millions of Americans with diabetes.

title: TherapeuticsMD Inc. stock falls Thursday, underperforms market
summary: Shares of TherapeuticsMD Inc. (TXMD) fell 5.48% on Thursday, closing at $3.45, despite a positive day for the broader market with NASDAQ and Dow Jones showing gains. This marked the stock's sixth consecutive day of losses and put it significantly below its 52-week high. The company also underperformed compared to competitors like AbbVie Inc. (ABBV) and Pfizer Inc. (PFE), although it fared better than Agile Therapeutics Inc. (AGRX).

title: A biotech stumbles in its bid to challenge Novo’s obesity drug
summary: Altimmune's experimental obesity drug, pemvidutide, showed significant weight loss in a Phase 2 trial but was plagued by high rates of side effects, leading nearly a quarter of participants to discontinue treatment. This outcome caused Altimmune's shares to fall over 50%, raising doubts about its ability to compete with established drugs like Novo Nordisk's Wegovy and Eli Lilly's Mounjaro due to investor expectations for better efficacy and a more favorable side effect profile.

title: Scientists at DeepMind and Meta Press Fusion of AI, Biology
summary: Scientists from DeepMind and Meta are pushing for a closer integration of AI and biology, citing recent breakthroughs in computational biology as evidence of its potential. Meta Platforms' new tool for predicting protein structures is presented as a continuation of advancements initiated by Alphabet's DeepMind, with experts anticipating that these AI systems will significantly accelerate progress in life sciences, especially in drug development.

title: Catalyst Pharmaceuticals Inc. stock falls Wednesday, underperforms market
summary: Catalyst Pharmaceuticals Inc. (CPRX) shares dropped 1.94% to $16.21 on Wednesday, underperforming the broader market which also saw declines in the NASDAQ Composite and Dow Jones Industrial Average. This fall ended a four-day winning streak for CPRX, leaving the stock $5.90 below its 52-week high. The company also underperformed its competitors like Johnson & Johnson, Pfizer Inc., and Abbott Laboratories.

title: FDA advisors vote against effectiveness of Biogen's ALS drug for rare and aggressive form of the disease
summary: An independent FDA panel voted against the effectiveness of Biogen's investigational ALS drug, tofersen, for a rare form of the disease, though they unanimously agreed it could reduce a protein associated with disease severity. The drug targets a specific genetic mutation of ALS and is seeking accelerated approval, with the FDA's final decision expected on April 25. While the trial data on slowing disease progression was mixed, the panel focused on significant reductions in key protein biomarkers and considered patient testimonies regarding extended life.

title: US FDA grants accelerated approval for Incyte's skin cancer therapy
summary: The U.S. FDA has granted accelerated approval for Incyte Corp's Zynyz, a monoclonal antibody for treating a rare and aggressive type of skin cancer called Merkel cell carcinoma. The therapy, developed by MacroGenics Inc and licensed to Incyte, is a PD-1 inhibitor. While Incyte expects Zynyz to be available in early April with a comparable price to other drugs in its class, analysts, like William Blair, see limited commercial opportunity due to the strong market presence of existing treatments like Merck & Co's Keytruda.

title: Dr Reddy’s focuses on differentiated portfolio in key therapy areas for growth in India: GlobalData
summary: Dr. Reddy's Laboratories is strategically focusing on a differentiated product portfolio in key therapy areas like cardiovascular and oncology to achieve its goal of becoming a top-five pharmaceutical company in India. This strategy involves divesting non-core brands and acquiring product rights from other companies to strengthen its offerings. GlobalData notes that Dr. Reddy's has been actively engaging in both divestment and acquisition deals to optimize its portfolio for long-term growth.

title: Jasper Therapeutics taps Dr. Daniel Adelman as acting chief medical officer
summary: Jasper Therapeutics has appointed Dr. Daniel Adelman as its acting chief medical officer, leveraging his three decades of experience in immunology and drug development. Adelman brings a strong background from leadership roles at companies like Genentech, Aimmune Therapeutics, and Alvine Pharmaceuticals. His expertise will be crucial in advancing Jasper Therapeutics' mission to develop innovative therapies for chronic spontaneous urticaria and other mast cell diseases.

title: Hyrimoz, a High-Concentration Humira Biosimilar, Approved by FDA
summary: The FDA has approved a citrate-free, high-concentration formulation (HCF) of Hyrimoz, a Humira biosimilar from Sandoz, for seven indications. Sandoz plans to launch both high- and low-concentration versions of Hyrimoz on July 1st. Despite the entry of multiple Humira biosimilars, including those with interchangeability applications under review, a report suggests that significant cost savings may not be realized in the short term due to factors like physician reluctance to switch patients and AbbVie's potential rebate increases to maintain market share.

title: Amgen-Sanofi patent case divides makers of antibody drugs
summary: A U.S. Supreme Court case involving Amgen's cholesterol drug Repatha and Sanofi/Regeneron's Praluent is dividing antibody drugmakers. The ruling will determine how much information companies must disclose in patents and could reshape U.S. patent law, impacting competition in the $181 billion monoclonal antibodies market. Companies on each side are advocating for either broad or narrow patent protection, with significant implications for future drug development and market exclusivity.

title: Here’s Why Viking Therapeutics Rose Over 50% on Obesity Drug Data
summary: Viking Therapeutics (NASDAQ: VKTX) saw its stock jump over 50% following positive Phase 1 clinical trial data for its novel dual GLP-1/GLP agonist compound VK2735, an obesity treatment. The trial showed significant weight loss in participants, with up to a 7.8% reduction from baseline, and the drug was well-tolerated. This success highlights Viking's potential in the competitive weight loss market, where it faces companies like Eli Lilly and Pfizer.

title: Here’s Why Viking Therapeutics Rose Over 50% on Obesity Drug Data
summary: Viking Therapeutics (NASDAQ: VKTX) jumped over 50% after releasing positive Phase 1 data for its obesity drug VK2735. The clinical trial showed that participants lost up to 7.9% of their body weight from baseline, with good tolerability, and Viking plans to proceed with a Phase 2 trial in mid-2023. The company also has five other compounds in its pipeline, including a lead compound for NASH, which could further impact its stock performance.

title: Acquired patents aid J&J defense of top-selling drug from biosimilar challenge
summary: Johnson & Johnson is utilizing patents acquired through its 2020 purchase of Momenta Pharmaceuticals to defend its top-selling psoriasis drug, Stelara, against biosimilar competition from Amgen. These patents, which relate to manufacturing processes, could potentially delay Amgen's market entry even though Stelara's primary patent is set to expire in September 2023. Critics argue that this strategy is a common tactic by drugmakers to create "patent thickets" and extend market exclusivity, ultimately hindering competition and increasing healthcare costs.

title: J&J bows out of RSV vaccine race after scrapping trial
summary: Johnson & Johnson (J&J) has announced it will discontinue the late-stage study of its adult respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccine. This decision follows moves by rivals Pfizer and GSK gaining a lead in the race for the first RSV vaccine and is attributed to J&J's strategy to focus on medicines with the greatest potential benefit. J&J's study, which began in 2021 across multiple countries, had previously shown 80% effectiveness in a mid-stage trial.

title: 'You forget to eat': How Ozempic went from diabetes medicine to blockbuster diet drug
summary: Ozempic, originally a diabetes medication, has become a highly sought-after weight loss drug, leading to supply issues for diabetic patients. The drug's popularity, fueled by celebrity endorsements and social media, has driven up prices and spurred new businesses. Doctors express concern over its prescription for non-life-threatening weight loss and potential unknown long-term side effects.

title: Pfizer officially unveils new headquarters at Hudson Yards
summary: Pfizer has officially opened its new headquarters at Hudson Yards in New York City. Alongside the headquarters unveiling, the company also launched the Pfizer School of Science program, aimed at middle schoolers in New York City.

title: Amgen Inc. stock rises Monday, outperforms market
summary: Amgen Inc. (AMGN) stock rose 1.11% on Monday, closing at $244.44, outperforming the broader market indices like the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average. This marked the stock's fifth consecutive day of gains, though it remained below its 52-week high. Despite the overall positive performance, Amgen's stock underperformed some competitors like Johnson & Johnson and Pfizer on the same day.

title: Gilead details promising early COVID antiviral data, setting up larger studies
summary: Gilead Sciences Inc. announced promising early data from its experimental oral COVID-19 antiviral, obeldesivir, in healthy volunteers, paving the way for two large Phase III trials. The drug, designed to prevent the coronavirus from replicating, showed good concentrations in blood and no serious side effects, positioning it as a potential alternative to existing treatments like Paxlovid and Lagevrio, especially given its simpler dosing and fewer drug interactions.

title: Vaccination against chickenpox is estimated to significantly reduce varicella cases and deaths in both children and adults and would be cost-effective, per a modelling study in Denmark, informing policymakers around routine immunization
summary: A modeling study conducted in Denmark suggests that universal vaccination against chickenpox would significantly reduce varicella cases and deaths in both children and adults, while also being cost-effective. The findings aim to inform policymakers regarding the potential implementation of routine chickenpox immunization programs. The research, funded by Merck Sharp & Dohme LLC, evaluated different vaccination strategies and their impact over time.

title: Starbucks hires ex-Medtronic lawyer as new legal chief
summary: Starbucks has appointed Brad Lerman, formerly of Medtronic Plc, as its new executive vice president and general counsel, reporting directly to CEO Laxman Narasimhan. Lerman's appointment comes as Starbucks faces criticism regarding its stance on union organizing, with over 290 U.S. stores having voted to unionize. He will start his new role on May 8, succeeding Zabrina Jenkins, who has been acting general counsel since the dismissal of Rachel Gonzalez.

title: A $606 Million Litigation Fund Eyes Moderna
summary: Sina Toussi, founder of Two Seas Capital, a hedge fund with $606 million in assets under management, is using Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) requests to research companies like Moderna, Pfizer, and others, indicating potential litigation interests. Two Seas Capital specializes in investments with a litigation or regulatory component, and its FOIA requests, particularly concerning Moderna's Covid-19 vaccine, suggest it is exploring opportunities in the pharmaceutical sector. This strategy highlights the growing trend of litigation funding and its potential impact on publicly traded companies and markets.

title: Centrum launches specialised nutritious gummies in India
summary: Centrum, part of Haleon, has launched a new line of beneficial gummies called 'Benefit Blends' in India. This range includes five variants catering to immune defense, sleep, digestive balance for adults, and immune fuel and growth fuel for children. These vegetarian, gluten-free, and non-habit-forming gummies aim to address the nutritional gaps faced by Indian consumers due to their hectic lifestyles.

title: Biogen, aiming for a better Alzheimer’s therapy, licenses a Denali program
summary: Biogen has licensed a program from Denali Therapeutics to develop new Alzheimer's disease therapies that are safer or more effective. The program utilizes Denali's "transport vehicle" platform to help large therapeutic molecules cross the blood-brain barrier. Biogen will be responsible for development and commercialization, with Denali eligible for an upfront payment, milestone payments, and royalties.

title: Merck to buy inflammatory disease drugmaker Prometheus for $10.8B
summary: Merck has agreed to acquire Prometheus Biosciences for approximately $10.8 billion, aiming to boost its immunology portfolio with an experimental inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) drug. This acquisition marks Merck's second-largest deal this year and is intended to help offset the upcoming patent expiration of its top-selling cancer medicine, Keytruda. The Prometheus drug, targeting the TL1A protein, has shown promising Phase 2 results for ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease.

title: Merck to buy Prometheus Biosciences for $10.8 billion
summary: Merck & Co. Inc. announced a deal to acquire Prometheus Biosciences Inc. for $10.8 billion, or $200 a share. Prometheus is a clinical-stage biotechnology company that focuses on autoimmune treatments. One of its key treatments in development is PRA023, designed for conditions like ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease.

title: Can new M&A boost the ALPS Medical Breakthroughs ETF?
summary: The ALPS Medical Breakthroughs ETF (SBIO) has faced challenges since 2021 due to investor aversion to growth stocks, but recent signs of easing inflation and increased M&A activity in the biotech sector suggest a potential recovery. The ETF, whose top holding Prometheus Biosciences (RXDX) is being acquired by Merck for $10.8 billion, focuses on companies with drugs in clinical trials. This acquisition, along with Pfizer's recent deals, signals a broader trend of large pharmaceutical companies acquiring smaller biotech firms, which could further boost SBIO's performance.

title: Merck’s latest deal turns up the spotlight on immune system drugmakers
summary: Merck's acquisition of Prometheus Biosciences for almost $11 billion highlights the intense pharmaceutical industry interest in immunology medicines, particularly those targeting inflammatory diseases. Analysts believe this deal will spur further M&A activity among drugmakers with promising immune system drugs, especially given upcoming patent expirations for many large firms. The article details several companies that could be potential takeover targets and discusses the burgeoning interest in TL1A and TYK2 inhibitor drugs.

title: FDA Expands AbbVie's (ABBV) Qulipta Label in Chronic Migraine
summary: The FDA has approved AbbVie's Qulipta (atogepant) 60mg dose for the prevention of chronic migraine in adults, making it the first and only oral CGRP receptor antagonist approved for both episodic and chronic migraines. This label expansion is based on positive results from the phase III PROGRESS study. AbbVie now has three migraine drugs, including Botox and Ubrelvy, positioning it strongly against competitors like Pfizer.

title: AbbVie Wins FDA Approval for New Migraine Indication
summary: AbbVie's Qulipta (atogepant) has received FDA approval for an expanded indication to treat chronic migraine, making it the only oral CGRP receptor antagonist approved for both episodic and chronic migraine prevention. This approval was based on data from the pivotal Phase III PROGRESS trial, which demonstrated a significant decrease in monthly migraine days for patients treated with Qulipta. The drug's expanded label strengthens AbbVie's position in the migraine market, complementing its existing treatments Botox and Ubrelvy, against competitors like Pfizer's Nurtec ODT and Zavzpret.

title: Infographic: Highlights of Abbott Laboratories’ Q1 2023 results
summary: Abbott Laboratories announced its financial results for the first quarter of 2023, reporting a significant decline in net sales and adjusted earnings due to decreased COVID-19 testing-related sales. First-quarter net sales fell 18% year-over-year to $9.75 billion, with adjusted earnings per share dropping to $1.03 from $1.73 in the prior year. Unadjusted net income also saw a substantial decrease to $1.32 billion, or $0.75 per share.

title: Erasing or replacing errors in a patient’s genetic code can treat and cure some genetic diseases
summary: Gene editing, primarily through base editing and prime editing, offers promising solutions for treating and potentially curing genetic diseases by correcting DNA "misspellings." Developed by David Liu and his team, these techniques allow for precise alterations to the genetic code, with base editing addressing common single-letter errors and prime editing offering broader "search and replace" capabilities for larger mutations. While significant progress has been made, including treatments for progeria and sickle-cell disease in mice and leukemia in humans, further research into safety, efficacy, delivery methods, and ethical considerations is crucial for widespread therapeutic application.

title: Relief For Excedrin Migraine, Green For Package
summary: Excedrin Migraine is undergoing a packaging overhaul that includes new labeling for retail display trays and the addition of "Relief" to the product name. This change aims to update the product's presentation and branding.

title: Lilly sells emergency diabetes drug for $500M
summary: Eli Lilly has sold its emergency diabetes treatment, Baqsimi, an intranasal glucagon, to Amphastar Pharmaceuticals for an upfront payment of $500 million, with potential for an additional $575 million in future payments. Baqsimi, which had $139 million in sales last year, is an emergency treatment for severe hypoglycemia, a side effect of insulin therapy, and despite being part of Lilly's core diabetes business, it was overshadowed by blockbuster drugs like Trulicity and Mounjaro. This divestiture aligns Baqsimi, which fits with Amphastar's specialization in injectable, inhalable, and intranasal drugs for emergency medical conditions, better with the acquiring company's product line.

title: Top 10 pharma employers of 2023: A comprehensive analysis
summary: This article provides a comprehensive analysis of the top 10 pharma employers of 2023, based on employee reviews and industry trends. The ranking criteria include Glassdoor and Comparably ratings, company benefits, and inclusion in other top employer lists. Recursion Pharmaceuticals and Ultragenyx topped the list, praised for their strong culture and supportive leadership, while other major companies like Merck, Novartis, and Pfizer were recognized for competitive pay and benefits despite some management challenges.

title: ABBV Infographic: AbbVie’s Q1 2023 earnings and revenue decline
summary: Pharmaceutical company AbbVie, Inc. (NYSE: ABBV) reported a decline in its first-quarter 2023 adjusted earnings and revenues. Total revenues decreased 9.7% year-over-year to $12.23 billion, with adjusted net income also falling compared to the prior-year period. Despite the declines, CEO Richard A. Gonzalez stated the quarter was off to an excellent start, exceeding expectations due to strong commercial execution.

title: Patients & Purpose: 2023
summary: Patients & Purpose (P&P) saw double-digit growth in 2022 and continues its patient-centric approach through digital innovation, data mastery, and breakthrough creative. Key initiatives for P&P include expanding its social marketing efforts, launching a sister agency Science & Purpose for integrated HCP and patient marketing, and focusing on purposeful innovation in emerging digital trends. The agency also emphasizes accessibility in its communications, offers comprehensive patient services programs, and integrates DE&I principles in its work, all while committing to employee philanthropy and pro bono efforts like the "Nature Heals" campaign with the NYC Parks Foundation.

title: Has the CRISPR Revolution Arrived Yet?
summary: Dr. Greg Licholai discusses the current state of CRISPR technology, noting that the first CRISPR-based drugs are nearing approval for genetic illnesses like sickle cell anemia and beta thalassemia, potentially offering revolutionary single-dose cures. While the scientific progress is significant, the interview highlights major challenges, including ethical concerns, regulatory standards, extremely high pricing, and ensuring equitable access to these transformative therapies. The discussion also touches on ongoing research for other diseases and the continued moratorium on human embryo experimentation.

title: Seres’s Bacteria in a Pill Becomes First FDA-Approved Oral Microbiome Therapy
summary: Seres Therapeutics has received FDA approval for Vowst, making it the first oral microbiome therapy for preventing recurrent Clostridioides difficile (C. diff) infection in adults. The drug, a capsule containing spores of beneficial bacteria derived from healthy donor stool, aims to restore gut microbiome balance. This approval follows an earlier setback in 2016 and positions Seres to commercialize Vowst with Nestle Health Science, with future pipelines already being developed.

title: Seagen records major revenue jump ahead of Pfizer acquisition
summary: Seagen reported a significant revenue jump, generating $520 million in the first quarter, as it moves towards its proposed acquisition by Pfizer. This financial update comes amidst news of leadership changes and continued growth plans for the cancer drug maker.

title: AstraZeneca beats estimates on strong emerging market sales as COVID wanes
summary: AstraZeneca surpassed first-quarter profit and revenue expectations due to robust sales of its cancer treatment Imfinzi and strong demand in emerging markets, which compensated for declining COVID product sales. The company's focus on cancer, cardiovascular, kidney, rare, and respiratory diseases, along with its acquisition of Alexion, has contributed to its strong performance and investor confidence. While COVID vaccine sales significantly dropped, AstraZeneca maintained its 2023 forecast, with emerging markets and China showing substantial growth.

title: Ovid partners with Waksal startup to develop drugs for rare brain disorders
summary: Ovid Therapeutics is partnering with Graviton Bioscience, a startup founded by Sam Waksal, to develop drugs for rare brain disorders. The collaboration will focus on an experimental drug targeting the ROCK2 enzyme, with Ovid investing $10 million in Graviton. This partnership aims to leverage Ovid's neurology expertise and Graviton's ROCK2 knowledge to address conditions with limited treatment options.

title: Pfizer turns focus to new drugs as COVID vaccine revenue falls
summary: Pfizer is shifting its focus to new drug launches as revenue from its COVID-19 vaccine declines. The company reported first-quarter revenue that beat expectations despite a significant drop from the previous year due to plummeting vaccine sales, but COVID antiviral Paxlovid sales were unexpectedly high. Pfizer is anticipating key regulatory approvals for several new products, including an RSV vaccine and a multiple myeloma drug, which are crucial for achieving its projected non-COVID revenue growth.

title: A biopharma CEO opens up about executive salaries — and why he wants to change the status quo
summary: Dr. Richard Miller, CEO of Corvus Pharmaceuticals, has significantly reduced his salary in favor of stock options to align with shareholders and employees, advocating for a shift in biopharma executive compensation. This move, stemming from his belief in Corvus's science and products, challenges the industry's status quo of large salaries and bonuses, especially during a challenging biotech market. Miller hopes his actions inspire other leaders to prioritize scientific advancement and company performance over personal financial gain.

title: FDA Approves First ‘Fecal Transplant’ Pill to Prevent C. Diff Recurrence
summary: The FDA has approved Vowst, the first oral pill that mimics fecal transplants to prevent recurrent C. difficile infections. This new treatment, developed by Seres Therapeutics, is derived from screened donor feces and offers a more accessible alternative to traditional fecal microbiota transplants. Clinical trials showed that Vowst significantly reduced C. diff recurrence, providing an important advancement for patients suffering from this potentially life-threatening condition.

title: Focus: Novo Nordisk rivals see room to compete in $100 billion weight-loss drug market
summary: The demand for weight-loss drugs like Novo Nordisk's Wegovy is expected to create a market worth up to $100 billion, attracting numerous competitors including Pfizer and Amgen. Rivals are developing similar therapies, and an oral GLP-1 drug from Pfizer is anticipated to be a major product for the company. The market is primarily driven by the U.S. due to the large number of potential patients and higher drug pricing.

title: 10 Stocks for a Recession
summary: As recession fears persist in 2023, Morningstar identifies 10 undervalued, high-quality stocks in defensive sectors that are suitable for a diversified portfolio. These "recession-resistant" companies operate in healthcare, consumer defensive, and utilities, possess wide economic moats, and have low or medium uncertainty ratings. The article details each of the 10 recommended stocks, including GSK, Roche Holding, Imperial Brands, and Pfizer, with key Morningstar metrics.

title: Sinusitis Market to Register Stunning Growth, Estimates DelveInsight | Key Players in the Market - Optinose, GeneOne Life Science, Lyra, Sanofi, Regeneron, Genentech, AstraZeneca, Sanofi, Bayer, Pfizer
summary: The sinusitis market is projected for significant growth between 2023 and 2032, driven by new drug launches, increased healthcare spending, and improved diagnosis across the 7MM. Leading pharmaceutical companies are actively developing novel therapies, which are expected to advance the market. Despite a robust pipeline, challenges such as the lack of a gold standard for management and the availability of off-label treatments may impact growth.

title: Frank D’Amelio, CFO-in-Residence, on Setting Priorities in Challenging Times
summary: Frank D’Amelio, former CFO of Pfizer and now CFO-in-Residence for Deloitte, discusses key priorities for CFOs in a challenging economy. He emphasizes execution excellence, cash management, and capital allocation, citing Pfizer's successful $68 billion acquisition of Wyeth during the 2008-2009 recession. D'Amelio also shares insights on talent development, advocating for team members, and the evolving role of the CFO, highlighting the increasing importance of technology and strategic involvement.

title: A skin patch to treat peanut allergies? Study in toddlers shows promise
summary: An experimental skin patch called Viaskin shows promise in treating highly allergic toddlers to peanuts by training their bodies to tolerate small amounts. A study published in the New England Journal of Medicine indicated that two-thirds of toddlers using the patch daily for a year could safely ingest more peanuts, providing hope for a condition with limited treatment options, especially for young children. This patch offers an alternative to oral immunotherapies and aims to fill a significant unmet need in peanut allergy treatment.

title: B.C. court dismissed proposed class action against Zantac over increased cancer risk, GSK says
summary: A British Columbia court has dismissed a proposed class action lawsuit against the drug Zantac regarding increased cancer risk, as confirmed by GSK. The drug maker stated it welcomes the decision and will continue to vigorously defend against similar class actions filed in Ontario and Quebec, as well as individual actions in Canada. Zantac, originally marketed by a GSK forerunner and later sold to other companies, has been asserted by all four drug makers not to cause cancer, in line with scientific consensus.

title: Pfizer's India unit posts 3% rise in Q4 profit
summary: Pfizer Ltd, the Indian unit of Pfizer Inc, reported a 3.1% rise in its fourth-quarter profit, reaching 1.30 billion rupees, driven by lower raw material expenses. The company also declared a final dividend of 35 rupees per share and a special dividend of 5 rupees per share. This performance follows parent company Pfizer Inc's higher-than-expected first-quarter revenue and profit, and compares to rivals like Cipla Ltd and Novartis India Ltd which also reported increased profits.

title: IDEAYA Expands Clinical Trial Collaboration and Supply Agreements with Pfizer to Support Registrational Trial Evaluating Darovasertib and Crizotinib Combination in First-Line Metastatic Uveal Melanoma
summary: IDEAYA Biosciences announced an expansion of its clinical trial collaboration and supply agreements with Pfizer. This expanded partnership will support a planned Phase 2/3 registrational clinical trial evaluating the combination of darovasertib and crizotinib for first-line metastatic uveal melanoma (MUM). The trial aims for potential accelerated approval based on progression-free survival as a primary endpoint, building on promising Phase 2 clinical data.

title: FTC sues to block Amgen's $27.8 billion deal for Horizon Therapeutics
summary: The U.S. Federal Trade Commission (FTC) has filed a lawsuit to block Amgen's $27.8 billion acquisition of Horizon Therapeutics, citing concerns that Amgen might leverage its market position to unfairly favor Horizon's key drugs, Tepezza and Krystexxa. This rare move by the FTC to challenge a major pharmaceutical merger has led to a significant drop in Horizon's stock price and increased scrutiny on other pending biotech acquisitions. Amgen has expressed disappointment and plans to work with the court to complete the transaction, while analysts predict potential shifts in M&A strategies for drugmakers.

title: Pfizer Stock: Lackluster Valuation, Soft Growth Outlook (PFE)
summary: Pfizer has underperformed in the S&P 500 this year despite being a strong free-cash-flow generator. While it boasts a low earnings multiple and high dividend yield, its growth prospects are modest, leading to a fairly-valued assessment. The article highlights key price ranges to watch and suggests bearish sentiment based on current charts.

title: Teva puts rival to Prometheus, Pfizer drugs at center of turnaround plans
summary: Teva Pharmaceutical is centering its turnaround strategy on an experimental inflammatory disease drug, TEV-48574, which targets the protein TL1A. Despite missing its primary goal in an asthma trial, the company has initiated a Phase 2 trial for ulcerative colitis and Crohn’s disease, touting its "best-in-class" potency. However, Teva faces a significant lead from rival therapies from Pfizer and Prometheus Biosciences (acquired by Merck), with sales of TEV-48574 not expected until 2028.

title: US FDA panel backs Pfizer's maternal RSV vaccine for protecting infants
summary: A U.S. FDA advisory panel has endorsed Pfizer's experimental respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccine for maternal use, aiming to protect infants from the illness. The panel voted favorably on the vaccine's efficacy and safety for pregnant women, despite some concerns regarding a potential link to pre-term births. If approved, this vaccine could significantly impact infant health, adding to Pfizer's new medicine pipeline.

title: CureVac Announces Developments in Patent Litigation with Pfizer/BioNTech
summary: CureVac announced developments in its patent litigation with Pfizer/BioNTech, including the transfer of its U.S. litigation to the Eastern District of Virginia, which is expected to accelerate the timeline to a 2024 trial date. CureVac is filing a broadened counterclaim in the U.S., alleging infringement of nine patents relevant to mRNA vaccine design, formulation, and manufacturing by Comirnaty®. The company also highlighted a preliminary opinion from the German Federal Patent Court supporting the validity of one of its patents at issue.

title: AbbVie Adds Crohn’s Disease to Rinvoq’s Growing List of Indications
summary: AbbVie's drug Rinvoq (upadacitinib) has received FDA approval for treating moderate to severely active Crohn's disease, marking its seventh overall indication. This approval is significant as Rinvoq is the first oral drug for Crohn's disease and could help AbbVie offset declining sales of its blockbuster drug Humira due to increasing biosimilar competition. Clinical trials demonstrated Rinvoq's effectiveness in achieving endoscopic response and clinical remission in patients.

title: Pfizer’s RSV Vaccine for Pregnant Women Wins FDA Panel Support
summary: An FDA advisory committee has recommended Pfizer's RSV vaccine for use in pregnant women to protect newborns, making it the first such vaccine to gain panel support. While the vaccine was deemed effective, safety concerns were raised by some panelists regarding a higher rate of pre-term births, though Pfizer stated the difference was not statistically significant. This development marks a significant step in Pfizer's efforts to compete in the growing RSV vaccine market.

title: Novo Nordisk pauses ads for weight loss drug Wegovy as it struggles to meet demand
summary: Novo Nordisk is pausing advertising for its obesity drug Wegovy due to overwhelming demand that the company is struggling to meet. This decision includes stopping local television ads and postponing national campaigns, as well as adjusting promotional efforts to healthcare professionals. Wegovy, along with its sister drug Ozempic, has become highly popular for its effectiveness in weight loss.

title: May 22 Quick Takes: Ironwood building GI franchise via $1B VectivBio acquisition
summary: Ironwood Pharmaceuticals Inc. announced its acquisition of VectivBio Holding AG for $1 billion, integrating GLP2 analog apraglutide into its gastrointestinal portfolio. VectivBio, a 2019 spinout, had advanced apraglutide into Phase III testing for short bowel syndrome. Additionally, Krystal Biotech Inc. raised $160 million in a PIPE transaction following FDA approval of Vyjuvek for dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa, with a Q3 2023 launch anticipated.

title: FDA approves Krystal gene therapy for rare wound disorder
summary: The FDA has approved Krystal Biotech's gene therapy, Vyjuvek, for dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa, a rare genetic skin disease causing severe blistering. This marks the first topical gene therapy approval and is expected to be available in the third quarter with an estimated annual cost of $631,000 per patient. Vyjuvek delivers a functional gene to promote collagen production and wound healing, offering a new treatment option for a condition previously limited to pain and wound management.

title: Oculis announces positive top line results from Phase 3 trial of OCS-01 drops for diabetic macular edema
summary: Oculis announced positive top line results from Stage 1 of its Phase 3 DIAMOND trial for OCS-01 eye drops in diabetic macular edema (DME). The trial met its primary and secondary endpoints with statistical significance, showing strong visual gain and a decrease in retinal thickness. OCS-01, a topical formulation of dexamethasone, is positioned as a potential first-line treatment and complement to existing therapies due to its non-invasive nature.

title: Omada Health Launches GLP-1-Specific Program for Patients Battling Chronic Obesity
summary: Omada Health has introduced a specialized program for individuals using GLP-1 medications for weight management, recognizing the increasing demand and addressing concerns about long-term efficacy and cost. The program incorporates behavior and lifestyle changes alongside medication through specialized training for coaches, free educational resources, community support, and services to assist employers and PBMs with reimbursement policies. This initiative aims to align with FDA guidelines emphasizing GLP-1 use as an adjunct to diet and exercise to ensure sustained weight loss and avoid reliance solely on medication.

title: Sizing up VectivBio’s takeout premium among '23 M&A deals
summary: This article analyzes the premium paid for VectivBio in its acquisition by Ironwood, comparing it to other biopharma M&A deals valued over $1 billion in 2023. While VectivBio's deal premium appeared modest, a preceding stock run-up influenced the final percentage. The article notes that only the Pfizer acquisition of Seagen had a smaller premium, though it was a much larger deal, and also experienced a pre-acquisition share price increase.

title: Annexon claims a silver lining in failed eye drug study
summary: Annexon's experimental drug ANX007 for geographic atrophy failed its primary goal of slowing lesion growth in a Phase 2 study, unlike competitor drugs. However, the company is continuing development, citing a secondary analysis that suggests the drug may help preserve vision, a claim its CEO used to defend the results. Despite this, Annexon's shares fell significantly as analysts questioned the regulatory acceptance of vision preservation as a primary endpoint without lesion growth reduction.

title: Fast Five: Medtronic’s nearly $740M acquisition, Boston Scientific bows out of an acquisition
summary: This article covers key developments in the medical technology industry, including Medtronic's acquisition of EOFlow for $738 million and Boston Scientific's decision to withdraw from acquiring a majority stake in M.I. Tech. It also highlights HeartBeam's AI-related patent for a handheld vector ECG device and the FDA's approval of Zoll therapy for sleep apnea patients undergoing MRI scans. The Fast Five hosts discuss the implications of these strategic moves and technological advancements.

title: Pfizer, Moderna hit with new Alnylam patent lawsuits over COVID-19 vaccines
summary: Alnylam Pharmaceuticals has filed new lawsuits against Pfizer and Moderna, alleging their COVID-19 vaccines infringe on its patents for lipid nanoparticle (LNP) technology. This marks the third time Alnylam has sued the companies over their vaccine technology, seeking an unspecified share of royalties from their substantial vaccine sales. The lawsuits are part of a broader trend of patent disputes surrounding COVID-19 vaccines.

title: Big Pharma Companies Have Higher US FDA Approval Percentage Than Everybody Else
summary: The article states that large pharmaceutical companies have a higher percentage of drug approvals from the US FDA compared to other companies. It mentions authors and source information, indicating a publication from May 29, 2023. The content includes a list of related companies, predominantly pharmaceutical and biotech firms.

title: Pfizer's hemophilia therapy reduces bleeding in late-stage study
summary: Pfizer announced that its experimental hemophilia therapy, marstacimab, successfully met its main goal in a late-stage study, demonstrating superiority in reducing bleeding rates in hemophilia A and B patients. The therapy achieved a 92% reduction in bleeding compared to current standard of care treatments. Pfizer is also developing other hemophilia therapies and testing marstacimab in a broader patient population.

title: For the First Time Ever, Single-Stock ETFs Will Close Soon
summary: Seven single-stock ETFs, primarily offering leveraged or inverse exposure to individual stocks, are set to close in June, marking the first time such products will cease trading. Despite initial high expectations when they launched in July 2022, most single-stock ETFs have struggled, with minimal assets under management for those slated for closure. AXS will close five of its single-stock ETFs tied to companies like Nike, Pfizer, and PayPal, while GraniteShares is closing a Tesla-related fund, and AXS will also close two other leveraged/inverse ETFs targeting China internet and de-SPAC companies.

title: How Supreme Court's decision in Amgen v. Sanofi alters patent law
summary: The Supreme Court's decision in Amgen Inc. v. Sanofi has significantly altered patent law for the pharmaceutical industry, raising the bar for "enablement" in "genus" type patents. This ruling emphasizes the need for extensive detail to reproduce and use the entire class of items covered by a patent, creating uncertainty for drug developers as it applies a stricter standard than previously used by the Federal Circuit. Experts anticipate a period of adaptation and further legal clarity, similar to the impact of the Alice Corp. v. CLS Bank International decision on the software industry.

title: Seagen shareholders approve $43B acquisition by Pfizer
summary: Seagen shareholders have approved the proposed $43 billion acquisition by Pfizer. The companies anticipate closing the deal later in the current year or early next year, although they still face at least one remaining hurdle.

title: 2022’s Top Advertisers: P&G, Comcast Join Radio’s $200 Million Club.
summary: Procter & Gamble and Comcast Corp. both surpassed $200 million in radio ad spending in 2022, securing their positions as top advertisers. P&G increased its radio allocation by 48% and Comcast by 35%, while other significant spenders included Deutsche Telekom, the U.S. Government, Berkshire Hathaway, and Pfizer, with Pfizer showing the fastest growth among major advertisers. The article also highlights shifts in ad spending across different media, with AVOD and local radio seeing significant increases.

title: Pfizer says its experimental antibiotic combo can treat some superbug infections
summary: Pfizer announced that late-stage trials showed its experimental antibiotic combination, aztreonam-avibactam (ATM-AVI), was effective against deadly infections caused by drug-resistant bacteria, or superbugs. The trials demonstrated efficacy and good tolerability in treating complicated intra-abdominal infections and hospital-acquired pneumonia, showing higher cure rates compared to existing treatments. This development addresses the growing global concern of antibiotic resistance.

title: Why Shares of BioNTech Rose Friday
summary: BioNTech's stock rose on Friday after the company released positive trial data for its non-small cell lung cancer therapy candidate, BNT316/ONC-392. Despite a significant decline in revenue and EPS in the first quarter of 2023 due to falling sales of its COVID-19 vaccine, Comirnaty, the company plans to advance its cancer therapy to a phase 3 trial and possesses substantial cash reserves to fund its oncology pipeline. BioNTech aims to diversify its revenue streams beyond the COVID-19 vaccine market.

title: Erasca erases part of pipeline after revealing mixed hand of early-phase cancer data
summary: Erasca is reprioritizing its pipeline following underwhelming early-phase cancer data, leading to the discontinuation of several ERAS-007 applications and shelving a KRAS inhibitor. While some ERAS-007 trials in combination with other drugs disappointed, the company saw promising partial responses in metastatic BRAF V600E-mutated colorectal cancer patients. The biotech attributes some of these decisions to an increasingly competitive landscape.

title: Intellia Therapeutics Announces New Positive Clinical Data from Phase 1 Study of NTLA-2002, an Investigational In Vivo CRISPR Genome Editing Treatment for Hereditary Angioedema (HAE)
summary: Intellia Therapeutics announced positive new clinical data from its Phase 1 study of NTLA-2002, an investigational in vivo CRISPR genome editing treatment for Hereditary Angioedema (HAE). The data showed a 95% mean reduction in monthly HAE attack rates across all patients, with many remaining attack-free for extended periods. NTLA-2002 was well tolerated, reinforcing its potential as a functional cure and addressing the significant treatment burden associated with current HAE therapies.

title: Novartis to buy Seattle biotech firm Chinook Therapeutics in $3.2B deal
summary: Novartis announced its plan to acquire Seattle-based Chinook Therapeutics for $3.2 billion, with the deal potentially reaching $3.5 billion if regulatory milestones are met. Chinook, founded in 2019, specializes in therapies for chronic kidney disorders, including IgA Nephropathy, with lead experimental drugs atrasentan and zigakibart in advanced clinical trials. This acquisition highlights a continuing trend of major biotech deals in the Seattle region, following Pfizer's acquisition of Seagen and Sobi's deal to buy CTI BioPharma.

title: Spero Therapeutics Appoints Sath Shukla as CEO
summary: Spero Therapeutics announced the appointment of Satyavrat “Sath” Shukla as its new President, CEO, and a member of the Board of Directors, effective August 1, 2023. Shukla, currently the CFO and Treasurer, will succeed Ankit Mahadevia, M.D., who will become Chairman of the Board. This leadership transition aims to build upon Spero's foundation in anti-infectives and rare diseases, furthering the development of key drug candidates like tebipenem HBr and SPR720.

title: Bristol Myers sues US government over Medicare drug price negotiation plan
summary: Bristol Myers Squibb Co has sued the U.S. government over its Medicare drug price negotiation plan, arguing it violates the Fifth and First Amendments. This is the third lawsuit challenging the Inflation Reduction Act's provision, which the pharmaceutical industry claims will cut profits and hinder new drug development. Analysts expect Bristol Myers' blood thinner Eliquis to be among the first ten drugs chosen for price negotiation.

title: Bullish or Bearish? Vetting Animal Health Care Stocks
summary: The article discusses the resurgence of pet care stocks, particularly focusing on animal health care companies, driven by increased pet owner spending on health and wellness. It vets two specific companies, Zoetis, Inc. (NYSE: ZTS) and Elanco Animal Health, Inc. (NYSE: ELAN), examining their growth drivers, financial performance, and future prospects within the expanding U.S. pet care market. The piece highlights key developments like new drug approvals and financial guidance updates for both companies.

title: Eli Lilly's migraine drug fails to prove superiority to Pfizer's
summary: Eli Lilly announced that its migraine prevention drug, Emgality, did not demonstrate superiority over Pfizer's rival drug, Nurtec, in a recent post-approval study. The three-month study, involving 580 patients, was the first head-to-head comparison of the two drugs. Despite not proving superiority, Emgality still showed "clinically meaningful" efficacy and safety results.

title: Apogee Therapeutics Strengthens Team with Appointments of Industry Leaders to Board of Directors and Management
summary: Apogee Therapeutics announced the appointments of Jennifer Fox and William “BJ” Jones to its board of directors, with Ms. Fox also chairing the audit committee. The company also appointed Rebecca Dabora, Ph.D., as chief technology officer. These additions bring extensive experience in healthcare investment banking, commercial strategy, and chemistry, manufacturing, and controls (CMC) to support Apogee's advancement of biologics for atopic dermatitis and COPD.

title: Lilly's phase 2 results published in the New England Journal of Medicine show orforglipron, a once-daily oral nonpeptide GLP-1 receptor agonist, achieved up to 14.7% mean weight reduction at 36 weeks in adults with obesity or overweight
summary: Eli Lilly and Company announced positive Phase 2 results for orforglipron, a once-daily oral nonpeptide GLP-1 receptor agonist, demonstrating significant weight reduction and improved A1C levels. Published in the New England Journal of Medicine, the study showed up to 14.7% mean weight reduction at 36 weeks in adults with obesity or overweight, and in The Lancet, up to 2.1% reduction in A1C for adults with type 2 diabetes. These findings support the progression of orforglipron into Phase 3 clinical programs for chronic weight management and type 2 diabetes.

title: RNA Based Therapeutic Market Trend 2023: Anticipated Growth to Reach $25.12 Billion by 2030 | 17.6%
summary: The RNA-based therapeutic market is projected to reach $25.12 billion by 2030, growing at a CAGR of 17.6% from its 2021 valuation of $4.93 billion. This growth is driven by increasing R&D investments, technological advancements like mRNA and RNAi therapeutics, and the rising demand for targeted and personalized medicine. Key players like Moderna, BioNTech, and Alnylam Pharmaceuticals are actively involved, with North America leading the market and Asia-Pacific showing the fastest growth.

title: ACTIVELY INVESTING IN GLOBAL HEALTH: Real-world approaches to healthcare make a difference
summary: The article highlights the partnership between Pfizer, The Pfizer Foundation, and World Vision to combat communicable and infectious diseases, which are leading causes of child mortality, particularly in marginalized communities. Their collaboration focuses on strengthening healthcare systems and implementing community-based programs. An example is the Expanding Access to Immunization and Treatment program in Uganda, which has screened over 129,000 children and trained over 1,000 community health workers, aiming to reduce child mortality.

title: FDA approves somatrogon-ghla to treat pediatric growth hormone deficiency
summary: The FDA has approved somatrogon-ghla (NGENLA; Pfizer Inc and OPKO Health Inc) for children aged 3 and older with growth failure due to insufficient growth hormone secretion. This new once-weekly injection aims to reduce the burden of daily treatments and improve adherence for pediatric patients with growth hormone deficiency (GHD). The approval is based on phase 3 study data showing its non-inferiority to somatropin in annual height velocity at 12 months.

title: Pfizer (PFE) and OPKO (OPK) Announce FDA Approval of NGENLA
summary: Pfizer and OPKO Health have announced that the U.S. FDA has approved NGENLA (somatrogon-ghla), a once-weekly human growth hormone analog, for pediatric patients three years and older with growth failure due to inadequate secretion of endogenous growth hormone. This approval is based on a Phase 3 study showing non-inferiority to daily somatropin, offering a potentially less burdensome treatment option. NGENLA is expected to be available in the U.S. in August 2023 and is already approved in over 40 other markets.

title: FDA Approves Pfizer, OPKO’s Once Weekly Ngenla for Human Growth Deficiency in Pediatric Patients
summary: The FDA has approved somatrogon-ghla (Ngenla) from Pfizer and OPKO Health for pediatric patients aged 3 and older with growth failure due to inadequate growth hormone secretion. This once-weekly subcutaneous injection offers a significant reduction in treatment burden compared to daily injections. Clinical trials demonstrated its non-inferiority to daily somatropin and a comparable safety profile, with potential availability in the US market by August 2023.

title: FDA approval of BioMarin’s Roctavian to test gene therapy pricing model
summary: The FDA has approved BioMarin's Roctavian for severe hemophilia A, marking an important gene therapy milestone for 2023. The launch of Roctavian, priced at $2.9 million, will be a crucial test for the marketability and pricing models of gene therapies, especially considering its outcomes-based warranty. This warranty promises up to 100% reimbursement if the patient does not respond to the treatment.

title: FDA rejects Alvotech’s Humira biosimilar for the third time
summary: The FDA has rejected Alvotech's Humira biosimilar, AVT02, for the third time due to deficiencies at a manufacturing facility in Reykjavik, Iceland. This rejection further delays the drug's US launch, despite its prior approval in Australia, Canada, and the EU. Alvotech plans to resubmit the biologics license application (BLA) with additional data for interchangeability designation and is exploring capital raising options.

title: FDA Approves BioMarin’s Hemophilia A Gene Therapy Roctavian
summary: The FDA has approved BioMarin’s valoctocogene roxaparvovec (Roctavian) for adults with severe hemophilia A, making it the first gene therapy for this condition in the US. The approval was based on positive data from the phase 3 GENEr8-1 clinical trial, showing significant reductions in annualized bleeding rates and FVIII utilization. BioMarin plans to price the one-time treatment at $2.9 million and offer an outcomes-based warranty.

title: New Humira rivals likely to hit US market with small discounts in July
summary: Multiple biosimilar versions of AbbVie's top-selling drug Humira are expected to launch in the U.S. in July, adding to the competition started by Amgen in January. Despite increased generic competition, industry experts anticipate only small price discounts for these new versions due to pharmacy benefit managers' negotiation strategies. This pricing dynamic means that while health plans might secure some savings, patients paying co-insurance based on list prices may not see significant relief.

title: Samsung Bioepis, Celltrion Healthcare launch Humira biosimilar in US
summary: Samsung Bioepis and Celltrion Healthcare have launched their respective Humira biosimilars, Hadlima and Yuflyma, in the U.S. market. Hadlima offers an 85% discount compared to Humira's list price and includes patient support programs, while Yuflyma provides a 5% discount, with actual selling prices variable due to rebates. The article highlights the significant role of Pharmacy Benefit Managers (PBMs) in drug formulary inclusion and pricing in the U.S. market.

title: First Trust Exchange-Traded Fund III - First Trust Morningstar Dividend Leaders Index Fund (FDL) News, Articles, Events & Latest Updates
summary: This article provides recent news and updates for the First Trust Morningstar Dividend Leaders Index Fund (FDL). It highlights several financial articles discussing FDL and other dividend ETFs outperforming the S&P 500, offering current income, and gaining investor interest amid market volatility and sector rotations. The feed includes news from Zacks and Stocktwits discussing various dividend-focused investment strategies and company-specific financial reports impacting dividend stocks.

title: Settlement checks in the mail from Roundup, EpiPen, Zoom, others
summary: Readers of Top Class Actions are reporting the receipt of settlement checks from seven different class action lawsuits. These settlements address various claims including false advertising for Roundup, spam calls from Bath Saver, privacy issues related to Yahoo data breaches, antitrust violations by EpiPen manufacturers, price-fixing for lithium-ion batteries, Apple iCloud storing data on third-party servers, and security failures by Zoom that led to "Zoom bombing." Claimants are receiving payments ranging from small amounts to several thousands of dollars depending on the settlement terms and individual claims.

title: The Commercial Market for Legal Psychedelics: Spravato
summary: This article examines the commercial market for legal psychedelics, focusing on Spravato (esketamine), the first FDA-approved psychedelic. It highlights Spravato's impressive sales growth, showing the potential for psychedelics in mainstream pharma. The piece also discusses the future outlook for upcoming psychedelic drugs like those from MAPS and Compass Pathways.

title: Pfizer backs CRISPR biotech Caribou in latest cell therapy investment
